1.116.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
vasiṣṭhavaṃśajānviprānnibodha gadato mama ..
ekārṣeyaśca pravaro vasiṣṭhānāṃ prakīrtitāḥ .. 1 ..
1.116.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
वसिष्ठवंशजान्विप्रान्निबोध गदतो मम ॥
एकार्षेयश्च प्रवरो वसिष्ठानां प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 1 ॥
1.116.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Learn from me as I declare the brahmins born of Vasiṣṭha's lineage.
The pravara of the Vasiṣṭhas is proclaimed as consisting of one sage.

1.116.s:
vasiṣṭha eva vāsiṣṭhā avivāhyā vasiṣṭhajaiḥ ..
vyāghrapādā aupagavāḥ vaiklavā śādvalāyanāḥ .. 2 ..
1.116.d:
वसिष्ठ एव वासिष्ठा अविवाह्या वसिष्ठजैः ॥
व्याघ्रपादा औपगवाः वैक्लवा शाद्वलायनाः ॥ 2 ॥
1.116.m:
Vasiṣṭha alone is [the pravara] of the Vāsiṣṭhas; they cannot be married into by those born of Vasiṣṭha:
the Vyāghrapādas, Aupagavas, Vaiklavas, Śādvalāyanas,

1.116.s:
kāpiṣṭhalā kṣaiṭalomā āśvalāḥ sarvaṭākarāḥ ..
gopāyanā bodhayaśca dvākalpā apavāhyakṛt .. 3 ..
1.116.d:
कापिष्ठला क्षैटलोमा आश्वलाः सर्वटाकराः ॥
गोपायना बोधयश्च द्वाकल्पा अपवाह्यकृत् ॥ 3 ॥
1.116.m:
Kāpiṣṭhalas, Kṣaiṭalomas, Āśvalas, Sarvaṭākaras,
Gopāyanas, Bodhas, Dvākalpas, Apavāhyakṛt,

1.116.s:
bāliśeyā pāliśiṣyāstathomāṅkuravaśca ye ..
āyasthūṇāḥ śītavṛkṣāstathā brahmapurohitāḥ .. 4 ..
1.116.d:
बालिशेया पालिशिष्यास्तथोमाङ्कुरवश्च ये ॥
आयस्थूणाः शीतवृक्षास्तथा ब्रह्मपुरोहिताः ॥ 4 ॥
1.116.m:
Bāliśeyas, Pāliśiṣyas, and those who are Omāṅkuras,
Āyasthūṇas, Śītavṛkṣas, and the Brahmapurohitas,

1.116.s:
lomātyāḥ svastikarāḥ māṇḍalirgautalistathā ..
vāhnehaṇḍiśca sumanā śvapādirviddhireva ca .. .. 5 ..
1.116.d:
लोमात्याः स्वस्तिकराः माण्डलिर्गौतलिस्तथा ॥
वाह्नेहण्डिश्च सुमना श्वपादिर्विद्धिरेव च ॥ ॥ 5 ॥
1.116.m:
Lomātyas, Svastikaras, Māṇḍali, Gautali,
Vāhnehaṇḍi, Sumanas, Śvapādi, and Viddhi,

1.116.s:
śaulirlolirbrahmabalo vailiśravasa eva ca ..
mauṇḍavo yājñavalkyaśca ekārṣeyāstathā nṛpa .. 6 ..
1.116.d:
शौलिर्लोलिर्ब्रह्मबलो वैलिश्रवस एव च ॥
मौण्डवो याज्ञवल्क्यश्च एकार्षेयास्तथा नृप ॥ 6 ॥
1.116.m:
Śauli, Loli, Brahmabala, and Vailiśravasa,
Mauṇḍava, and Yājñavalkya—these have a pravara of one sage, O king.

1.116.s:
vasiṣṭha eṣāṃ pravara avaivāhyāḥ parasparam..
śailālayo mahākarṇo kauravyaḥ kraivaṇistathā ..7..
1.116.d:
वसिष्ठ एषां प्रवर अवैवाह्याः परस्परम्॥
शैलालयो महाकर्णो कौरव्यः क्रैवणिस्तथा ॥7॥
1.116.m:
Vasiṣṭha is their pravara; they cannot intermarry with one another.
Śailālaya, Mahākarṇa, Kauravya, and Kraivaṇi,

1.116.s:
kapiñjalo bālaśikhirbhāgavittāyanāśca ye ..
kaurāyaṇā lākahayā kaulakṛdbhāgurāyaṇāḥ .. 8 ..
1.116.d:
कपिञ्जलो बालशिखिर्भागवित्तायनाश्च ये ॥
कौरायणा लाकहया कौलकृद्भागुरायणाः ॥ 8 ॥
1.116.m:
Kapiñjala, Bālaśikhin, and those who are Bhāgavittāyanas,
Kaurāyaṇas, Lākahayas, the Kaulakṛt Bhāgurāyaṇas,

1.116.s:
śākahavyāḥ kaśāpeyā atho ulvapayāśca ye ..
sāṅkhyāyanā anaḍuhā atho māṣaśirādhayaḥ .. 9 ..
1.116.d:
शाकहव्याः कशापेया अथो उल्वपयाश्च ये ॥
साङ्ख्यायना अनडुहा अथो माषशिराधयः ॥ 9 ॥
1.116.m:
Śākahavyas, Kaśāpeyas, and further, those who are Ulvapayas,
Sāṅkhyāyanas, Anaḍuhas, and further, Māṣaśirādhis,

1.116.s:
dāmakāyanā vāhayavo vākyayogorathastathā ..
ābāyanāśca ṛṣayo ye ca kroḍādanāyavāḥ .. 1.116.10 ..
1.116.d:
दामकायना वाहयवो वाक्ययोगोरथस्तथा ॥
आबायनाश्च ऋषयो ये च क्रोडादनायवाः ॥ 1.116.10 ॥
1.116.m:
Dāmakāyanas, Vāhayus, Vākyayoga, Uratha,
and the sage Ābāyanas, and those who are Kroḍādanāyavas,

1.116.s:
pralambāyanāśca ṛṣaya aupamanyava eva ca ..
sāṅkhyāyanāśca ṛṣayastathā ye ca daśerakāḥ .... 11 ..
1.116.d:
प्रलम्बायनाश्च ऋषय औपमन्यव एव च ॥
साङ्ख्यायनाश्च ऋषयस्तथा ये च दशेरकाः ॥॥ 11 ॥
1.116.m:
and the sage Pralambāyanas, and Aupamanyava,
and the sage Sāṅkhyāyanas, and also those who are Daśerakas,

1.116.s:
pādakāyana audgrāhā ṛṣayaścaiva lekhayaḥ ..
māleyā brahmavalayaḥ pūrṇāgāṃristathaiva ca .. 12 ..
1.116.d:
पादकायन औद्ग्राहा ऋषयश्चैव लेखयः ॥
मालेया ब्रह्मवलयः पूर्णागांरिस्तथैव च ॥ 12 ॥
1.116.m:
Pādakāyana, Audgrāhas, and the sage Lekhas,
Māleyas, Brahmavalis, and likewise Pūrṇāgāṃri—

1.116.s:
tryārṣeyo'pi mataścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarastathā..
bhago vasurvasiṣṭhaśca indraḥ sammatireva ca .. 13 ..
1.116.d:
त्र्यार्षेयोऽपि मतश्चैषां सर्वेषां प्रवरस्तथा॥
भगो वसुर्वसिष्ठश्च इन्द्रः सम्मतिरेव च ॥ 13 ॥
1.116.m:
the pravara of all of these is likewise held to consist of three sages:
Bhaga, Vasu, Vasiṣṭha, Indra, and Sammati.

1.116.s:
parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
aupasvasthāḥ svasthalayo vālo hālo hayāśca ye .. .. 14 ..
1.116.d:
परस्परमवैवाह्या ऋषयः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
औपस्वस्थाः स्वस्थलयो वालो हालो हयाश्च ये ॥ ॥ 14 ॥
1.116.m:
These sages are proclaimed as unable to intermarry with one another.
The Aupasvasthas, Svasthalayas, Vāla, Hāla, and the Hayas,

1.116.s:
madhyandinā akṣatayaḥ paippalā devicaṅkapī ..
traiśṛṅgā vanagā ālavāḥ kuṇḍināśca narottama .. 19 ..
1.116.d:
मध्यन्दिना अक्षतयः पैप्पला देविचङ्कपी ॥
त्रैशृङ्गा वनगा आलवाः कुण्डिनाश्च नरोत्तम ॥ 19 ॥
1.116.m:
Madhyandinas, Akṣatas, Paippalas, Devicaṅkapī,
Traiśṛṅgas, Vanagas, Ālavas, and the Kuṇḍinas, O best of men—

1.116.s:
tryārṣeyo'pi mataścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravaraḥ śubhaḥ ..
vasiṣṭhamitrāvaruṇau kuṇḍinaśca mahātapāḥ .. 16 ..
1.116.d:
त्र्यार्षेयोऽपि मतश्चैषां सर्वेषां प्रवरः शुभः ॥
वसिष्ठमित्रावरुणौ कुण्डिनश्च महातपाः ॥ 16 ॥
1.116.m:
the auspicious pravara of all of these is held to consist of three sages:
Vasiṣṭha, Mitrāvaruṇa, and Kuṇḍina of great ascetic heat.

1.116.s:
parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
jātūkarṇā yavaścaiva pādapāśca tathaiva ca .. 17 ..
1.116.d:
परस्परमवैवाह्या ऋषयः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
जातूकर्णा यवश्चैव पादपाश्च तथैव च ॥ 17 ॥
1.116.m:
These sages are proclaimed as unable to intermarry with one another.
The Jātūkarṇas, Yavas, and likewise the Pādapas—

1.116.s:
tryārṣeyo'pi mataścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarastathā ..
jātūkarṇo vasiṣṭhaśca tathaivāntyaśca pārthiva ..
parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 18 ..
1.116.d:
त्र्यार्षेयोऽपि मतश्चैषां सर्वेषां प्रवरस्तथा ॥
जातूकर्णो वसिष्ठश्च तथैवान्त्यश्च पार्थिव ॥
परस्परमवैवाह्या ऋषयः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 18 ॥
1.116.m:
the pravara of all of these is likewise held to consist of three sages:
Jātūkarṇa, Vasiṣṭha, and likewise the last, O ruler of the earth.
These sages are proclaimed as unable to intermarry with one another.

1.116.s:
vasiṣṭhavaṃśe'bhihitā mayaite ṛṣiprabarhā nṛpa gotrakārāḥ ..
yeṣāntu nāmnāṃ parikīrtanena pāpaṃ samagraṃ puruṣo jahāti ..19 ..
1.116.d:
वसिष्ठवंशेऽभिहिता मयैते ऋषिप्रबर्हा नृप गोत्रकाराः ॥
येषान्तु नाम्नां परिकीर्तनेन पापं समग्रं पुरुषो जहाति ॥19 ॥
1.116.m:
These eminent sages, founders of gotras in the lineage of Vasiṣṭha, have been declared by me, O king,
by the recitation of whose names a man casts off all evil.

1.117.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
vasiṣṭhastu mahātejā nimeḥ pūrvapurohitaḥ .. 1 ..
1.117.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
वसिष्ठस्तु महातेजा निमेः पूर्वपुरोहितः ॥ 1 ॥
1.117.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Vasiṣṭha of great splendour was formerly the family priest of Nimi.

1.117.s:
babhūva pārthivaśreṣṭha yajñaistasya samantataḥ ..
śāntātmā pārthivaśreṣṭha viśaśrāma tadā purā .. 2 ..
1.117.d:
बभूव पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ यज्ञैस्तस्य समन्ततः ॥
शान्तात्मा पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ विशश्राम तदा पुरा ॥ 2 ॥
1.117.m:
[After] he had been, O best of kings, [busy] with his sacrifices everywhere,
his mind at peace, O best of kings, he then rested in former times.

1.117.s:
taṃ gatvā pārthivaśreṣṭho nimirvacanamabravīt ..
bhagavanyaṣṭumicchāmi tanmā yājaya mā ciram .. 3 ..
1.117.d:
तं गत्वा पार्थिवश्रेष्ठो निमिर्वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
भगवन्यष्टुमिच्छामि तन्मा याजय मा चिरम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.117.m:
Having approached him, Nimi, the best of kings, spoke [these] words:
'Lord, I desire to sacrifice; therefore, officiate for me without delay.'

1.117.s:
tamuvāca mahātejā vaśiṣṭhaḥ pārthivottamam ..
kañcitkālaṃ pratīkṣasva tava yajñaiḥ samantataiḥ .. 4 ..
1.117.d:
तमुवाच महातेजा वशिष्ठः पार्थिवोत्तमम् ॥
कञ्चित्कालं प्रतीक्षस्व तव यज्ञैः समन्ततैः ॥ 4 ॥
1.117.m:
Vasiṣṭha of great splendour spoke to that best of kings:
'Wait for some time; through your sacrifices all around,

1.117.s:
bhṛśaṃ śrānto'smi viśramya yājayiṣyāmi te nṛpa ..
evamuktaḥ pratyuvāca vasiṣṭhaṃ nṛpasattamaḥ ..5..
1.117.d:
भृशं श्रान्तोऽस्मि विश्रम्य याजयिष्यामि ते नृप ॥
एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच वसिष्ठं नृपसत्तमः ॥5॥
1.117.m:
I am utterly exhausted. Having rested, I will officiate for you, O king.'
Having been spoken to thus, that best of kings replied to Vasiṣṭha:

1.117.s:
pāralaukikakāryeṣu kaḥ pratīkṣitumutsahe ..
na yasya sauhṛdaṃ brahmankṛtāntena balīyasā .. 6 ..
1.117.d:
पारलौकिककार्येषु कः प्रतीक्षितुमुत्सहे ॥
न यस्य सौहृदं ब्रह्मन्कृतान्तेन बलीयसा ॥ 6 ॥
1.117.m:
'In matters concerning the next world, who can dare to wait,
when no one has friendship, O brahmin, with the all-powerful Ender?

1.117.s:
dharmakārye tvarā kāryā calaṃ yasmāddhi jīvitama ..
dharmamārgarato janturmṛto'pi sukhamaśnute .. 7 ..
1.117.d:
धर्मकार्ये त्वरा कार्या चलं यस्माद्धि जीवितम ॥
धर्ममार्गरतो जन्तुर्मृतोऽपि सुखमश्नुते ॥ 7 ॥
1.117.m:
Haste should be made in deeds of dharma, for life is indeed fleeting.
A creature devoted to the path of dharma enjoys happiness even when dead.

1.117.s:
śvaḥkāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhne cāparāhṇikam ..
na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ vāsya na vā kṛtam .. 8 ..
1.117.d:
श्वःकार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्ने चापराह्णिकम् ॥
न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतं वास्य न वा कृतम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.117.m:
Tomorrow's work one should do today, and afternoon's in the forenoon;
for Death does not wait [to see] whether one's work is done or not done.

1.117.s:
kṣetrāpatyagṛhāsaktamanyatra gatamānasam ..
vṛkīvoraṇamāsādya mṛtyurādāya gacchati .. 9 ..
1.117.d:
क्षेत्रापत्यगृहासक्तमन्यत्र गतमानसम् ॥
वृकीवोरणमासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति ॥ 9 ॥
1.117.m:
Attached to fields, offspring, and home, with his mind fixed elsewhere,
Death seizes him and departs, as a she-wolf [carries off] a sheep she has caught.

1.117.s:
na kālasya priyaḥ kaściddveṣyo vāsya na vidyate ..
āyuṣye karmaṇi kṣīṇe prasahya harate janam .. 1.117.10 ..
1.117.d:
न कालस्य प्रियः कश्चिद्द्वेष्यो वास्य न विद्यते ॥
आयुष्ये कर्मणि क्षीणे प्रसह्य हरते जनम् ॥ 1.117.10 ॥
1.117.m:
Time has no one dear, nor is anyone hateful to it;
when the lifespan and karma are exhausted, it violently carries off a person.

1.117.s:
prāṇo vāyuścalatvañca vāyorviditameva ca ..
yatra yajjīvyate brahmankṣaṇamātraṃ tadadbhutam .. 11 ..
1.117.d:
प्राणो वायुश्चलत्वञ्च वायोर्विदितमेव च ॥
यत्र यज्जीव्यते ब्रह्मन्क्षणमात्रं तदद्भुतम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.117.m:
Breath is wind, and the nature of wind is known to be flickering;
that one lives at all for just a moment, O brahmin, is a wonder.

1.117.s:
so'haṃ sambhṛtasaṃbhāge bhavanmūlamupāgataḥ ..
na cedyājayase mahyaṃ yāsyāmyanyaṃ tu yājakam .. 12 ..
1.117.d:
सोऽहं सम्भृतसंभागे भवन्मूलमुपागतः ॥
न चेद्याजयसे मह्यं यास्याम्यन्यं तु याजकम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.117.m:
So having gathered the provisions, I have approached your presence;
if you will not officiate for me, I shall go to another officiating priest.'

1.117.s:
evamuktastadā tena niminā brāhmaṇottamaḥ ..
śaśāpa taṃ nimiṃ krodhādvidehastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi ..13..
1.117.d:
एवमुक्तस्तदा तेन निमिना ब्राह्मणोत्तमः ॥
शशाप तं निमिं क्रोधाद्विदेहस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥13॥
1.117.m:
Having been spoken to thus by that Nimi, the best of brahmins
in anger cursed that Nimi: 'You shall become bodiless!

1.117.s:
śrāntaṃ māṃ tvaṃ samutsṛjya yasmādanyaṃ dvijottamam ..
dharmajñaḥ sannarendrādya yājakaṃ kartumarhasi ..14..
1.117.d:
श्रान्तं मां त्वं समुत्सृज्य यस्मादन्यं द्विजोत्तमम् ॥
धर्मज्ञः सन्नरेन्द्राद्य याजकं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥14॥
1.117.m:
Since you, forsaking me who am exhausted, dare to make another best of twice-born
your officiating priest today, O king, while knowing dharma?'

1.117.s:
nimistaṃ pratyuvācātha dharmakāryaratasya me ..
vighnaṃ karoṣi nānyena yājanaṃ ca tathecchasi .. 15 ..
1.117.d:
निमिस्तं प्रत्युवाचाथ धर्मकार्यरतस्य मे ॥
विघ्नं करोषि नान्येन याजनं च तथेच्छसि ॥ 15 ॥
1.117.m:
Nimi then replied to him: 'You cause an obstacle to me
who am devoted to deeds of dharma, and you do not wish [my] sacrifice by another.

1.117.s:
śāpaṃ dadāmi tasmāttvaṃ videho'dya bhaviṣyasi ..
evamukte tu tau jātau videhau dvijapārthivau .. 16 ..
1.117.d:
शापं ददामि तस्मात्त्वं विदेहोऽद्य भविष्यसि ॥
एवमुक्ते तु तौ जातौ विदेहौ द्विजपार्थिवौ ॥ 16 ॥
1.117.m:
"Therefore I pronounce a curse: today you shall become bodiless."
When this was said, the twice-born and the king both became bodiless.

1.117.s:
dehahīnau tayorjīvau brahmāṇamupajagmatuḥ ..
āgatau tau samīpe'tha brahmā vacanamabravīt ..17..
1.117.d:
देहहीनौ तयोर्जीवौ ब्रह्माणमुपजग्मतुः ॥
आगतौ तौ समीपेऽथ ब्रह्मा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥17॥
1.117.m:
Deprived of bodies, their two life-souls approached Brahmā.
When they had arrived near him, Brahmā spoke these words:

1.117.s:
adyaprabhṛti te sthānaṃ nime jīvaṃ dadāmyaham ..
netrapakṣmasu sarveṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 18 ..
1.117.d:
अद्यप्रभृति ते स्थानं निमे जीवं ददाम्यहम् ॥
नेत्रपक्ष्मसु सर्वेषां मनुष्याणां भविष्यसि ॥ 18 ॥
1.117.m:
"From this day forth, Nimi, I assign a place to your life-soul:
you shall dwell in the eyelashes of all human beings.

1.117.s:
tvatsambandhāttathā teṣāṃ nimeṣaḥ sambhaviṣyati ..
cālayiṣyanti tu yadā netrapakṣmāṇi mānavāḥ .. 19 ..
1.117.d:
त्वत्सम्बन्धात्तथा तेषां निमेषः सम्भविष्यति ॥
चालयिष्यन्ति तु यदा नेत्रपक्ष्माणि मानवाः ॥ 19 ॥
1.117.m:
And through your connection with them, their blinking shall take place,
whenever human beings move their eyelashes."

1.117.s:
evamukte manuṣyāṇāṃ netrapakṣmasu sarvaśaḥ ..
jagāma nimijīvaṃ tu varadānātsvayambhuvaḥ .. 1.117.20 ..
1.117.d:
एवमुक्ते मनुष्याणां नेत्रपक्ष्मसु सर्वशः ॥
जगाम निमिजीवं तु वरदानात्स्वयम्भुवः ॥ 1.117.20 ॥
1.117.m:
When this was said, through the boon granted by the Self-born,
the life-soul of Nimi entered everywhere into the eyelashes of human beings.

1.117.s:
vaśiṣṭhajīvaṃ bhagavānbrahmā vacanamabravīt ..
mitrāvaruṇayoḥ putro vaśiṣṭha tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 21 ..
1.117.d:
वशिष्ठजीवं भगवान्ब्रह्मा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
मित्रावरुणयोः पुत्रो वशिष्ठ त्वं भविष्यसि ॥ 21 ॥
1.117.m:
Lord Brahmā then addressed these words to the life-soul of Vasiṣṭha:
"Vasiṣṭha, you shall become the son of Mitra and Varuṇa.

1.117.s:
vaśiṣṭha iti te nāma tatrāpi ca bhaviṣyati ..
janmadvayamatītaṃ ca tatrāpi tvaṃ smariṣyasi .. 22 ..
1.117.d:
वशिष्ठ इति ते नाम तत्रापि च भविष्यति ॥
जन्मद्वयमतीतं च तत्रापि त्वं स्मरिष्यसि ॥ 22 ॥
1.117.m:
There too your name shall be Vasiṣṭha,
and there too you shall remember your two past births."

1.117.s:
etasminneva kāle tu mitraśca varuṇastathā ..
badaryāśramamāsādya tapastepaturavyayam .. 23 ..
1.117.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मित्रश्च वरुणस्तथा ॥
बदर्याश्रममासाद्य तपस्तेपतुरव्ययम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.117.m:
At that very time, Mitra and Varuṇa
reached the hermitage of Badarī and performed imperishable ascetic penance.

1.117.s:
tapasyatostayorevaṃ kadācinmādhave ṛtau ..
puṣpitadrumasaṃchinne śubhe dakṣiṇamārute .. 24 ..
1.117.d:
तपस्यतोस्तयोरेवं कदाचिन्माधवे ऋतौ ॥
पुष्पितद्रुमसंछिन्ने शुभे दक्षिणमारुते ॥ 24 ॥
1.117.m:
As the two were thus engaged in ascetic penance, once in the spring season,
when the flowering trees were stirred by an auspicious southern wind,

1.117.s:
urvaśyatha varārohā kurvatī kusumoccayam ..
sasūkṣmaraktavasanā tayordṛṣṭipathaṃ gatā .. 25 ..
1.117.d:
उर्वश्यथ वरारोहा कुर्वती कुसुमोच्चयम् ॥
ससूक्ष्मरक्तवसना तयोर्दृष्टिपथं गता ॥ 25 ॥
1.117.m:
Urvaśī, a woman of lovely hips, gathering blossoms,
clad in a fine red garment, came into their field of vision.

1.117.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sumukhīṃ subhrūṃ nīlanīrajalocanām ..
ubhau cukṣubhaturvīryāttadrūpaparimohitau .. 25 ..
1.117.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा सुमुखीं सुभ्रूं नीलनीरजलोचनाम् ॥
उभौ चुक्षुभतुर्वीर्यात्तद्रूपपरिमोहितौ ॥ 25 ॥
1.117.m:
Beholding her with lovely face, charming brows, and eyes like blue lotuses,
both were agitated with passion, enchanted by her beauty.

1.117.s:
skannaṃ retastayordṛṣṭvā śāpabhītā varāpsarāḥ ..
cakāra kalaśe subhrūstoyapūrṇe manorame .. 27 ..
1.117.d:
स्कन्नं रेतस्तयोर्दृष्ट्वा शापभीता वराप्सराः ॥
चकार कलशे सुभ्रूस्तोयपूर्णे मनोरमे ॥ 27 ॥
1.117.m:
Seeing their spilled semen, the excellent apsaras, fearful of a curse,
the fair-browed maiden placed it into a delightful jar filled with water.

1.117.s:
tasmādṛṣivarau jātau tejasāpratimo bhuvi ..
vaśiṣṭhaścāpyagastyaśca mitrāvaruṇayoḥ sutau .. 28 ..
1.117.d:
तस्मादृषिवरौ जातौ तेजसाप्रतिमो भुवि ॥
वशिष्ठश्चाप्यगस्त्यश्च मित्रावरुणयोः सुतौ ॥ 28 ॥
1.117.m:
From it were born two eminent sages, matchless in splendor on earth,
Vasiṣṭha and Agastya, the two sons of Mitra and Varuṇa.

1.117.s:
vaśiṣṭhastūpayemetha bhaginīṃ nāradasya tu ..
arundhatīṃ varārohāṃ tasyāṃ śaktimajījanat .. 29 ..
1.117.d:
वशिष्ठस्तूपयेमेथ भगिनीं नारदस्य तु ॥
अरुन्धतीं वरारोहां तस्यां शक्तिमजीजनत् ॥ 29 ॥
1.117.m:
Then Vasiṣṭha married the sister of Nārada,
the shapely Arundhatī, and begot Śakti upon her.

1.117.s:
śakteḥ parāśaraḥ putrastasya vaṃśaṃ nibodha me ..
yasya dvaipāyanaḥ putraḥ svayaṃ viṣṇurajāyata .. 1.117.30 ..
1.117.d:
शक्तेः पराशरः पुत्रस्तस्य वंशं निबोध मे ॥
यस्य द्वैपायनः पुत्रः स्वयं विष्णुरजायत ॥ 1.117.30 ॥
1.117.m:
Śakti's son was Parāśara; hear from me his lineage,
whose son was Dvaipāyana, Viṣṇu himself born [as a human],

1.117.s:
prakāśo janito yena loke bhāratacandramāḥ ..
parāśarasya tasya tvaṃ śṛṇu vaṃśamanuttamam .. 31 ..
1.117.d:
प्रकाशो जनितो येन लोके भारतचन्द्रमाः ॥
पराशरस्य तस्य त्वं शृणु वंशमनुत्तमम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.117.m:
by whom light was brought forth in the world as the moon of the Mahābhārata.
Hear from me that incomparable lineage of Parāśara.

1.117.s:
kārdramayo vāhayāno jaimayo maimatāyanaḥ ..
gopāliḥ pañcamaścaiṣāṃ jñeyā kṛṣṇaparāśarāḥ .. 32 ..
1.117.d:
कार्द्रमयो वाहयानो जैमयो मैमतायनः ॥
गोपालिः पञ्चमश्चैषां ज्ञेया कृष्णपराशराः ॥ 32 ॥
1.117.m:
Kārdramaya, Vāhayāna, Jaimaya, Maimatāyana,
and Gopāli as the fifth among these—they are to be known as the Black Parāśaras.

1.117.s:
prārohayo bāhyatapāḥ pārṣayaḥ kautujātayaḥ ..
hāryaśviḥ pañcamaścaiṣāṃ jñeyā nīlaparāśarāḥ .. 33 ..
1.117.d:
प्रारोहयो बाह्यतपाः पार्षयः कौतुजातयः ॥
हार्यश्विः पञ्चमश्चैषां ज्ञेया नीलपराशराः ॥ 33 ॥
1.117.m:
Prārohaya, Bāhyatapas, Pārṣaya, Kautujāti,
and Hāryaśvi as the fifth among these—they are to be known as the Blue Parāśaras.

1.117.s:
kārṣṇāyaṇāḥ kāpisaudhāḥ kokeyasyā tayāstapāḥ ..
puṣkaraḥ pañcamaścaiṣāṃ jñeyā raktaparāśarāḥ .. 34 ..
1.117.d:
कार्ष्णायणाः कापिसौधाः कोकेयस्या तयास्तपाः ॥
पुष्करः पञ्चमश्चैषां ज्ञेया रक्तपराशराः ॥ 34 ॥
1.117.m:
Kārṣṇāyaṇas, Kāpisaudhas, Kokeyasyas, Tayāstapas,
and Puṣkara as the fifth among these—they are to be known as the Red Parāśaras.

1.117.s:
śraviṣṭhāyanā vārṣṇeyā dāseyāḥ ślokajāśca ye ..
iṣīkahastaḥ pañcamaśca ete śvetā parāśarāḥ .. 35..
1.117.d:
श्रविष्ठायना वार्ष्णेया दासेयाः श्लोकजाश्च ये ॥
इषीकहस्तः पञ्चमश्च एते श्वेता पराशराः ॥ 35॥
1.117.m:
Śraviṣṭhāyanas, Vārṣṇeyas, Dāseyas, and those who are Ślokajas,
and Iṣīkahasta as the fifth—these are the White Parāśaras.

1.117.s:
vaṭikā bādarāścaiva skambhanyāḥ krośakātayaḥ ..
kṣāmireṣāṃ pañcamaśca ete gauraparāśarāḥ ..35 ..
1.117.d:
वटिका बादराश्चैव स्कम्भन्याः क्रोशकातयः ॥
क्षामिरेषां पञ्चमश्च एते गौरपराशराः ॥35 ॥
1.117.m:
Vaṭikas, Bāadaras, Skambhanyas, Krośakātis,
and Kṣāmira as the fifth among these—these are the Pale-Yellow Parāśaras.

1.117.s:
khalvāyaṇī vārṣpayaṇī tilvaṇo bailvayūthapaḥ ..
tāmireṣāṃ pañcamaśca ete dhūmraparāśarāḥ .. 37 ..
1.117.d:
खल्वायणी वार्ष्पयणी तिल्वणो बैल्वयूथपः ॥
तामिरेषां पञ्चमश्च एते धूम्रपराशराः ॥ 37 ॥
1.117.m:
Khalvāyaṇī, Vārṣpayaṇī, Tilvaṇa, Bailvayūthapa,
and Tāmira as the fifth among these—these are the Smoky Parāśaras.

1.117.s:
parāśarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ tryārṣeyaḥ pravaro mataḥ ..
parāśaraśca śaktiśca vaśiṣṭhaśca mahātapāḥ .. 38 ..
1.117.d:
पराशराणां सर्वेषां त्र्यार्षेयः प्रवरो मतः ॥
पराशरश्च शक्तिश्च वशिष्ठश्च महातपाः ॥ 38 ॥
1.117.m:
For all the Parāśaras, a three-sage pravara is acknowledged:
Parāśara, Śakti, and Vasiṣṭha of great ascetic penance.

1.117.s: parasparamavaivāhyāḥ sarva eva parāśarāḥ .. 39 ..
1.117.d: परस्परमवैवाह्याः सर्व एव पराशराः ॥ 39 ॥
1.117.m: All Parāśaras without exception are forbidden from intermarrying.

1.117.s:
uktāstathaite nṛpa vaṃśamukhyāḥ pārāśarāḥ sūrya samaprabhāvāḥ ..
yeṣāṃ tu nāmnā parikīrtanena pāpaṃ samagraṃ puruṣo jahāti .. 1.117.40 ..
1.117.d:
उक्तास्तथैते नृप वंशमुख्याः पाराशराः सूर्य समप्रभावाः ॥
येषां तु नाम्ना परिकीर्तनेन पापं समग्रं पुरुषो जहाति ॥ 1.117.40 ॥
1.117.m: Thus, O king, these foremost of lineages, the descendants of Parāśara, having splendor equal to the sun, have been proclaimed, / by the recitation of whose names a man casts off all sin.

1.118.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ataḥ paramagastyasya vakṣye vaṃśodbhavāndvijān ..
āgastyeyaḥ karambho yaḥ kausalyākulajāstathā ..1..
1.118.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अतः परमगस्त्यस्य वक्ष्ये वंशोद्भवान्द्विजान् ॥
आगस्त्येयः करम्भो यः कौसल्याकुलजास्तथा ॥1॥
1.118.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall declare the twice-born sprung from the lineage of Agastya: / the descendant of Agastya, Karambha, and those born in the family of Kausalyā,

1.118.s:
svamedhaso mayobhuvastathā gāndhārakāyaniḥ..
paulastyāḥ pulahāścaiva kratuvaṃśabhavāstathā..2..
1.118.d:
स्वमेधसो मयोभुवस्तथा गान्धारकायनिः॥
पौलस्त्याः पुलहाश्चैव क्रतुवंशभवास्तथा॥2॥
1.118.m: Svamedhas, the Mayobhuvs, and Gāndhārakāyani, / the Paulastyas, the Pulahas, and those born in the lineage of Kratu.

1.118.s:
vārṣṇeyo'pi mataścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ ..
agastyaśca mahendraśca ṛṣiścaiva mayobhuvaḥ .. 3 ..
1.118.d:
वार्ष्णेयोऽपि मतश्चैषां सर्वेषां प्रवराः शुभाः ॥
अगस्त्यश्च महेन्द्रश्च ऋषिश्चैव मयोभुवः ॥ 3 ॥
1.118.m: Vārṣṇeya also is acknowledged, and the auspicious pravaras of all these are: / Agastya, Mahendra, and the sage Mayobhuva.

1.118.s:
parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
paurṇamāsāḥ pāraṇāśca tryārṣṇeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..4..
1.118.d:
परस्परमवैवाह्या ऋषयः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
पौर्णमासाः पारणाश्च त्र्यार्ष्णेयाः परिकीर्तिताः ॥4॥
1.118.m: These sages are proclaimed to be forbidden from intermarrying. / The Paurṇamāsas and the Pāraṇas are proclaimed to have three sage-ancestors:

1.118.s:
agastyaḥ paurṇamāsaśca pāraṇaśca mahātapāḥ ..
parasparamavaivāhyā paurṇamāsāśca pāraṇam .. 5..
1.118.d:
अगस्त्यः पौर्णमासश्च पारणश्च महातपाः ॥
परस्परमवैवाह्या पौर्णमासाश्च पारणम् ॥ 5॥
1.118.m: Agastya, Paurṇamāsa, and Pāraṇa of great ascetic penance. / The Paurṇamāsas and the Pāraṇas are forbidden from intermarrying.

1.118.s:
etaduktamṛṣīṇāṃ te vaṃśamuktamapūruṣam ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kiṃ tavānagha kathyatām ..6..
1.118.d:
एतदुक्तमृषीणां ते वंशमुक्तमपूरुषम् ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि किं तवानघ कथ्यताम् ॥6॥
1.118.m: This lineage of the sages, free from human flaw, has been told to you. / What shall I declare to you beyond this, O sinless one? Speak.

1.118.s:
vajra uvāca ..
pulahasya pulastyasya kratoścaiva mahātmanaḥ ..
agastyasya tathā caikaṃ kathaṃ vaṃśaṃ taducyate .. 7 ..
1.118.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
पुलहस्य पुलस्त्यस्य क्रतोश्चैव महात्मनः ॥
अगस्त्यस्य तथा चैकं कथं वंशं तदुच्यते ॥ 7 ॥
1.118.m: Vajra said: / How is it said that the lineage of Pulaha, of Pulastya, of the noble Kratu, / and of Agastya is one?

1.118.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
kratuḥ khalvanapatyo'sti rājanvaivasvatentare ..
idhmavāhaṃ sa putratve jagrāha nṛpasattama .. 8 ..
1.118.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
क्रतुः खल्वनपत्योऽस्ति राजन्वैवस्वतेन्तरे ॥
इध्मवाहं स पुत्रत्वे जग्राह नृपसत्तम ॥ 8 ॥
1.118.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Kratu indeed is childless in the period of Vaivasvata, O king; / he took Idhmavāha as his son, O best of kings,

1.118.s:
agastyaputraṃ dharmajña āgastyātkratavastathā ..
pulahasya tathā putraḥ tiraścaḥ pṛthivīpate .. 9 ..
1.118.d:
अगस्त्यपुत्रं धर्मज्ञ आगस्त्यात्क्रतवस्तथा ॥
पुलहस्य तथा पुत्रः तिरश्चः पृथिवीपते ॥ 9 ॥
1.118.m: the son of Agastya, O knower of dharma; and thus the Kratus descend from the Agastyas. / Likewise, O ruler of the earth, the son of Pulaha was Tiryañc.

1.118.s:
teṣāṃ te janma vakṣyāmi uttaratra yathā vidhi ..
pulahastvaprajāṃ dṛṣṭvā nātiprītamanā hyabhūt .. 1.118.10 ..
1.118.d:
तेषां ते जन्म वक्ष्यामि उत्तरत्र यथा विधि ॥
पुलहस्त्वप्रजां दृष्ट्वा नातिप्रीतमना ह्यभूत् ॥ 1.118.10 ॥
1.118.m: I shall relate their birth to you later according to rule. / Seeing himself without offspring, Pulaha was not at all pleased in mind.

1.118.s:
agastyajaṃ dṛḍhasyuṃ taṃ putratve kṛtavāṃstadā ..
paulahāśca tathā rājannāgastyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ .. 11 ..
1.118.d:
अगस्त्यजं दृढस्युं तं पुत्रत्वे कृतवांस्तदा ॥
पौलहाश्च तथा राजन्नागस्त्याः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 11 ॥
1.118.m: Then he took Dṛḍhasyu, born of Agastya, as his son; / and thus, O king, the Paulahas are proclaimed as Agastyas.

1.118.s:
ete tavoktāḥ pravarā dvijānāṃ mahānubhāvā nṛpa gotrakārāḥ ..
yeṣāṃ ca nāmnāṃ parikīrtanena pāpaṃ samagraṃ puruṣo jahāti .. 12 ..
1.118.d:
एते तवोक्ताः प्रवरा द्विजानां महानुभावा नृप गोत्रकाराः ॥
येषां च नाम्नां परिकीर्तनेन पापं समग्रं पुरुषो जहाति ॥ 12 ॥
1.118.m: These illustrious twice-born, the founders of gotras, have been declared to you, O king, / by the recitation of whose names a man casts off all sin.

1.119.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
asminvaivasvate prāpte śṛṇu dharmasya pārthiva ..
dākṣāyaṇyāśca sakalaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ vaṃśamuttamam .. 1 ..
1.119.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अस्मिन्वैवस्वते प्राप्ते शृणु धर्मस्य पार्थिव ॥
दाक्षायण्याश्च सकलं शृणु त्वं वंशमुत्तमम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.119.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Now that this [manvantara] of Vaivasvata has arrived, hear, O king, / hear completely the excellent lineage of Dharma and Dākṣāyaṇī.

1.119.s:
evaṃ tāni mahīdurgaśarīrāṇi narādhipa ..
arundhatyā prasūtāni dharmo vaivasvatentare .. 2 ..
1.119.d:
एवं तानि महीदुर्गशरीराणि नराधिप ॥
अरुन्धत्या प्रसूतानि धर्मो वैवस्वतेन्तरे ॥ 2 ॥
1.119.m: In this manner those bodies of the mountain-strongholds of the earth, O ruler of men, / were brought forth by Arundhatī through Dharma in the period of Vaivasvata.

1.119.s:
aṣṭau ca vasavaḥ putrā somapāśca vasostathā ..
dharo dhruvaśca somaśca āpaścaivānalānilau .. 3 ..
1.119.d:
अष्टौ च वसवः पुत्रा सोमपाश्च वसोस्तथा ॥
धरो ध्रुवश्च सोमश्च आपश्चैवानलानिलौ ॥ 3 ॥
1.119.m: And the eight Vasus were the sons of Vasu, who drink Soma: / Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Āpa, Anala, Anila,

1.119.s:
pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ ..
dharasya putrā'mbunimbaḥ kālaḥ putro dhruvasya ca .. 4 ..
1.119.d:
प्रत्यूषश्च प्रभासश्च वसवोऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
धरस्य पुत्राऽम्बुनिम्बः कालः पुत्रो ध्रुवस्य च ॥ 4 ॥
1.119.m: Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa—these are proclaimed as the eight Vasus. / The son of Dhara was Ambunimba, and Kāla was the son of Dhruva.

1.119.s:
kālasyāvayavānāṃ tu śarīrāṇi narādhipa ..
muhūrtavarjaṃ kālāddhi prasūtānyaviśeṣataḥ .. 5 ..
1.119.d:
कालस्यावयवानां तु शरीराणि नराधिप ॥
मुहूर्तवर्जं कालाद्धि प्रसूतान्यविशेषतः ॥ 5 ॥
1.119.m: The bodies of the divisions of Time, O ruler of men, / were born without distinction from Time, with the exception of the muhūrta.

1.119.s:
somasya bhagavānvarcāḥ śramastvāpasya kīrtyate ..
anekajanmā janavaḥ kumāraścānalasya tu .. 6 ..
1.119.d:
सोमस्य भगवान्वर्चाः श्रमस्त्वापस्य कीर्त्यते ॥
अनेकजन्मा जनवः कुमारश्चानलस्य तु ॥ 6 ॥
1.119.m: Soma's [son was] the lord Varcas; Śrama is recorded as Āpa's; / while Aneka-janman, Janavas, and Kumāra were Anala's.

1.119.s:
purojavāścānilasya pratyūṣasya ca devalaḥ ..
viśvakarmā prabhāsasya tridaśānāṃ sa vārdhakiḥ .. 7 ..
1.119.d:
पुरोजवाश्चानिलस्य प्रत्यूषस्य च देवलः ॥
विश्वकर्मा प्रभासस्य त्रिदशानां स वार्धकिः ॥ 7 ॥
1.119.m: And Anila's was Purojava; and Pratyūṣa's was Devala; / Prabhāsa's was Viśvakarman, the carpenter of the thirty [gods].

1.119.s:
jāmī duhitaraḥ proktā nāgavīthyādayo nava ..
laṃbāputraḥ smṛto ghoro bhānoḥ putraśca bhānavaḥ .. 8 ..
1.119.d:
जामी दुहितरः प्रोक्ता नागवीथ्यादयो नव ॥
लंबापुत्रः स्मृतो घोरो भानोः पुत्रश्च भानवः ॥ 8 ॥
1.119.m: Jāmī's daughters are spoken of as nine, beginning with Nāgavīthī. / Lambā's son is recorded as Ghora, and the Bhānus were the sons of Bhānu.

1.119.s:
graharkṣāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ cānyeṣāmapi tejasām ..
marutvatyāṃ marutvantaḥ sarve putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 9 ..
1.119.d:
ग्रहर्क्षाणां तु सर्वेषां चान्येषामपि तेजसाम् ॥
मरुत्वत्यां मरुत्वन्तः सर्वे पुत्राः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 9 ॥
1.119.m: Of all the planets, lunar mansions, and other luminaries too, / the Marutvants born of Marutvatī are proclaimed as all the sons.

1.119.s:
saṃkalpāyāśca saṃkalpāstathā putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
muhūrtāśca muhūrtāyāḥ sādhyātsādhyāsutāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 1.119.10 ..
1.119.d:
संकल्पायाश्च संकल्पास्तथा पुत्राः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
मुहूर्ताश्च मुहूर्तायाः साध्यात्साध्यासुताः स्मृताः ॥ 1.119.10 ॥
1.119.m: And the Saṃkalpas are proclaimed as sons of Saṃkalpā; / and the Muhūrtas, of Muhūrtā; the Sādhyas are recorded as the sons of Sādhyā:

1.119.s:
mattonmattaśca prāṇaśca naropāṇaśca vīryavān ..
cittirnaro hayaścaiva haṃso nārāyaṇastathā .. 11 ..
1.119.d:
मत्तोन्मत्तश्च प्राणश्च नरोपाणश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
चित्तिर्नरो हयश्चैव हंसो नारायणस्तथा ॥ 11 ॥
1.119.m: Matta, Unmatta, Prāṇa, and the powerful Naropāṇa, / Citti, Nara, Haya, Haṃsa, and Nārāyaṇa,

1.119.s:
vibhuścāpi prabhuścāpi sādhyā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ..
viśvāyāśca tathā putrā viśvedevāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 15 ..
1.119.d:
विभुश्चापि प्रभुश्चापि साध्या द्वादश कीर्तिताः॥
विश्वायाश्च तथा पुत्रा विश्वेदेवाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 15 ॥
1.119.m: as well as Vibhu and Prabhu; these twelve are proclaimed as the Sādhyas. / And the sons of Viśvā are proclaimed as the Viśvedevas:

1.119.s:
kraturdakṣo vasuḥ satyaḥ kālaḥ kāmo dhunistathā ..
ūravānmanujo viśveromāyāśca hi te daśa .. 13 ..
1.119.d:
क्रतुर्दक्षो वसुः सत्यः कालः कामो धुनिस्तथा ॥
ऊरवान्मनुजो विश्वेरोमायाश्च हि ते दश ॥ 13 ॥
1.119.m: Kratu, Dakṣa, Vasu, Satya, Kāla, Kāma, Dhuni, / Ūravān, Manuja, and Viśveromā—these ten are hers.

1.119.s:
etāvaduktaṃ tava dharmavaṃśaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ pārthivasaṃghamukhya ..
vyāsena vaktuṃ na hi śaktirasti rājanvinā varṣaśatairanekaiḥ .. 14 ..
1.119.d:
एतावदुक्तं तव धर्मवंशं संक्षेपतः पार्थिवसंघमुख्य ॥
व्यासेन वक्तुं न हि शक्तिरस्ति राजन्विना वर्षशतैरनेकैः ॥ 14 ॥
1.119.m: So much of the lineage of Dharma has been told to you in brief, O chief of the assembly of kings; / it is not possible, O king, to relate it in detail even in many hundreds of years.

1.120.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
ataḥ paraṃ kaśyapasya śṛṇu vaṃśaṃ narādhipa ..
yatra prāyeṇa saṃbhūtaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam .. 1 ..
1.120.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
अतः परं कश्यपस्य शृणु वंशं नराधिप ॥
यत्र प्रायेण संभूतं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.120.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hear now the lineage of Kaśyapa, O ruler of men, / from which almost the entire universe, both stationary and moving, came into being.

1.120.s:
aditerdvādaśādityā devaputrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
dhātā putro'ryamā pūṣā śakroṃ'śo varuṇo bhagaḥ .. 2 ..
1.120.d:
अदितेर्द्वादशादित्या देवपुत्राः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
धाता पुत्रोऽर्यमा पूषा शक्रोंऽशो वरुणो भगः ॥ 2 ॥
1.120.m: Twelve Ādityas are proclaimed as Aditi's sons, the gods: / Dhātṛ is a son, Aryaman, Pūṣan, Śakra, Aṃśa, Varuṇa, Bhaga,

1.120.s:
tvaṣṭā vivasvānvaruṇo viṣṇurdvādaśamastathā ..
viṣṇoraṃśena saṃbhūtāḥ sādhyā devagaṇā nṛpa .. 3 ..
1.120.d:
त्वष्टा विवस्वान्वरुणो विष्णुर्द्वादशमस्तथा ॥
विष्णोरंशेन संभूताः साध्या देवगणा नृप ॥ 3 ॥
1.120.m: Tvaṣṭṛ, Vivasvat, Varuṇa, and Viṣṇu as the twelfth. / The divine hosts of Sādhyas arose from a portion of Viṣṇu, O king.

1.120.s:
ta eva tejaso'rdhena jātāścaivāditeḥ sutāḥ ..
naranārāyaṇau cobhau yau te rājanmayeritau ..4 ..
1.120.d:
त एव तेजसोऽर्धेन जाताश्चैवादितेः सुताः ॥
नरनारायणौ चोभौ यौ ते राजन्मयेरितौ ॥4 ॥
1.120.m: They indeed were born as the sons of Aditi from half of his splendour; / and both Nara and Nārāyaṇa, who have been mentioned to you by me, O king,

1.120.s:
indrāviṣṇū tathaivoktā vādityeṣu narādhipa ..
manorantaramāsādya sarvatraiva janārdanaḥ .. 5 ..
1.120.d:
इन्द्राविष्णू तथैवोक्ता वादित्येषु नराधिप ॥
मनोरन्तरमासाद्य सर्वत्रैव जनार्दनः ॥ 5 ॥
1.120.m: as well as Indra and Viṣṇu, are likewise spoken of among the Ādityas, O ruler of men. / In every period of Manu, Janārdana,

1.120.s:
aṃśenaikena bhavati sagaṇaḥ somapāyinām ..
tasmingaṇe devavaro viṣṇurloka namaskṛtaḥ .. 6 ..
1.120.d:
अंशेनैकेन भवति सगणः सोमपायिनाम् ॥
तस्मिन्गणे देववरो विष्णुर्लोक नमस्कृतः ॥ 6 ॥
1.120.m: takes form with one portion along with the host of soma-drinkers. / In that host, the foremost of gods, Viṣṇu, is revered by the world.

1.120.s:
tejasā'bhyadhiko naiko bhavatīti na saṃśayaḥ ..
yasteṣāmārtiśamanaṃ karoti vasudhādhipa .. 7 ..
1.120.d:
तेजसाऽभ्यधिको नैको भवतीति न संशयः ॥
यस्तेषामार्तिशमनं करोति वसुधाधिप ॥ 7 ॥
1.120.m: In splendour, more than one does not excel him; of this there is no doubt— / he who brings an end to their distress, O lord of the earth.

1.120.s:
karmāṇyatīteṣu tathāntareṣu vakṣye bhaviṣyeṣu tathā narendra ..
manvantarāṇāṃ parikīrtaneṣu śṛṇuṣva tāvadditivaṃśamugram .. 8 ..
1.120.d:
कर्माण्यतीतेषु तथान्तरेषु वक्ष्ये भविष्येषु तथा नरेन्द्र ॥
मन्वन्तराणां परिकीर्तनेषु शृणुष्व तावद्दितिवंशमुग्रम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.120.m: I shall speak of [his] deeds in past periods of Manu as well as in future ones, O king, / in the recitals of the manvantaras; meanwhile, hear of the fierce lineage of Diti.

1.121.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
ditiḥ putradvayaṃ rājañjanayāmāsa viśrutam ..
hiraṇyākṣaṃ ca durdharṣaṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ tathā .. 1 ..
1.121.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
दितिः पुत्रद्वयं राजञ्जनयामास विश्रुतम् ॥
हिरण्याक्षं च दुर्धर्षं हिरण्यकशिपुं तथा ॥ 1 ॥
1.121.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Diti gave birth, O king, to two renowned sons: / the unassailable Hiraṇyākṣa and likewise Hiraṇyakaśipu.

1.121.s:
hiraṇyākṣo hato rājannṛvarāheṇa saṃyuge ..
hiraṇyakaśyapū rājannṛsiṃhena nipātitaḥ .. 2 ..
1.121.d:
हिरण्याक्षो हतो राजन्नृवराहेण संयुगे ॥
हिरण्यकश्यपू राजन्नृसिंहेन निपातितः ॥ 2 ॥
1.121.m: Hiraṇyākṣa was slain in battle by the Boar-man, O king; / Hiraṇyakaśipu was felled by Narasiṃha, O king.

1.121.s:
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putraḥ prahlādo'rikulāntakaḥ ..
kālanemiśca durdharṣo viṣṇunā ghātito yudhi .. 3 ..
1.121.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्रः प्रह्लादोऽरिकुलान्तकः ॥
कालनेमिश्च दुर्धर्षो विष्णुना घातितो युधि ॥ 3 ॥
1.121.m: Hiraṇyakaśipu's son was Prahlāda, slayer of the families of his foes; / and unassailable Kālanemi was struck down by Viṣṇu in battle.

1.121.s:
ārādhya keśavaṃ devaṃ prahlādaśca mahābalaḥ ..
prāptavāñjīvitaṃ dīrghaṃ brāhmaṃ dinamanuttamam .. 4 ..
1.121.d:
आराध्य केशवं देवं प्रह्लादश्च महाबलः ॥
प्राप्तवाञ्जीवितं दीर्घं ब्राह्मं दिनमनुत्तमम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.121.m: Having propitiated the divine Keśava, the mighty Prahlāda / obtained a long life, an incomparable day of Brahmā.

1.121.s:
kālanemiśca durdharṣo mahābalaparākramaḥ ..
nihato vāsudevena nivṛtte tārakāmaye .. 5..
1.121.d:
कालनेमिश्च दुर्धर्षो महाबलपराक्रमः ॥
निहतो वासुदेवेन निवृत्ते तारकामये ॥ 5॥
1.121.m: And unassailable Kālanemi, of great strength and valour, / was slain by Vāsudeva when the Tārakāmaya war had ceased.

1.121.s:
prahrādasya sutaḥ śrīmānrājannāmnā virocanaḥ ..
virocanasutaḥ śrīmānbalirityeva viśrutaḥ .. 6 ..
1.121.d:
प्रह्रादस्य सुतः श्रीमान्राजन्नाम्ना विरोचनः ॥
विरोचनसुतः श्रीमान्बलिरित्येव विश्रुतः ॥ 6 ॥
1.121.m: Prahrāda's illustrious son, O king, was named Virocana; / Virocana's illustrious son was renowned as Bali.

1.121.s:
vāmanaṃ rūpamāsthāya baddho yo viṣṇunā purā ..
balerbāṇaḥ suto rājansmṛto bāhusahasravān .. 7 ..
1.121.d:
वामनं रूपमास्थाय बद्धो यो विष्णुना पुरा ॥
बलेर्बाणः सुतो राजन्स्मृतो बाहुसहस्रवान् ॥ 7 ॥
1.121.m: Assuming the form of a dwarf, Viṣṇu bound him in ancient times. / Bali's son, O king, is remembered as Bāṇa of a thousand arms.

1.121.s:
pituste śvaśuraḥ śrīmānpiturarthe tavānagha ..
vivāhaṃ kṛtavānkṛṣṇo nagare śoṇitāhvaye .. 8 ..
1.121.d:
पितुस्ते श्वशुरः श्रीमान्पितुरर्थे तवानघ ॥
विवाहं कृतवान्कृष्णो नगरे शोणिताह्वये ॥ 8 ॥
1.121.m: He was the father-in-law of your father, O blameless one; for the sake of your father, / Kṛṣṇa performed the marriage in the city called Śoṇita,

1.121.s:
yasminsa vai devavaraḥ prasahya skandaṃ ca rudraṃ ditijaiḥ sametam ..
raṇe vijigye nṛpatipradhāna sahānugaṃ vīryabalopapannam .. 9 ..
1.121.d:
यस्मिन्स वै देववरः प्रसह्य स्कन्दं च रुद्रं दितिजैः समेतम् ॥
रणे विजिग्ये नृपतिप्रधान सहानुगं वीर्यबलोपपन्नम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.121.m: wherein that foremost of gods by force conquered in battle / Skanda, and Rudra joined with the sons of Diti, and [Bāṇa] the chief of rulers along with his followers, endowed with heroism and strength.

1.122.s:
vajra uvāca..
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putro kālanemirmahāsuraḥ..
kathaṃ kṛṣṇena nihatastanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ..1..
1.122.d:
वज्र उवाच॥
हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्रो कालनेमिर्महासुरः॥
कथं कृष्णेन निहतस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥1॥
1.122.m: Vajra said: / How was the great asura Kālanemi, the son of Hiraṇyakaśipu, / slain by Kṛṣṇa? Tell me that as I ask.

1.122.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
yadā daityavadhe vṛtte daityāḥ pātālamāśritāḥ..
mayatārau samāśritya bhūyo devānpradudruvuḥ .. 2 ..
1.122.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
यदा दैत्यवधे वृत्ते दैत्याः पातालमाश्रिताः॥
मयतारौ समाश्रित्य भूयो देवान्प्रदुद्रुवुः ॥ 2 ॥
1.122.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When, after the slaughter of the daityas had occurred, the daityas took refuge in Pātāla, / relying on Maya and Tāra, they attacked the gods once more.

1.122.s:
tatra devagaṇāḥ sarve mayatārapuraḥsaraiḥ ..
dānavairnihatā yuddhe devācāryaṃ bṛhaspatim .. 3 ..
1.122.d:
तत्र देवगणाः सर्वे मयतारपुरःसरैः ॥
दानवैर्निहता युद्धे देवाचार्यं बृहस्पतिम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.122.m: There, all the hosts of gods, struck down in battle by the dānavas / led by Maya and Tāra, [fled] to the preceptor of the gods, Bṛhaspati.

1.122.s:
saṃprāptāḥ śaraṇaṃ vipraṃ tānuvāca bṛhaspatiḥ ..
tārakaśca mayaścaiva mahābalaparākramau .. 4 ..
1.122.d:
संप्राप्ताः शरणं विप्रं तानुवाच बृहस्पतिः ॥
तारकश्च मयश्चैव महाबलपराक्रमौ ॥ 4 ॥
1.122.m: They approached the brahmin for refuge. Bṛhaspati said to them: / 'Tāraka and Maya are endowed with great strength and valour;

1.122.s:
yayurjetuṃ devagaṇām̐stāvimau codayāmyaham ..
evamuktvā devagaṇāndevācāryo bṛhaspatiḥ ..
tuṣṭāva devadeveśaṃ bahurūpaṃ hutāśanam .. 5 ..
1.122.d:
ययुर्जेतुं देवगणाम्̐स्ताविमौ चोदयाम्यहम् ॥
एवमुक्त्वा देवगणान्देवाचार्यो बृहस्पतिः ॥
तुष्टाव देवदेवेशं बहुरूपं हुताशनम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.122.m: they have gone out to conquer the hosts of gods. I shall urge those two.' / Having spoken thus to the hosts of gods, Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods, / praised the fire-god, the ruler of the god of gods, of manifold forms.

1.122.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca ..
tvamagne sarvabhūtānāmantaścarasi pāvaka ..
vedāstvadarthaṃ jātāśca jātavedāstathā hyasi .. 6 ..
1.122.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥
त्वमग्ने सर्वभूतानामन्तश्चरसि पावक ॥
वेदास्त्वदर्थं जाताश्च जातवेदास्तथा ह्यसि ॥ 6 ॥
1.122.m: Bṛhaspati said: / 'O Agni, you move within all beings, O purifier; / the Vedas arose for your sake, and indeed you are Jātavedas.

1.122.s:
tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkārastvaṃ havīṃṣi mahādyute ..
tvaṃ sa deva carasyātmā viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ .. 7 ..
1.122.d:
त्वं यज्ञस्त्वं वषट्कारस्त्वं हवींषि महाद्युते ॥
त्वं स देव चरस्यात्मा विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥ 7 ॥
1.122.m: You are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the oblations, O one of great splendour; / you move, O god, as the self of Viṣṇu of boundless splendour.

1.122.s:
tvaṃ mukhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ sarvasyātmā tathā bhavān ..
ūṣmā tvaṃ dehināṃ dehe bhuktapītavatastathā..8..
1.122.d:
त्वं मुखं सर्वदेवानां सर्वस्यात्मा तथा भवान् ॥
ऊष्मा त्वं देहिनां देहे भुक्तपीतवतस्तथा॥8॥
1.122.m: You are the mouth of all the gods, and you are the self of all; / you are the heat within the body of embodied beings, of one who has eaten and drunk.

1.122.s:
yacchaktiḥ sarvadevānāṃ tvadīyā bhūtabhāvana..
prāptā tvayāhutiḥ samyagāditya mupatiṣṭhate .. 9 ..
1.122.d:
यच्छक्तिः सर्वदेवानां त्वदीया भूतभावन॥
प्राप्ता त्वयाहुतिः सम्यगादित्य मुपतिष्ठते ॥ 9 ॥
1.122.m: Whatever power belongs to all the gods is yours, O originator of beings; / the oblation duly received by you approaches the sun.

1.122.s:
ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭerannaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ ..
sarvadevavareśānaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ .. 1.122.10 ..
1.122.d:
आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिर्वृष्टेरन्नं ततः प्रजाः ॥
सर्वदेववरेशानः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः ॥ 1.122.10 ॥
1.122.m: From the sun rain is born, from rain food, and thence living beings; / you are the lord, foremost among all gods, revered by all worlds.

1.122.s:
trailokyasya samutpattāvekaḥ kāraṇatāṃ gataḥ ..
kālāgnirudro bhagavāñjagatsaṃhārakārakaḥ..11..
1.122.d:
त्रैलोक्यस्य समुत्पत्तावेकः कारणतां गतः ॥
कालाग्निरुद्रो भगवाञ्जगत्संहारकारकः॥11॥
1.122.m: In the origination of the threefold world, you alone have become the cause; / you are the lord Kālāgnirudra, the author of the destruction of the universe.

1.122.s:
sthitau nimittaṃ ca bhavānsarveṣāṃ dehināṃ śamaḥ..
atīva durdharaṃ deva tava tejaḥ sudāruṇam ..12...
1.122.d:
स्थितौ निमित्तं च भवान्सर्वेषां देहिनां शमः॥
अतीव दुर्धरं देव तव तेजः सुदारुणम् ॥12॥।
1.122.m: And during its maintenance you are the cause, the tranquility of all embodied beings; / exceedingly difficult to bear, O god, is your most dreadful splendour.'

1.122.s:
tejasā tena daityendrāñjahi mā tvaṃ ciraṃ kṛthā ..
sakhā ca te raṇe deva bhaviṣyati samīraṇaḥ ..13..
1.122.d:
तेजसा तेन दैत्येन्द्राञ्जहि मा त्वं चिरं कृथा ॥
सखा च ते रणे देव भविष्यति समीरणः ॥13॥
1.122.m:
With that splendour, destroy the lords of the Daityas; do not delay!
And in battle, O god, the Wind shall be your ally.

1.122.s:
ityevamuktoṅgirasā mahātmā tatheti taṃ prāha nṛpendra pūjyam ..
jīvo'pi gatvā pavanaṃ jagāda deveśvarasyānaghasiddhimicchan..14..
1.122.d:
इत्येवमुक्तोङ्गिरसा महात्मा तथेति तं प्राह नृपेन्द्र पूज्यम् ॥
जीवोऽपि गत्वा पवनं जगाद देवेश्वरस्यानघसिद्धिमिच्छन्॥14॥
1.122.m:
Having been spoken to thus by the son of Aṅgiras, the great-souled [Fire], O worshipful king of men, replied to him: "So be it!"
Jīva also, desiring unblemished success for the lord of the gods, went and spoke to the Wind.

1.123.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca..
jagadāyurbhavānvāyo śarīrasthaḥ śarīriṇām.
anantamūrtirdharmātmā devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ ..1..
1.123.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच॥
जगदायुर्भवान्वायो शरीरस्थः शरीरिणाम्।
अनन्तमूर्तिर्धर्मात्मा देवो नारायणः प्रभुः ॥1॥
1.123.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
You, O Wind, are the life-breath of the world, abiding within the body of embodied beings.
You are the lord, the god Nārāyaṇa, whose forms are endless, whose self is dharma,

1.123.s:
acintyavīryaḥ puruṣaḥ sadādhāraḥ sanātanaḥ ..
sākṣibhūtaśca sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ śubhapāpayoḥ ..2..
1.123.d:
अचिन्त्यवीर्यः पुरुषः सदाधारः सनातनः ॥
साक्षिभूतश्च सर्वेषां कर्मणां शुभपापयोः ॥2॥
1.123.m:
The Cosmic Person of inconceivable valour, the eternal foundation of all,
And the witness of all actions, both virtuous and evil.

1.123.s:
ghrāṇastvaṃ dehināṃ dehe ceṣṭitañca tathā bhavān ..
bhavānrudro bhavānbrahmā bhavānviṣṇuḥ sanātana .. 3 ..
1.123.d:
घ्राणस्त्वं देहिनां देहे चेष्टितञ्च तथा भवान् ॥
भवान्रुद्रो भवान्ब्रह्मा भवान्विष्णुः सनातन ॥ 3 ॥
1.123.m:
You are the sense of smell in the body of embodied beings, and likewise you are their movement.
You are Rudra, you are Brahmā, you are Viṣṇu, O eternal one!

1.123.s:
tavāyattaṃ hi jagatāṃ varṣāvarṣaṃ śubhāśubhama ..
bhavānvisṛjate meghānbhavānsaṃharate punaḥ .. 4 ..
1.123.d:
तवायत्तं हि जगतां वर्षावर्षं शुभाशुभम ॥
भवान्विसृजते मेघान्भवान्संहरते पुनः ॥ 4 ॥
1.123.m:
Dependent on you indeed is the rain and drought, the auspicious and inauspicious for the worlds.
You release the clouds; you draw them back again.

1.123.s:
bhavāndhārayate meghānvarṣamāṇām̐stathā divi ..
ādityaraśmipītasya meghodaragatasya ca ..5..
1.123.d:
भवान्धारयते मेघान्वर्षमाणाम्̐स्तथा दिवि ॥
आदित्यरश्मिपीतस्य मेघोदरगतस्य च ॥5॥
1.123.m:
You sustain the raining clouds in the sky.
Of the moisture drunk by the rays of the sun and entered into the belly of the clouds,

1.123.s:
rasasya bhaṅktā satataṃ bhavāneva nabhastale ..
taḍillatānāṃ ca tathā bhavānkartā jagattraye.. 6 ..
1.123.d:
रसस्य भङ्क्ता सततं भवानेव नभस्तले ॥
तडिल्लतानां च तथा भवान्कर्ता जगत्त्रये॥ 6 ॥
1.123.m:
You alone are constantly the breaker in the sky;
And in the three worlds, you are likewise the maker of the creepers of lightning.

1.123.s:
ambhasāṃ bhedakāle tu sarvādhāraḥ samīraṇa ..
parasparaṃ hi bhavatastathā saṃghaṭanātprabho .. 7 ..
1.123.d:
अम्भसां भेदकाले तु सर्वाधारः समीरण ॥
परस्परं हि भवतस्तथा संघटनात्प्रभो ॥ 7 ॥
1.123.m:
At the time of dispersing the waters, you are the support of all, O Wind!
For through your mutual collision [of the clouds], O Lord,

1.123.s:
garjitaṃ jāyate loke meghodara gataṃ mahat ..
balena tvatsamaṃ nānyaṃ bhūtaṃ paśyāmi bhūtale ..8 ..
1.123.d:
गर्जितं जायते लोके मेघोदर गतं महत् ॥
बलेन त्वत्समं नान्यं भूतं पश्यामि भूतले ॥8 ॥
1.123.m:
Great thundering arises in the world from within the belly of the clouds.
I see no other being on the face of the earth equal to you in strength.
Therefore, grant your assistance to the Fire, whose form is the Veda.

1.123.s:
etāvaduktoṅgirasā mahātmā tatheti taṃ prāha samīraṇo'pi ..
jagāma yuddhaṃ saha pāvakena daityeśvarāndevaripūnmahātmā .. 1.123.10 ..
1.123.d:
एतावदुक्तोङ्गिरसा महात्मा तथेति तं प्राह समीरणोऽपि ॥
जगाम युद्धं सह पावकेन दैत्येश्वरान्देवरिपून्महात्मा ॥ 1.123.10 ॥
1.123.m:
Addressed with these words by the descendant of Aṅgiras, the great-souled Wind also said to him: "So be it!"
The great-souled one went to battle along with Fire against the lords of the Daityas, the enemies of the gods.

1.124.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
vāyvagnī sahitau gatvā mayatārapurogamān ...
jigyatuḥ samare daityānnānāpraharaṇodyatāna .. 1 ..
1.124.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
वाय्वग्नी सहितौ गत्वा मयतारपुरोगमान् ॥।
जिग्यतुः समरे दैत्यान्नानाप्रहरणोद्यतान ॥ 1 ॥
1.124.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Wind and Fire, having gone together, conquered in battle
The Daityas led by Maya and Tāra, who were upraised with various weapons.

1.124.s:
vijitāste raṇe daityā mayatārapurogamāḥ..
tyaktadevālayāḥ sarve varuṇālayamāgatāḥ .. 2 ..
1.124.d:
विजितास्ते रणे दैत्या मयतारपुरोगमाः॥
त्यक्तदेवालयाः सर्वे वरुणालयमागताः ॥ 2 ॥
1.124.m:
Vanished in battle, those Daityas led by Maya and Tāra,
Having abandoned all the abodes of the gods, went to the abode of Varuṇa.

1.124.s:
etasminneva kāle tu hiraṇyakaśipoḥ sutaḥ ..
kālanemiriti khyātaḥ śataśīrṣonudṛśyate..3..
1.124.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु हिरण्यकशिपोः सुतः ॥
कालनेमिरिति ख्यातः शतशीर्षोनुदृश्यते॥3॥
1.124.m:
At that very time, the son of Hiraṇyakaśipu,
Renowned as Kālanemi, was seen with a hundred heads,

With a hundred arms, a vast body, appearing like a mountain,
Fierce, having obtained a boon from Brahmā, with an appearance like a scorched mountain,

1.124.s:
ekodaro dvipādaśca ekagrīvaḥ surāntakaḥ..
aṅgadī baddhamukuṭaḥ kuṇḍalāmbarabhūṣaṇaḥ..
sarvāyudhadharo raudro gadāpāṇirvibhīṣaṇaḥ ..
dattvā'bhayaṃ sa daityānāṃ tasmai meruṃ surālayam .. 6 ..
1.124.d:
एकोदरो द्विपादश्च एकग्रीवः सुरान्तकः॥
अङ्गदी बद्धमुकुटः कुण्डलाम्बरभूषणः॥
सर्वायुधधरो रौद्रो गदापाणिर्विभीषणः ॥
दत्त्वाऽभयं स दैत्यानां तस्मै मेरुं सुरालयम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.124.m:
With one belly, two feet, and a single neck, the destroyer of the gods,
Wearing armlets, with his diadem bound, adorned with earrings and garments,
Bearing all weapons, terrible, with a mace in his hand, terrifying.
Having granted protection to the Daityas, [he went] to Meru, the abode of the gods;

1.124.s:
gatvā vijigye tridaśānsthānebhyaścāvaropayat ..
trailokyamātmasātkṛtvā sukhamāste triviṣṭape .. 7 ..
1.124.d:
गत्वा विजिग्ये त्रिदशान्स्थानेभ्यश्चावरोपयत् ॥
त्रैलोक्यमात्मसात्कृत्वा सुखमास्ते त्रिविष्टपे ॥ 7 ॥
1.124.m:
Having gone, he conquered the thirty gods and drove them down from their places;
Having brought the three worlds under his own control, he dwelt happily in heaven.

1.124.s:
tasya te hyanugāḥ sarve lokāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ ..
tadājñākāriṇaḥ sarve tadbhāvasyānuvartakāḥ .. 8 ..
1.124.d:
तस्य ते ह्यनुगाः सर्वे लोकाः स्थावरजङ्गमाः ॥
तदाज्ञाकारिणः सर्वे तद्भावस्यानुवर्तकाः ॥ 8 ॥
1.124.m:
All the worlds, mobile and immobile, were his followers;
All carried out his commands and conformed to his disposition.

1.124.s:
pañca tatrābhyavartanta viparītena karmaṇā ..
vedo dharmaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ śrīśca nārāyaṇāśrayā .. 9 ..
1.124.d:
पञ्च तत्राभ्यवर्तन्त विपरीतेन कर्मणा ॥
वेदो धर्मः क्षमा सत्यं श्रीश्च नारायणाश्रया ॥ 9 ॥
1.124.m:
Five [alone] operated there with contrary action:
The Veda, dharma, forbearance, truth, and Śrī, who has Nārāyaṇa as her refuge.

Because of their constant alliance, the enraged lord of the Dānavas,
Seeking the realm of Viṣṇu, went into the presence of Nārāyaṇa.

1.124.s:
jñātvā daityamathāyāntaṃ devopi madhusūdanaḥ..
tārkṣyamāvāhayāñcakre āruroha ca taṃ hariḥ..
sa dadarśa hariṃ devaṃ tārkṣyasthaṃ daityarāṭ tadā..
sajalajaladanīlaṃ padmapatrāyatākṣaṃ khagapatimavarūḍhaṃ kalpavṛkṣopamānam..
halamusalagadābhiḥ śobhitaṃ devadevaṃ varapuruṣamajeyaṃ śārṅgacakrāsipāṇim..12..
1.124.d:
ज्ञात्वा दैत्यमथायान्तं देवोपि मधुसूदनः॥
तार्क्ष्यमावाहयाञ्चक्रे आरुरोह च तं हरिः॥
स ददर्श हरिं देवं तार्क्ष्यस्थं दैत्यराट् तदा॥
सजलजलदनीलं पद्मपत्रायताक्षं खगपतिमवरूढं कल्पवृक्षोपमानम्॥
हलमुसलगदाभिः शोभितं देवदेवं वरपुरुषमजेयं शार्ङ्गचक्रासिपाणिम्॥12॥
1.124.m:
Knowing that the Daitya was approaching, the god, the slayer of Madhu,
Summoned Tārkṣya, and Hari mounted him.
The king of the Daityas then saw the god Hari stationed upon Tārkṣya—
Dark as a water-laden cloud, with eyes as long as lotus petals, mounted upon the king of birds, resembling the wishing-tree,
The god of gods adorned with ploughshare, pestle, and mace, the supreme, unconquerable Person, holding the bow Śārṅga, the discus, and the sword in his hands.

1.125.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
dṛṣṭvā sa purato devaṃ dānavānabhyabhāṣata ..
ayaṃ sa dṛśyate viṣṇurdānavā yena ghātitāḥ .. 1 ..
1.125.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
दृष्ट्वा स पुरतो देवं दानवानभ्यभाषत ॥
अयं स दृश्यते विष्णुर्दानवा येन घातिताः ॥ 1 ॥
1.125.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Seeing the god before him, he addressed the Dānavas:
"This is seen to be that Viṣṇu by whom the Dānavas were slain.

1.125.s:
kutṛṣṇayeva śakrārthe babhūva kila vāmanaḥ ..
yadā vañcitavānputraṃ bhrātṛvyasya baliṃ mama .. 2 ..
1.125.d:
कुतृष्णयेव शक्रार्थे बभूव किल वामनः ॥
यदा वञ्चितवान्पुत्रं भ्रातृव्यस्य बलिं मम ॥ 2 ॥
1.125.m:
As if out of base greed, for the sake of Śakra, he indeed became the Dwarf,
When he deceived Bali, the son of my brother.

1.125.s:
nṛvarāhavapuḥ kṛtvā lokacittaharaṃ puro ..
hiraṇyākṣaṃ jaghānaiva pitṛvyaṃ mama vismitam .. 3 ..
1.125.d:
नृवराहवपुः कृत्वा लोकचित्तहरं पुरो ॥
हिरण्याक्षं जघानैव पितृव्यं मम विस्मितम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.125.m:
Having assumed the form of a man-boar captivating the hearts of the world, in earlier times
He slew Hiraṇyākṣa, my father's brother, who was struck with astonishment.

1.125.s:
apūrvaṃ rūpamāsthāya narasiṃhasya dānavāḥ ..
pitaraṃ yo jaghānaiva hiraṇyakaśipuṃ raṇe.. 4 ..
1.125.d:
अपूर्वं रूपमास्थाय नरसिंहस्य दानवाः ॥
पितरं यो जघानैव हिरण्यकशिपुं रणे॥ 4 ॥
1.125.m:
Having assumed the unprecedented form of Narasiṃha, O Dānavas,
He slew my father Hiraṇyakaśipu in battle.

1.125.s:
varāharūpiṇānena pātālatalamāsthitāḥ ..
asambhāvyabhayenājau dānavā vinipātitāḥ .. 5 ..
1.125.d:
वराहरूपिणानेन पातालतलमास्थिताः ॥
असम्भाव्यभयेनाजौ दानवा विनिपातिताः ॥ 5 ॥
1.125.m:
By this one in the form of a boar, the Dānavas dwelling in the depths of Pātāla
Were struck down in battle by an unimaginable terror.

1.125.s:
narāśva vapuṣā yena madhukaiṭabhayoḥ purā ..
pātālādāhṛtā vedāstatastau yudhi ghātitau .. 6 ..
1.125.d:
नराश्व वपुषा येन मधुकैटभयोः पुरा ॥
पातालादाहृता वेदास्ततस्तौ युधि घातितौ ॥ 6 ॥
1.125.m:
By him who in earlier times, with the body of a man-horse, brought back the Vedas
From Pātāla from Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and then slew the two in battle.

1.125.s:
asyājñākāriṇo devā na saṃtiṣṭhanti śāsane ..
ayaṃ sa rakṣāṃ devānāmasmābhirviprakṛṣyatām .. 7 ..
1.125.d:
अस्याज्ञाकारिणो देवा न संतिष्ठन्ति शासने ॥
अयं स रक्षां देवानामस्माभिर्विप्रकृष्यताम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.125.m:
The gods who carry out his commands do not abide by our rule;
Let this protector of the gods be dragged down by us!

1.125.s:
trailokye daityamudbhūtaṃ yuddhenaiva punaḥpunaḥ ..
devasādgama ityeva tena vadhyo'tha me ripuḥ .. 8 ..
1.125.d:
त्रैलोक्ये दैत्यमुद्भूतं युद्धेनैव पुनःपुनः ॥
देवसाद्गम इत्येव तेन वध्योऽथ मे रिपुः ॥ 8 ॥
1.125.m:
Whatever Daitya has arisen in the three worlds has repeatedly, through battle alone,
Gone into the power of the gods; therefore, this enemy of mine must be slain.

1.125.s:
atītasyādya kālasya durnayasya kṛtasya ca ..
bhokṣyate'yaṃ phalaṃ daityāḥ sarve paśyantu mā ciram .. 9 ..
1.125.d:
अतीतस्याद्य कालस्य दुर्नयस्य कृतस्य च ॥
भोक्ष्यतेऽयं फलं दैत्याः सर्वे पश्यन्तु मा चिरम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.125.m:
For his misconduct committed in past times,
He shall today enjoy the fruit! Let all the Daityas watch; do not delay!"

1.125.s:
ityetaddaityanāthasya vākyaṃ śrutvaiva dānavāḥ ..
jayaśabdaṃ tataścakruḥ siṃhanādaravaṃ tathā .. 1.125.10 ..
1.125.d:
इत्येतद्दैत्यनाथस्य वाक्यं श्रुत्वैव दानवाः ॥
जयशब्दं ततश्चक्रुः सिंहनादरवं तथा ॥ 1.125.10 ॥
1.125.m:
Hearing these words of the lord of the Daityas, the Dānavas
Then uttered shouts of victory and the roar of a lion's roar.

1.125.s:
vācaśca pratikūlāstāstena duṣṭena cetasā ..
tacchrutvā ca harirdevaḥ kruddho nāmedamabravīt .. 11 ..
1.125.d:
वाचश्च प्रतिकूलास्तास्तेन दुष्टेन चेतसा ॥
तच्छ्रुत्वा च हरिर्देवः क्रुद्धो नामेदमब्रवीत् ॥ 11 ॥
1.125.m:
And with that wicked mind he spoke those hostile words.
Hearing that, the god Hari, enraged, said this:

1.125.s:
kimidaṃ garjase daitya śāradāmbudavadvṛthā..
prajāpatikṛtaṃ setuṃ kathaṃ laṅghitumicchasi..12..
1.125.d:
किमिदं गर्जसे दैत्य शारदाम्बुदवद्वृथा॥
प्रजापतिकृतं सेतुं कथं लङ्घितुमिच्छसि॥12॥
1.125.m:
"Why do you roar thus in vain, O Daitya, like an autumn cloud?
How do you wish to transgress the boundary established by the Lord of Creatures?"

1.125.s:
evaṃ kathatordevadaityayoḥ pārthivottama..
prāvartata raṇo ghoro gadāpātavibhīṣaṇaḥ..13..
1.125.d:
एवं कथतोर्देवदैत्ययोः पार्थिवोत्तम॥
प्रावर्तत रणो घोरो गदापातविभीषणः॥13॥
1.125.m:
While the god and the Daitya were speaking thus, O best of kings,
A dread battle commenced, terrifying with the falling of maces.

1.125.s:
dānavairdevadevo'pi kālanemipuraḥsaraiḥ..
saṃchādyate mahāstraughairmeghairiva nabhastalam..14..
1.125.d:
दानवैर्देवदेवोऽपि कालनेमिपुरःसरैः॥
संछाद्यते महास्त्रौघैर्मेघैरिव नभस्तलम्॥14॥
1.125.m:
The god of gods was covered by the Dānavas headed by Kālanemi
With streams of great weapons, as the vault of the sky is covered by clouds.

1.125.s:
saṃchādyamāno daityendrairdevadevo na vivyathe ..
yodhayāmāsa sa raṇe gadayā dānavānbahūn .. 15 ..
1.125.d:
संछाद्यमानो दैत्येन्द्रैर्देवदेवो न विव्यथे ॥
योधयामास स रणे गदया दानवान्बहून् ॥ 15 ॥
1.125.m:
Though covered by the lords of the Daityas, the god of gods was not shaken;
He fought many Dānavas in battle with his mace.

1.125.s:
tasya daityaprasaktasya kālanemirmahāsuraḥ ..
pātayāmāsa vegena gadāṃ garuḍamūrdhani .. 16 ..
1.125.d:
तस्य दैत्यप्रसक्तस्य कालनेमिर्महासुरः ॥
पातयामास वेगेन गदां गरुडमूर्धनि ॥ 16 ॥
1.125.m:
While he was engaged with the Daityas, the great Asura Kālanemi
Violently hurled a mace onto the head of Garuḍa.

1.125.s:
gadāghātena raudreṇa tena tārkṣyasya mānada ..
nāsā bhagnā vyathā jātā raktacchardiśca dāruṇā .. 17 ..
1.125.d:
गदाघातेन रौद्रेण तेन तार्क्ष्यस्य मानद ॥
नासा भग्ना व्यथा जाता रक्तच्छर्दिश्च दारुणा ॥ 17 ॥
1.125.m: By that terrible blow of the club, O giver of honor, / Tārkṣya's beak was broken, pain arose, and terrible vomiting of blood [ensued].

1.125.s:
vyathitaṃ garuḍaṃ dṛṣṭvā devena harimedhasā ..
kṣiptaṃ daityavināśāya tadā cakraṃ sudāruṇam .. 18 ..
1.125.d:
व्यथितं गरुडं दृष्ट्वा देवेन हरिमेधसा ॥
क्षिप्तं दैत्यविनाशाय तदा चक्रं सुदारुणम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.125.m: Seeing Garuḍa afflicted, the god Harimedhas / then hurled his exceedingly fierce discus for the destruction of the Daitya.

1.125.s:
yattatsudarśanaṃ nāma sūryatejaḥsamudbhavam ..
vajranābhaṃ sahasrāraṃ kṣaraparyantamaṇḍalam .. 19 ..
1.125.d:
यत्तत्सुदर्शनं नाम सूर्यतेजःसमुद्भवम् ॥
वज्रनाभं सहस्रारं क्षरपर्यन्तमण्डलम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.125.m: That which is named Sudarśana, born from the splendor of the sun, / having a navel of diamond, a thousand spokes, and a rim-circle sharp as a razor,

1.125.s:
cyutaṃ cakrikarāccakraṃ kālanemiṃ mahāsuram ..
śīghraṃ viśirasaṃ cakre vibāhuṃ ca tathā nṛpa .. 1.125.20 ..
1.125.d:
च्युतं चक्रिकराच्चक्रं कालनेमिं महासुरम् ॥
शीघ्रं विशिरसं चक्रे विबाहुं च तथा नृप ॥ 1.125.20 ॥
1.125.m: the discus, released from the hand of the discus-bearer, O king, / swiftly made the great Asura Kālanemi headless and armless.

1.125.s:
vibāhuśirasaṃ kṛtvā devahastamupeyivān ..
vibāhuśirasaṃ kāyaṃ kṣaracchoṇitanirjharam .. 21 ..
1.125.d:
विबाहुशिरसं कृत्वा देवहस्तमुपेयिवान् ॥
विबाहुशिरसं कायं क्षरच्छोणितनिर्झरम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.125.m: Having made him armless and headless, it returned to the god's hand. / The body, deprived of arms and head, streaming with a torrent of blood,

1.125.s:
na papātāsya medinyāṃ yadā tārkṣyastato rayāt ..
urusā pātayāmāsa devānāṃ paśyatāṃ tadā .. 25 ..
1.125.d:
न पपातास्य मेदिन्यां यदा तार्क्ष्यस्ततो रयात् ॥
उरुसा पातयामास देवानां पश्यतां तदा ॥ 25 ॥
1.125.m: did not fall to the earth; then Tārkṣya, with swift speed, / cast it down with his chest while the gods looked on.

1.125.s:
patatā daityakāyena saśailavanakānanā ..
kampitā vasudhā sarvā patitāśca śiloccayāḥ .. 23 ..
1.125.d:
पतता दैत्यकायेन सशैलवनकानना ॥
कम्पिता वसुधा सर्वा पतिताश्च शिलोच्चयाः ॥ 23 ॥
1.125.m: By the falling body of the Daitya, the entire earth, / with its mountains, woods, and forests, was shaken, and peaks of stone collapsed.

1.125.s:
dānavendraṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā mayatārapurogamāḥ ..
tuṣṭuvurdevadevaśaṃ varacakrāsipāṇinam .. 24 ..
1.125.d:
दानवेन्द्रं हतं दृष्ट्वा मयतारपुरोगमाः ॥
तुष्टुवुर्देवदेवशं वरचक्रासिपाणिनम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.125.m: Seeing the lord of Dānavas slain, [the demons] led by Maya and Tāra / praised the god of gods, who holds the excellent discus and sword in his hand.

1.125.s:
tuṣṭāva ca tadā devo brahmā śubhacaturmukhaḥ ..
stutaśca brahmaṇā devo lokapālānyathā purā ..25..
1.125.d:
तुष्टाव च तदा देवो ब्रह्मा शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥
स्तुतश्च ब्रह्मणा देवो लोकपालान्यथा पुरा ॥25॥
1.125.m: And then the auspicious four-faced god Brahmā praised [him]; / and praised by Brahmā, the god [restored] the guardians of the worlds as before,

1.125.s:
sthāneṣu yojayāmāsa yajñaṃ devamukhe tathā ..
jagāma brahmaṇā sārdhaṃ brahmalokaṃ tadā vibhuḥ ..26..
1.125.d:
स्थानेषु योजयामास यज्ञं देवमुखे तथा ॥
जगाम ब्रह्मणा सार्धं ब्रह्मलोकं तदा विभुः ॥26॥
1.125.m: appointed them to their places, and likewise [established] sacrifice in the mouth of the gods. / Then the all-pervading lord went together with Brahmā to the world of Brahmā.

1.125.s:
tatrātmānaṃ yajñamūrti mijyamānaṃ dvijottamaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā svayaṃ tu jagrāha yajñabhāgaṃ mahātmanām .. 27 ..
1.125.d:
तत्रात्मानं यज्ञमूर्ति मिज्यमानं द्विजोत्तमः ॥
दृष्ट्वा स्वयं तु जग्राह यज्ञभागं महात्मनाम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.125.m: Seeing himself there being worshiped as the embodiment of sacrifice by the best of the twice-born, / he himself took the sacrificial portion of the great-souled ones.

1.125.s:
tatra pūjāmupādāya jagāma sa hiraṇvatīm ..
astrairanugatastatra suṣvāpa kila yogavit ...28..
1.125.d:
तत्र पूजामुपादाय जगाम स हिरण्वतीम् ॥
अस्त्रैरनुगतस्तत्र सुष्वाप किल योगवित् ॥.28॥
1.125.m: Receiving worship there, he went to Hiraṇvatī; / followed there by his divine weapons, the master of yoga slept.

1.125.s:
evaṃ sa daityapravaro narendra kṛṣṇena cakreṇa purā nirastaḥ ..
ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ kathayāmi tubhyaṃ tanme vadasvāyatalohitākṣa ..29 ..
1.125.d:
एवं स दैत्यप्रवरो नरेन्द्र कृष्णेन चक्रेण पुरा निरस्तः ॥
अतः परं किं कथयामि तुभ्यं तन्मे वदस्वायतलोहिताक्ष ॥29 ॥
1.125.m: In this way, O lord of men, that foremost Daitya was long ago cast down by Kṛṣṇa with his discus. / What further shall I tell you beyond this? Tell me that, O long-and-red-eyed one!

1.126.s:
vajra uvāca ..
yaduktaṃ daityanāthena daityānāṃ kālaneminā ..
pātāladaityaśamanaṃ vapurdevasya cakriṇaḥ .. 1 ..
1.126.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
यदुक्तं दैत्यनाथेन दैत्यानां कालनेमिना ॥
पातालदैत्यशमनं वपुर्देवस्य चक्रिणः ॥ 1 ॥
1.126.m: Vajra said: / That which was spoken by Kālanemi, the lord of the Daityas, to the Daityas— / regarding the form of the god holding the discus, which quelled the Daityas of Pātāla—

1.126.s:
tadahaṃ śrotumicchāmi tatra me saṃśayo mahān ..
caritaṃ tasya devasya bhāvānvetti yathātatham..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
viṣṇunā tu balau baddhe pātālatalamāśritāḥ..
jaghnudaityagaṇā lokānbrāhmaṇāṃśca viśeṣataḥ..3.. .
1.126.d:
तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥
चरितं तस्य देवस्य भावान्वेत्ति यथातथम्॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
विष्णुना तु बलौ बद्धे पातालतलमाश्रिताः॥
जघ्नुदैत्यगणा लोकान्ब्राह्मणांश्च विशेषतः॥3॥ ।
1.126.m:
that I wish to hear; concerning that I have great doubt. / You know the deed of that god in its true nature.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When Bali was bound by Viṣṇu, taking refuge in the depths of Pātāla, / the hordes of Daityas began killing beings, and especially brahmins.

1.126.s:
bhūtale hanyamāne tu yajñe nāśamupāgate ..
kṣutkṣāmastridaśairbrahmā daityahetoḥ pracoditaḥ..4..
1.126.d:
भूतले हन्यमाने तु यज्ञे नाशमुपागते ॥
क्षुत्क्षामस्त्रिदशैर्ब्रह्मा दैत्यहेतोः प्रचोदितः॥4॥
1.126.m: While the surface of the earth was being devastated and sacrifice came to ruin, / Brahmā, emaciated with hunger, was urged by the gods because of the Daityas.

1.126.s:
brahmāpi codayāmāsa devadevaṃ janārdanam..
brahmaṇā codito devaḥ pātālagamanecchayā ..85..
1.126.d:
ब्रह्मापि चोदयामास देवदेवं जनार्दनम्॥
ब्रह्मणा चोदितो देवः पातालगमनेच्छया ॥85॥
1.126.m: Brahmā too urged Janārdana, the god of gods. / Urged by Brahmā, the god, desiring to go to Pātāla,

1.126.s:
cakāra rūpaṃ vārāhaṃ bhinnāñjanacayaprabham ..
śaśāṅkalekhādaṃṣṭrāgraṃ vajraprothakhuraṃ tathā ..6..
1.126.d:
चकार रूपं वाराहं भिन्नाञ्जनचयप्रभम् ॥
शशाङ्कलेखादंष्ट्राग्रं वज्रप्रोथखुरं तथा ॥6॥
1.126.m: assumed the form of a boar, shining like a mass of split collyrium, / having the tip of his tusks like the crescent moon, and with snout and hooves like vajra,

1.126.s:
vajrasaṃhananaṃ bhīmaṃ trailokyakṣobhakārakam ..
pīnavṛttāyataskandhaṃ mahāpīnaśirodharam .. 7 ..
1.126.d:
वज्रसंहननं भीमं त्रैलोक्यक्षोभकारकम् ॥
पीनवृत्तायतस्कन्धं महापीनशिरोधरम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.126.m: with a diamond-hard body, fierce, causing the three worlds to tremble, / with thick, round, broad shoulders and a massive, stout neck,

1.126.s:
vivṛttāsyaṃ mahākāyaṃ bhīmākṣaṃ bhīmanisvanam ..
āvarttiromasaṃghātaṃ tena vigrahamūrjitam .. .. 8 ..
1.126.d:
विवृत्तास्यं महाकायं भीमाक्षं भीमनिस्वनम् ॥
आवर्त्तिरोमसंघातं तेन विग्रहमूर्जितम् ॥ ॥ 8 ॥
1.126.m: with an open mouth, a huge body, fierce eyes, and a terrifying roar, / with dense swirls of bristles—such was the powerful body he assumed.

1.126.s:
sa samudreṇa pātālaṃ praviśya madhusūdanaḥ ..
daityānāṃ darśane tasthau mahābalaparākramaḥ .. 9 ..
1.126.d:
स समुद्रेण पातालं प्रविश्य मधुसूदनः ॥
दैत्यानां दर्शने तस्थौ महाबलपराक्रमः ॥ 9 ॥
1.126.m: Having entered Pātāla through the ocean, that Madhusūdana, / endowed with great strength and prowess, stood in the view of the Daityas.

1.126.s:
pātāle sūkaraṃ dṛṣṭvā prothadāritabhūtalam ..
sumustagarbhakavalaṃ śuṃśukārakṛtānanam .. 1.126.10 ..
1.126.d:
पाताले सूकरं दृष्ट्वा प्रोथदारितभूतलम् ॥
सुमुस्तगर्भकवलं शुंशुकारकृताननम् ॥ 1.126.10 ॥
1.126.m: Seeing the boar in Pātāla, who had torn open the surface of the earth with his snout, / with mouthfuls of bulbs of musta grass in his mouth, making grunting sounds,

1.126.s:
paṅkānuliptasarvāṅgaṃ niryayurdānavāstadā ..
satataṃ mṛgayāśīlā jaghnustañca varāyudhaiḥ .. 11 ..
1.126.d:
पङ्कानुलिप्तसर्वाङ्गं निर्ययुर्दानवास्तदा ॥
सततं मृगयाशीला जघ्नुस्तञ्च वरायुधैः ॥ 11 ॥
1.126.m: with all his limbs smeared with mud, the Dānavas then came forth; / ever devoted to hunting, they struck him with excellent weapons.

1.126.s:
sa hanyamāno daityāstraiḥ pṛṣatairiva parvataḥ ..
skandhakaṇḍūcchalenājau daityādhipaniveśanam .. 12 ..
1.126.d:
स हन्यमानो दैत्यास्त्रैः पृषतैरिव पर्वतः ॥
स्कन्धकण्डूच्छलेनाजौ दैत्याधिपनिवेशनम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.126.m: He, being struck with the weapons of the Daityas as a mountain with raindrops, / on the pretext of scratching his shoulder in battle, [hurled himself against] the dwelling of the Daitya king,

1.126.s:
pātayāmāsa vegena mahādriśikharopamam ..
veśmanaśca nipātena devadevasya māyayā .. 13 ..
1.126.d:
पातयामास वेगेन महाद्रिशिखरोपमम् ॥
वेश्मनश्च निपातेन देवदेवस्य मायया ॥ 13 ॥
1.126.m: and brought it crashing down with speed, like the peak of a great mountain. / And by the collapse of the dwelling through the divine illusion of the god of gods,

1.126.s:
hanyante dānavā ghorāḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
te kṣayāddaityamukhyānāṃ daityamukhyakṣayaṅkarāḥ..14..
1.126.d:
हन्यन्ते दानवा घोराः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
ते क्षयाद्दैत्यमुख्यानां दैत्यमुख्यक्षयङ्कराः॥14॥
1.126.m: dreadful Dānavas were slain by the hundreds and by the thousands. / Those who destroyed the chiefs of the Daityas, through the destruction of those chiefs of the Daityas,

1.126.s:
yathārthakṣayatāṃ jagmuḥ kṣaye raudra upasthite ..
kṣīyamāṇāḥ kṣayairdṛṣṭvā kṣatajotkṣiptamūrdhajān .. 15 ..
1.126.d:
यथार्थक्षयतां जग्मुः क्षये रौद्र उपस्थिते ॥
क्षीयमाणाः क्षयैर्दृष्ट्वा क्षतजोत्क्षिप्तमूर्धजान् ॥ 15 ॥
1.126.m: went to true destruction when fierce destruction arrived. / Wasting away in destruction, seeing those whose hair was tossed up by blood,

1.126.s:
kṣmātalasthānkṣatairgotraiḥ kṣaṇena kṣaṇadācarān ..
pradhānā daityamukhyā ye auraserana balena te ..16..
1.126.d:
क्ष्मातलस्थान्क्षतैर्गोत्रैः क्षणेन क्षणदाचरान् ॥
प्रधाना दैत्यमुख्या ये औरसेरन बलेन ते ॥16॥
1.126.m: those nocturnal wanderers lying on the surface of the earth with their bodies mangled in an instant, / the foremost leaders of the Daityas who [remained], with their inherent strength,

1.126.s:
jagmurvarāyudhairdevaṃ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..
sa hanyamāno daityendraiḥ prothena ditijottamān ..17..
1.126.d:
जग्मुर्वरायुधैर्देवं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
स हन्यमानो दैत्येन्द्रैः प्रोथेन दितिजोत्तमान् ॥17॥
1.126.m: attacked the god by the hundreds and thousands with excellent weapons. / Being struck by the chiefs of the Daityas, with his snout he [tore apart] the foremost sons of Diti,

1.126.s:
vidārayāmāsa raṇe daṃṣṭrāgreṇa tathāparān ..
evaṃ varāheṇa raṇe hatāndṛṣṭvā dite sutān .. 18 ..
1.126.d:
विदारयामास रणे दंष्ट्राग्रेण तथापरान् ॥
एवं वराहेण रणे हतान्दृष्ट्वा दिते सुतान् ॥ 18 ॥
1.126.m: and rent others in battle with the tip of his tusks. / Seeing the sons of Diti thus slain in battle by the boar,

1.126.s:
hariṃ vijñātavāndevaṃ prahrādo daityasattamaḥ ..
sa praṇamya hariṃ devaṃ tuṣṭāva paravīrahā .. 19 ..
1.126.d:
हरिं विज्ञातवान्देवं प्रह्रादो दैत्यसत्तमः ॥
स प्रणम्य हरिं देवं तुष्टाव परवीरहा ॥ 19 ॥
1.126.m: Prahrāda, the best of the Daityas, recognized the god as Hari. / Bowing to the god Hari, that slayer of enemy heroes praised him.

1.126.s:
taṃ jagāda mahātejā devadevo janārdanaḥ ..
anugrāhyo'si me daitya bhakto'si satataṃ yataḥ .. 1.126.20..
1.126.d:
तं जगाद महातेजा देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
अनुग्राह्योऽसि मे दैत्य भक्तोऽसि सततं यतः ॥ 1.126.20॥
1.126.m: To him spoke Janārdana, the god of gods of great splendor: / "You are worthy of my grace, O Daitya, because you are ever devoted to me.

1.126.s:
tavājñālaṅghakā ghorā prāyeṇa nihatā mayā ..
tavājñākāriṇo daityā na me vadhyā diteḥ sutāḥ .. 21 ..
1.126.d:
तवाज्ञालङ्घका घोरा प्रायेण निहता मया ॥
तवाज्ञाकारिणो दैत्या न मे वध्या दितेः सुताः ॥ 21 ॥
1.126.m: The terrifying transgressors of your command have mostly been slain by me; / the Daityas who obey your command, the sons of Diti, are not to be slain by me.

1.126.s:
śāsanaṃ pālaya mahyaṃ pātāle tvaṃ sukhī bhava ..
mārge sthāpaya daityām̐stvaṃ tvadājñāparibṛṃhitān ..22..
1.126.d:
शासनं पालय मह्यं पाताले त्वं सुखी भव ॥
मार्गे स्थापय दैत्याम्̐स्त्वं त्वदाज्ञापरिबृंहितान् ॥22॥
1.126.m: Obey my command: be happy in Pātāla; / establish on the proper path the Daityas who are strengthened by your authority.

1.126.s:
ābhūtasaṃplavaṃ daitya jīvaṃ tvaṃ na vimokṣyase ..
dharmiṣṭhānāṃ ca daityānāṃ sadā rājā bhaviṣyasi .. 23 ..
1.126.d:
आभूतसंप्लवं दैत्य जीवं त्वं न विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
धर्मिष्ठानां च दैत्यानां सदा राजा भविष्यसि ॥ 23 ॥
1.126.m: Until the dissolution of all beings, O Daitya, you shall not forfeit life, / and you shall forever be the king of the righteous Daityas.

1.126.s:
madbhaktyā parayā vatsa putrastava virocanaḥ ..
mārgacyuto'pi na hataḥ kalpāyuśca tathā kṛtaḥ .. 24 ..
1.126.d:
मद्भक्त्या परया वत्स पुत्रस्तव विरोचनः ॥
मार्गच्युतोऽपि न हतः कल्पायुश्च तथा कृतः ॥ 24 ॥
1.126.m: Through supreme devotion to me, dear child, your son Virocana, / though strayed from the path, was not slain, and his lifespan was made to last an aeon.

1.126.s:
balirvairocanaścaiva mayā baddhaḥ kṛte tava ..
kariṣyati sa śakratvaṃ prāpte sāvarṇikentare .. 25 ..
1.126.d:
बलिर्वैरोचनश्चैव मया बद्धः कृते तव ॥
करिष्यति स शक्रत्वं प्राप्ते सावर्णिकेन्तरे ॥ 25 ॥
1.126.m: And Bali, the son of Virocana, was bound by me for your sake; / he will perform the role of Śakra when the Sāvarṇika interval arrives.

1.126.s:
bāṇaṃ ca tanayaṃ tasya mama vipriyakārakam ..
tvatkṛte na haniṣyāmi tasya cchetsyāmi dordrumān .. 26 ..
1.126.d:
बाणं च तनयं तस्य मम विप्रियकारकम् ॥
त्वत्कृते न हनिष्यामि तस्य च्छेत्स्यामि दोर्द्रुमान् ॥ 26 ॥
1.126.m: And his son Bāṇa, though he causes displeasure to me, / I will not kill for your sake; I will [only] sever the tree of his arms.

1.126.s:
chinnabāhurmayā yuddhe harasyānucaro balī ..
mahākāla iti khyāto kalpasthāyī bhaviṣyati .. 27 ..
1.126.d:
छिन्नबाहुर्मया युद्धे हरस्यानुचरो बली ॥
महाकाल इति ख्यातो कल्पस्थायी भविष्यति ॥ 27 ॥
1.126.m: With his arms severed by me in battle, that mighty one will become an attendant of Hara, / renowned as Mahākāla, enduring for an aeon.

1.126.s:
ekamekaṃ tu daityendra santāne satataṃ tava ..
nāhaṃ vadhiṣye dharmajña tvatkṛte vyetu te bhayam .. 28 ..
1.126.d:
एकमेकं तु दैत्येन्द्र सन्ताने सततं तव ॥
नाहं वधिष्ये धर्मज्ञ त्वत्कृते व्येतु ते भयम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.126.m: In your lineage, O lord of Daityas, one by one, / I shall never kill, O knower of dharma; for your sake let your fear depart.

1.126.s:
bhavānbhaktastathā mahyaṃ bhakteṣvapi tathā mama ..
nāstyadeyaṃ mahābhāga tasmāttvaṃ gaccha nirvṛttaḥ .. 29 ..
1.126.d:
भवान्भक्तस्तथा मह्यं भक्तेष्वपि तथा मम ॥
नास्त्यदेयं महाभाग तस्मात्त्वं गच्छ निर्वृत्तः ॥ 29 ॥
1.126.m: You are devoted to me in that manner, and likewise among my devotees; / there is nothing that cannot be granted [to you], O fortunate one; therefore go, content,

1.126.s:
hataśeṣānupādāya daityānsatpathamāśritān ..
etāvaduktā prahrādaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata ..1.126.30 ..
1.126.d:
हतशेषानुपादाय दैत्यान्सत्पथमाश्रितान् ॥
एतावदुक्ता प्रह्रादं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥1.126.30 ॥
1.126.m: taking those remaining from the slaughter, the Daityas who have taken to the good path." / Having said this much to Prahrāda, he disappeared right there.

1.126.s:
etadvārāhacaritaṃ tava rājasiṃha proktaṃ mayā sakalakalmaṣanāśakāri ..
udavṛttadaityaśamanasya ṛṣistutasya kaṇḍūvinodanahatāsurapuṅgavasya .. 31 ..
1.126.d:
एतद्वाराहचरितं तव राजसिंह प्रोक्तं मया सकलकल्मषनाशकारि ॥
उदवृत्तदैत्यशमनस्य ऋषिस्तुतस्य कण्डूविनोदनहतासुरपुङ्गवस्य ॥ 31 ॥
1.126.m: This deed of the Boar has been told to you, O lion among kings, by me, destroying all defilements— / of him who pacified the rebellious Daityas, was praised by sages, and struck down the foremost Asura to relieve an itching.

1.127.s:
vajra uvāca ..
ditirvinaṣṭaputrā ca yaccakāra dvijottama ..
tanmamācakṣva saṃkṣepāttatra me saṃśayo mahān .. 1 ..
1.127.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
दितिर्विनष्टपुत्रा च यच्चकार द्विजोत्तम ॥
तन्ममाचक्ष्व संक्षेपात्तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥ 1 ॥
1.127.m: Vajra said: / And what Diti did when her sons were destroyed, O best of the twice-born, / tell me that in brief; concerning that I have great doubt.

1.127.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ditirvinaṣṭaputrā ca tapasā mahatā nṛpa ..
ārādhayāmāsa tadā bhartāraṃ kaśyapaṃ munim ..2 ..
1.127.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
दितिर्विनष्टपुत्रा च तपसा महता नृप ॥
आराधयामास तदा भर्तारं कश्यपं मुनिम् ॥2 ॥
1.127.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / And Diti, when her sons were destroyed, with great asceticism, O king, / then propitiated her husband, the sage Kaśyapa.

1.127.s:
ārādhitaḥ sutapasā cchandayāmāsa bhāminīm ..
vareṇa ca vacaḥ kāle putravyasanakarṣitām .. 3 ..
1.127.d:
आराधितः सुतपसा च्छन्दयामास भामिनीम् ॥
वरेण च वचः काले पुत्रव्यसनकर्षिताम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.127.m: Propitiated by her great asceticism, in due time he gratified the passionate woman / afflicted with grief for her sons with a boon and words.

1.127.s:
kaśyapa uvāca ..
varaṃ varaya suśroṇi varado'hamupasthitaḥ ..
evamuktā varaṃ vavre devī putravinākṛtā .. 4 ..
1.127.d:
कश्यप उवाच ॥
वरं वरय सुश्रोणि वरदोऽहमुपस्थितः ॥
एवमुक्ता वरं वव्रे देवी पुत्रविनाकृता ॥ 4 ॥
1.127.m: Kaśyapa said: / Choose a boon, O fair-hipped woman; as a giver of boons I have come. / Addressed thus, the goddess bereft of her sons chose a boon.

1.127.s:
ditiruvāca ..
śakrahantāramicchāmi putraṃ brahmanyaśasvinam ..
yadi tuṣṭo'si me brahmaṃstaṃ prayaccha sutaṃ mama .. 5 ..
1.127.d:
दितिरुवाच ॥
शक्रहन्तारमिच्छामि पुत्रं ब्रह्मन्यशस्विनम् ॥
यदि तुष्टोऽसि मे ब्रह्मंस्तं प्रयच्छ सुतं मम ॥ 5 ॥
1.127.m: Diti said: / I desire a son who will slay Śakra, devoted to sacred lore, and renowned. / If you are pleased with me, O holy one, grant me that son.

1.127.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktastadā bhartā nātiprīto'bravīdvaram ..
evaṃ te bhavitā bhadre śuci tvaṃ cedbhaviṣyasi .. 6 ..
1.127.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा भर्ता नातिप्रीतोऽब्रवीद्वरम् ॥
एवं ते भविता भद्रे शुचि त्वं चेद्भविष्यसि ॥ 6 ॥
1.127.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Addressed thus, her husband then, not very pleased, spoke the boon: / 'So it will be for you, fair lady, if you remain pure

1.127.s:
pūrṇavarṣasahasraṃ ca nānyathā tadbhaviṣyati ..
evamuktvā tayā sārdhamuvāsa rajanīṃ dvijaḥ ..7..
1.127.d:
पूर्णवर्षसहस्रं च नान्यथा तद्भविष्यति ॥
एवमुक्त्वा तया सार्धमुवास रजनीं द्विजः ॥7॥
1.127.m: for a full thousand years; and it will not be otherwise.' / Having spoken thus, the twice-born dwelt with her for the night.

1.127.s:
tato jagāma dharmātmā tapase dṛḍhaniścayaḥ ..
ātasthau niyamaṃ devī sagarbhā ca ditistadā ..
niyamasthāṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śakro vacanamabravīt.. 8 ..
1.127.d:
ततो जगाम धर्मात्मा तपसे दृढनिश्चयः ॥
आतस्थौ नियमं देवी सगर्भा च दितिस्तदा ॥
नियमस्थां तु तां दृष्ट्वा शक्रो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ 8 ॥
1.127.m: Then, resolute in purpose, the righteous one went away to practice asceticism. / And the goddess Diti, being pregnant, then undertook the observance. / But seeing her engaged in the observance, Śakra spoke these words:

1.127.s:
śakra uvāca ..
ahaṃ devi kariṣyāmi tava śuśrūṣaṇaṃ sadā ..
sthitāyā niyame ghore tadanujñātumarhasi .. 9..
1.127.d:
शक्र उवाच ॥
अहं देवि करिष्यामि तव शुश्रूषणं सदा ॥
स्थिताया नियमे घोरे तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ॥ 9॥
1.127.m: Śakra said: / 'O goddess, I will always render service to you / while you remain in this severe observance; you should permit that.'

1.127.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bāḍhamastvityathoktastu tayā devaḥ purandaraḥ ..
tatrovāsa cchalānveṣī śuśrūṣurmātaraṃ sadā .. 1.127.10 ..
1.127.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
बाढमस्त्वित्यथोक्तस्तु तया देवः पुरन्दरः ॥
तत्रोवास च्छलान्वेषी शुश्रूषुर्मातरं सदा ॥ 1.127.10 ॥
1.127.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Addressed by her with 'So be it,' the god Purandara / dwelt there, seeking a flaw, ever desiring to serve his mother.

1.127.s:
tadābdaśeṣe kāle ca divā suptā'ditirnṛpa ..
madhyāhnasamaye rājanpādayoḥ kṛtamūrdhajā .. 11 ..
1.127.d:
तदाब्दशेषे काले च दिवा सुप्ताऽदितिर्नृप ॥
मध्याह्नसमये राजन्पादयोः कृतमूर्धजा ॥ 11 ॥
1.127.m: Then, when the remainder of the years was [almost done], Diti slept by day, O king, / at midday, O king, having placed her hair at her feet.

1.127.s:
tasyāḥ saṃprāpya tacchidraṃ vajrī parapurañjayaḥ ..
viveśa garbhamārgeṇa vivṛtena nareśvara .. 12 ..
1.127.d:
तस्याः संप्राप्य तच्छिद्रं वज्री परपुरञ्जयः ॥
विवेश गर्भमार्गेण विवृतेन नरेश्वर ॥ 12 ॥
1.127.m: Finding that flaw in her, the wielder of the thunderbolt, conqueror of enemies' citadels, / entered by the open passage of the womb, O lord of men.

1.127.s:
saṃpraviśyaiva taṃ garbhaṃ vajreṇa śataparvaṇā ..
kṛtavānsaptadhā vajrī bhāgaṃbhāgaṃ tataḥ punaḥ .. 13 ..
1.127.d:
संप्रविश्यैव तं गर्भं वज्रेण शतपर्वणा ॥
कृतवान्सप्तधा वज्री भागंभागं ततः पुनः ॥ 13 ॥
1.127.m: Entering that womb, with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt / the wielder of the thunderbolt divided it into seven parts, and then again each part.

1.127.s:
ekaikaṃ saptadhā cakre garbho'pi prārudattadā ..
mā rudasveti taṃ vajrī prāha kārye svake sthitaḥ .. 14 ..
1.127.d:
एकैकं सप्तधा चक्रे गर्भोऽपि प्रारुदत्तदा ॥
मा रुदस्वेति तं वज्री प्राह कार्ये स्वके स्थितः ॥ 14 ॥
1.127.m: He made each one into seven, and the embryo then began to weep. / 'Do not weep!' the wielder of the thunderbolt said to it, intent upon his task.

1.127.s:
etasminneva kāle ca daityendrajananī tadā ..
vibuddhā vārayāmāsa śakraṃ daśaśatekṣaṇam .. 15 ..
1.127.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले च दैत्येन्द्रजननी तदा ॥
विबुद्धा वारयामास शक्रं दशशतेक्षणम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.127.m: At that very time, the mother of the lords of the Daityas then / awoke and restrained Śakra, the thousand-eyed.

1.127.s:
vajragarbhāñjaliḥ śakro māturvacanayantritaḥ ..
niścakrāmodarāttasyāḥ saha bālairmahātmabhiḥ .. 16 ..
1.127.d:
वज्रगर्भाञ्जलिः शक्रो मातुर्वचनयन्त्रितः ॥
निश्चक्रामोदरात्तस्याः सह बालैर्महात्मभिः ॥ 16 ॥
1.127.m: With thunderbolt in his hands joined in reverence, restrained by his mother's words, / Śakra came out of her womb together with the noble children.

1.127.s:
taṃ jagāda ditiḥ śakraṃ prāñjaliṃ purataḥ sthitam ..
na te śakrāparādho'sti mama garbhanikṛntane .. 17 ..
1.127.d:
तं जगाद दितिः शक्रं प्राञ्जलिं पुरतः स्थितम् ॥
न ते शक्रापराधोऽस्ति मम गर्भनिकृन्तने ॥ 17 ॥
1.127.m: Diti spoke to Śakra, who stood before her with joined hands: / 'There is no fault in you, Śakra, in the cutting up of my embryo.

1.127.s:
sarvopāyairniyantavyaḥ śatrurnayavidā sadā ..
mamāparādhādgarbho'yaṃ tvayādya bahudhā kṛtaḥ .. 18 ..
1.127.d:
सर्वोपायैर्नियन्तव्यः शत्रुर्नयविदा सदा ॥
ममापराधाद्गर्भोऽयं त्वयाद्य बहुधा कृतः ॥ 18 ॥
1.127.m: An enemy is always to be suppressed by all means by one who knows policy. / Because of my own fault, this embryo has today been made into many by you.

1.127.s:
bhavantu maruto nāma sarve devāḥ pṛthakpṛthak..
mā rudadhvamiti proktā yataḥ śakra tvayā sutāḥ ..19..
1.127.d:
भवन्तु मरुतो नाम सर्वे देवाः पृथक्पृथक्॥
मा रुदध्वमिति प्रोक्ता यतः शक्र त्वया सुताः ॥19॥
1.127.m: Let all of them be gods, separately named the Maruts, / because, O Śakra, your brothers were told by you, "Do not weep!"'

1.127.s:
tataśca maruto nāma bhaviṣyanti jagattraye ..
tvatsahāyā bhaviṣyanti tvadājñāvaśavartinaḥ .. 1.127.20 ..
1.127.d:
ततश्च मरुतो नाम भविष्यन्ति जगत्त्रये ॥
त्वत्सहाया भविष्यन्ति त्वदाज्ञावशवर्तिनः ॥ 1.127.20 ॥
1.127.m: [She said:] 'And therefore they will be named Maruts in the three worlds. / They will be your helpers, obedient to your command.

1.127.s:
na caitebhyo bhayaṃ kiñcitkadācitte bhaviṣyati ..
eṣāṃ nāmavibhāgām̐stu sthānāni ca tathā kuru .. 21 ..
1.127.d:
न चैतेभ्यो भयं किञ्चित्कदाचित्ते भविष्यति ॥
एषां नामविभागाम्̐स्तु स्थानानि च तथा कुरु ॥ 21 ॥
1.127.m: And there will never be any fear for you from them. / Make for them their allotment of names and also their stations.'

1.127.s:
ekajyotiśca dvirjyotistricaturjyotireva ca ..
ekaśakro dviśakraśca triśakraśca mahābalaḥ .. 22 ..
1.127.d:
एकज्योतिश्च द्विर्ज्योतिस्त्रिचतुर्ज्योतिरेव च ॥
एकशक्रो द्विशक्रश्च त्रिशक्रश्च महाबलः ॥ 22 ॥
1.127.m: Ekajyotis, Dvirjyotis, and Trijyotis, Caturjyotis, / Ekaśakra, Dviśakra, and Triśakra of great strength:

1.127.s:
prathame pavana skandhe gaṇo'yaṃ surathaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
indraśca gavyo dṛśyaśca itaḥ pratiśirāstathā .. 23 ..
1.127.d:
प्रथमे पवन स्कन्धे गणोऽयं सुरथः स्मृतः ॥
इन्द्रश्च गव्यो दृश्यश्च इतः प्रतिशिरास्तथा ॥ 23 ॥
1.127.m: this troop, Suratha by name, is traditionally held to be in the first level of the wind. / Indra, Gavya, Dṛśya, and here Pratiśiras,

1.127.s:
mitaśca sammitaścaiva amitaśca mahābalaḥ ..
dvitīye pavana skandhe gaṇo nāma praghoṣaṇaḥ ..24..
1.127.d:
मितश्च सम्मितश्चैव अमितश्च महाबलः ॥
द्वितीये पवन स्कन्धे गणो नाम प्रघोषणः ॥24॥
1.127.m: Mita, Sammita, and Amita of great strength: / in the second level of the wind is the troop named Praghoṣaṇa.

1.127.s:
ṛtajitsatyajiccaiva suṣeṇaḥ senajittathā ..
atimitro nāmitraśca pṛrumitro'parājitaḥ .. 25 ..
1.127.d:
ऋतजित्सत्यजिच्चैव सुषेणः सेनजित्तथा ॥
अतिमित्रो नामित्रश्च पृरुमित्रोऽपराजितः ॥ 25 ॥
1.127.m: Ṛtajit, Satyajit, Suṣeṇa, and Senajit, / Atimitra, Nāmitra, and Pṛrumitra, Aparājita:

1.127.s:
tṛtīye pavanaskandhe gaṇaḥ santāpanaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
ṛteśca ṛtavāndhātā vidhātā dharaṇo dhruvaḥ .. 26 ..
1.127.d:
तृतीये पवनस्कन्धे गणः सन्तापनः स्मृतः ॥
ऋतेश्च ऋतवान्धाता विधाता धरणो ध्रुवः ॥ 26 ॥
1.127.m: in the third level of the wind the troop is traditionally known as Santāpana. / Ṛte, Ṛtavat, Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Dharaṇa, Dhruva,

1.127.s:
vidhāraṇaḥ caturthastu gṛhamedho gaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
idṛkṣaśca sadṛkṣaśca etādṛgamṛtāśanaḥ .. 27 ..
1.127.d:
विधारणः चतुर्थस्तु गृहमेधो गणः स्मृतः ॥
इदृक्षश्च सदृक्षश्च एतादृगमृताशनः ॥ 27 ॥
