1.127.m: and Vidhāraṇa—the fourth troop is known as Gṛhamedha. / Īdṛkṣa, Sadṛkṣa, Etādṛś, Amṛtāśana,

1.127.s:
krītanaḥ prasadṛkṣaśca sarabhaśca mahāyaśāḥ ..
gṛhe ca roṣaṇā nāma vāyuskandhe ca pañcame .. 28 ..
1.127.d:
क्रीतनः प्रसदृक्षश्च सरभश्च महायशाः ॥
गृहे च रोषणा नाम वायुस्कन्धे च पञ्चमे ॥ 28 ॥
1.127.m: Krītana, Prasadṛkṣa, and Sarabha of great renown: / in the house and the fifth level of the wind is the troop named Roṣaṇā.

1.127.s:
dhartā durgadhva nirbhīmo hyabhiyuktiḥ kṛpā sahaḥ ..
ṣaṣṭhe tu pavanaskandhe sāsvī nāma gaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..29 ..
1.127.d:
धर्ता दुर्गध्व निर्भीमो ह्यभियुक्तिः कृपा सहः ॥
षष्ठे तु पवनस्कन्धे सास्वी नाम गणः स्मृतः ॥29 ॥
1.127.m: Dhartṛ, Durgadhva, Nirbhīma, Abhiyukti, Kṛpā, Saha: / in the sixth level of the wind, the troop is known as Sāsvī.

1.127.s:
dyutirvapuranādṛśyo kāmo jayo virāṭ ..
prejeṣaṇo gaṇo nāma vāyuskandhe ca saptame .. 1.127.30 ..
1.127.d:
द्युतिर्वपुरनादृश्यो कामो जयो विराट् ॥
प्रेजेषणो गणो नाम वायुस्कन्धे च सप्तमे ॥ 1.127.30 ॥
1.127.m: Dyuti, Vapus, Anādṛśya, Kāma, Jaya, Virāj, / Prejeṣaṇa is the name of the troop in the seventh level of the wind.

1.127.s:
eṣāṃ nāmavibhāgantu dattvā sthānāni cācyutaḥ ..
jagāma svagṛhaṃ prītyā ditiśca svagṛhaṃ yayau .. 31 ..
1.127.d:
एषां नामविभागन्तु दत्त्वा स्थानानि चाच्युतः ॥
जगाम स्वगृहं प्रीत्या दितिश्च स्वगृहं ययौ ॥ 31 ॥
1.127.m: Having granted the division of these names and their stations, the infallible one / went joyfully to his own home, and Diti went to her own home.

1.127.s:
etattavoktaṃ marutāṃ nṛvīra janmottamaṃ pāpabhayāpahāri ..
yasmiñśrutenaiva janasya loke bhavantu vṛttyā na bhaviṣyatīha .. 32 ..
1.127.d:
एतत्तवोक्तं मरुतां नृवीर जन्मोत्तमं पापभयापहारि ॥
यस्मिञ्श्रुतेनैव जनस्य लोके भवन्तु वृत्त्या न भविष्यतीह ॥ 32 ॥
1.127.m: This supreme birth of the Maruts, which removes sin and fear, has been told to you, O hero among men; / by merely hearing it, people in the world will not suffer a decline of their livelihood here.

1.128.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
janayāmāsa rājendra danurdānavapuṅgavān ..
vipracittimukhānvīrāndaityapakṣamupāśritān .. 1 ..
1.128.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
जनयामास राजेन्द्र दनुर्दानवपुङ्गवान् ॥
विप्रचित्तिमुखान्वीरान्दैत्यपक्षमुपाश्रितान् ॥ 1 ॥
1.128.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / O lord of kings, Danu brought forth foremost Dānavas, / heroic ones led by Vipracitti, who took the side of the Daityas.

1.128.s:
kālaṃ ca janayāmāsa kālakeyānsudāruṇān ..
daityapakṣāśritānkrūrānviruddhāndevatāgaṇe .. 2 ..
1.128.d:
कालं च जनयामास कालकेयान्सुदारुणान् ॥
दैत्यपक्षाश्रितान्क्रूरान्विरुद्धान्देवतागणे ॥ 2 ॥
1.128.m: And Kālā brought forth the exceedingly terrible Kālakeyas, / cruel ones who took the side of the Daityas, hostile to the host of deities.

1.128.s:
danāyuṣāyāḥ putrastu vṛtro nāma mahāsuraḥ ..
viruddhastu sadā devairdaityapakṣamupāśritaḥ .. 3 ..
1.128.d:
दनायुषायाः पुत्रस्तु वृत्रो नाम महासुरः ॥
विरुद्धस्तु सदा देवैर्दैत्यपक्षमुपाश्रितः ॥ 3 ॥
1.128.m: And the son of Danāyuṣ was the great Asura named Vṛtra, / always opposed to the gods, who took the side of the Daityas.

1.128.s:
siṃhikā janayāmāsa saiṃhikeyānmahāsurān ..
rāhusālvamukhānvīrānbahūnamitatejasaḥ .. 4 ..
1.128.d:
सिंहिका जनयामास सैंहिकेयान्महासुरान् ॥
राहुसाल्वमुखान्वीरान्बहूनमिततेजसः ॥ 4 ॥
1.128.m: Siṃhikā brought forth the Saiṃhikeyas, great Asuras, / many heroes of immeasurable splendour, headed by Rāhu and Sālva.

1.128.s:
gandharvāpsaraso divyā munayastānnivodha me ..
citrasenograsenau ca ūrṇāyuranaghastathā .. 5 ..
1.128.d:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसो दिव्या मुनयस्तान्निवोध मे ॥
चित्रसेनोग्रसेनौ च ऊर्णायुरनघस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
1.128.m: Learn from me the divine Gandharvas and Apsarases [born of] Muni: / Citrasena and Ugrasena, Ūrṇāyu, and Anagha,

1.128.s:
dhṛtarāṣṭraśca gopaśca sūryavarcāstathaiva ca ..
yugapastṛṇapaḥ pārṣṇirardhaścitrarathastathā .. 6 ..
1.128.d:
धृतराष्ट्रश्च गोपश्च सूर्यवर्चास्तथैव च ॥
युगपस्तृणपः पार्ष्णिरर्धश्चित्ररथस्तथा ॥ 6 ॥
1.128.m: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gopa, and Sūryavarcas, / Yugapa, Tṛṇapa, Pārṣṇi, Ardha, and Citraratha,

1.128.s:
kaliḥ śāliśirāścaiva parjanyo nāradastathā ..
teṣāṃ caiva yavīyasyo divyāścāpsarasaḥ śubhāḥ .. 7 ..
1.128.d:
कलिः शालिशिराश्चैव पर्जन्यो नारदस्तथा ॥
तेषां चैव यवीयस्यो दिव्याश्चाप्सरसः शुभाः ॥ 7 ॥
1.128.m: Kali, Śāliśiras, Parjanya, and Nārada; / and their younger sisters were the divine, auspicious Apsarases.

1.128.s:
anūcānānavadyā ca priyamukhyā gaṇeśvarī ..
miśrakeśī tathā cāpi parṇāśā puñjikasthalā .. 8 ..
1.128.d:
अनूचानानवद्या च प्रियमुख्या गणेश्वरी ॥
मिश्रकेशी तथा चापि पर्णाशा पुञ्जिकस्थला ॥ 8 ॥
1.128.m: Anūcānā, Anavadyā, Priyamukhyā, Gaṇeśvarī, / Miśrakeśī, Parṇāśā, and Puñjikasthalā;

1.128.s:
marīciḥ śucikā caiva vidyutparṇī tilottamā ..
āṭṭikā lakṣmaṇā kṣemā devī rambhā manoramā .. 9 ..
1.128.d:
मरीचिः शुचिका चैव विद्युत्पर्णी तिलोत्तमा ॥
आट्टिका लक्ष्मणा क्षेमा देवी रम्भा मनोरमा ॥ 9 ॥
1.128.m: Marīci, Śucikā, Vidyutparṇī, Tilottamā, / Āṭṭikā, Lakṣmaṇā, Kṣemā, the goddess Rambhā, Manoramā;

1.128.s:
āsitā ca subāhuśca suvratā suvapustathā ..
puṇḍarīkā sugandhā ca sudārā surasā tathā .. 1.128.10 ..
1.128.d:
आसिता च सुबाहुश्च सुव्रता सुवपुस्तथा ॥
पुण्डरीका सुगन्धा च सुदारा सुरसा तथा ॥ 1.128.10 ॥
1.128.m: Asitā, Subāhu, Suvratā, and Suvapus, / Puṇḍarīkā, Sugandhā, Sudārā, and Surasā;

1.128.s:
hemā śaradvatī caiva prasūtā kamalā ca yā ..
sumukhī haṃsamārgā ca saurīyāpsarasaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 11 ..
1.128.d:
हेमा शरद्वती चैव प्रसूता कमला च या ॥
सुमुखी हंसमार्गा च सौरीयाप्सरसः स्मृताः ॥ 11 ॥
1.128.m: Hemā, Śaradvatī, Prasūtā, and Kamalā, / Sumukhī, and Haṃsamārgā—these are remembered as the apsarases born of Saurī.

1.128.s:
kadrūśca janayāmāsa nāgāstīvraparākramān ..
yeṣāṃ śeṣaḥ pradhānastu viṣṇurnāgavapurdharaḥ .. 12 ..
1.128.d:
कद्रूश्च जनयामास नागास्तीव्रपराक्रमान् ॥
येषां शेषः प्रधानस्तु विष्णुर्नागवपुर्धरः ॥ 12 ॥
1.128.m: And Kadrū gave birth to nāgas of fierce prowess, / among whom the foremost is Śeṣa, who is Viṣṇu bearing the body of a serpent,

1.128.s:
yeneyaṃ dhāryate bhūmiḥ saśailavanakānanā ..
āheyī vāsudevasya pūrvaṃ mṛrtirmayeritā .. 13 ..
1.128.d:
येनेयं धार्यते भूमिः सशैलवनकानना ॥
आहेयी वासुदेवस्य पूर्वं मृर्तिर्मयेरिता ॥ 13 ॥
1.128.m: by whom this earth, with its mountains, forests, and woods, is upheld. / The serpentine form of Vāsudeva was previously described by me,

1.128.s:
ananta iti vikhyātā mahākalpavināśinī ..
mahākalpe mahāsattve svayaṃ bhavati sadā .. 14 ..
1.128.d:
अनन्त इति विख्याता महाकल्पविनाशिनी ॥
महाकल्पे महासत्त्वे स्वयं भवति सदा ॥ 14 ॥
1.128.m: celebrated as Ananta, the destroyer of the great aeon; / in the great aeon, possessing great being, he ever exists by himself.

1.128.s:
tasyāṃśena samutpannaḥ śeṣo hi dharaṇīdharaḥ ..
tasyānujāṃste nāgendrānprādhānyena vadāmyaham .. 15 ..
1.128.d:
तस्यांशेन समुत्पन्नः शेषो हि धरणीधरः ॥
तस्यानुजांस्ते नागेन्द्रान्प्राधान्येन वदाम्यहम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.128.m: Śeṣa, the bearer of the earth, was born from a portion of him. / I shall tell you of his younger brothers, the lords of serpents, according to their prominence:

1.128.s:
vāsukistakṣakaścaiva ailāpatro dhanañjayaḥ ..
airāvato mahāpadmaḥ kambalāśvatarāvubhau .. 16 ..
1.128.d:
वासुकिस्तक्षकश्चैव ऐलापत्रो धनञ्जयः ॥
ऐरावतो महापद्मः कम्बलाश्वतरावुभौ ॥ 16 ॥
1.128.m: Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Elāpatra, Dhanañjaya, / Airāvata, Mahāpadma, and both Kambala and Aśvatara,

1.128.s:
śaṅkhapadmau mahāpadmo dhṛtarāṣṭrabalāhakau ..
nīlāśvaḥ puṣpadantaśca sumukho durmukhastathā .. 17 ..
1.128.d:
शङ्खपद्मौ महापद्मो धृतराष्ट्रबलाहकौ ॥
नीलाश्वः पुष्पदन्तश्च सुमुखो दुर्मुखस्तथा ॥ 17 ॥
1.128.m: Śaṅkha and Padma, Mahāpadma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Balāhaka, / Nīlāśva, Puṣpadanta, Sumukha, and Durmukha,

1.128.s:
nahuṣaḥ kararomā ca kuruśca kulikastathā ..
krodhaśca janayāmāsa daśa kanyā narādhipa .. 18 ..
1.128.d:
नहुषः कररोमा च कुरुश्च कुलिकस्तथा ॥
क्रोधश्च जनयामास दश कन्या नराधिप ॥ 18 ॥
1.128.m: Nahuṣa, Kararomā, Kuru, and Kulika. / And Krodhā gave birth to ten daughters, O king;

1.128.s:
pulahāya ca tā dattāḥ kaśyapena mahātmanā ..
mṛgā ca mṛgamandā ca haribhadrā manoharā .. 19 ..
1.128.d:
पुलहाय च ता दत्ताः कश्यपेन महात्मना ॥
मृगा च मृगमन्दा च हरिभद्रा मनोहरा ॥ 19 ॥
1.128.m: and they were given to Pulaha by the high-souled Kaśyapa: / Mṛgā, Mṛgamandā, Haribhadrā, Manoharā,

1.128.s:
bhūtā ca kaśipā daṃṣṭrā sarasā surasā tathā ..
irā caiva tṛṇaṃ sarvaṃ janayāmāsa bhāminī .. 1.128.20 ..
1.128.d:
भूता च कशिपा दंष्ट्रा सरसा सुरसा तथा ॥
इरा चैव तृणं सर्वं जनयामास भामिनी ॥ 1.128.20 ॥
1.128.m: Bhūtā, Kaśipā, Daṃṣṭrā, Sarasā, and Surasā. / And passionate Irā gave birth to all the grasses

1.128.s:
pañcaprakāraṃ dharmajña taṃ me nigadataḥ śṛṇu ..
vṛkṣagulmalatā valyastvaksāratṛṇajātayaḥ .. 21 ..
1.128.d:
पञ्चप्रकारं धर्मज्ञ तं मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
वृक्षगुल्मलता वल्यस्त्वक्सारतृणजातयः ॥ 21 ॥
1.128.m: of five kinds, O knower of dharma; hear that from me as I speak: / trees, shrubs, climbers, creepers, and species of grass with reed-like stalks.

1.128.s:
antaḥsaṃjñā bhavanyetā ghoreṇa tamasā vṛtāḥ ..
eteṣāmabhimāninyo devatā yadunandana .. 22 ..
1.128.d:
अन्तःसंज्ञा भवन्येता घोरेण तमसा वृताः ॥
एतेषामभिमानिन्यो देवता यदुनन्दन ॥ 22 ॥
1.128.m: Possessed of inner consciousness, these exist enveloped by terrible darkness. / The deities presiding over them, O joy of the Yadus,

1.128.s:
janayāmāsa dharmajña irā dākṣāyaṇī śubhā ..
prādhā prasūtāpsarasastāsāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu .. 23 ..
1.128.d:
जनयामास धर्मज्ञ इरा दाक्षायणी शुभा ॥
प्राधा प्रसूताप्सरसस्तासां नामानि मे शृणु ॥ 23 ॥
1.128.m: auspicious Irā, daughter of Dakṣa, brought forth, O knower of dharma. / Prādhā brought forth apsarases; hear their names from me:

1.128.s:
anavadyā anūkā ca sūnūkā karuṇapriyā ..
manūnā subhagā caiva sahajanyā ca menakā .. 24 ..
1.128.d:
अनवद्या अनूका च सूनूका करुणप्रिया ॥
मनूना सुभगा चैव सहजन्या च मेनका ॥ 24 ॥
1.128.m: Anavadyā, Anūkā, Sūnūkā, Karuṇapriyā, / Manūnā, Subhagā, Sahajanyā, and Menakā,

1.128.s:
ghṛtasthūlā ghṛtācī ca viṣūcī pūrvacityapi ..
pramlocītyapsarāścaiva nimlocantī tathaiva ca .. 25 ..
1.128.d:
घृतस्थूला घृताची च विषूची पूर्वचित्यपि ॥
प्रम्लोचीत्यप्सराश्चैव निम्लोचन्ती तथैव च ॥ 25 ॥
1.128.m: Ghṛtasthūlā, Ghṛtācī, Viṣūcī, and Pūrvacitti, / the apsaras Pramlocā, and likewise Nimlocantī.

1.128.s:
anenaiva prasaṃgena tathānyāsāṃ mahīpate ..
janma te'psarasāṃ vakṣye tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu .. 26 ..
1.128.d:
अनेनैव प्रसंगेन तथान्यासां महीपते ॥
जन्म तेऽप्सरसां वक्ष्ये तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥ 26 ॥
1.128.m: In this very connection, O king, / I shall tell you of the birth of other apsarases; hear that from me as I speak.

1.128.s:
sundopasundanāśāya nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā ..
tilaṃtilaṃ samādāya sarvaratnaistilottamā ..27..
1.128.d:
सुन्दोपसुन्दनाशाय निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा ॥
तिलंतिलं समादाय सर्वरत्नैस्तिलोत्तमा ॥27॥
1.128.m: For the destruction of Sunda and Upasunda, Tilottamā was fashioned / by Viśvakarman, taking a particle by particle from all gems.

1.128.s:
yasyāḥ pradakṣiṇājjātaścaturvaktraḥ pinākabhṛt ..
sahasranayanaḥ śrīmānvajrī śakraśca pākahā .. 28 ..
1.128.d:
यस्याः प्रदक्षिणाज्जातश्चतुर्वक्त्रः पिनाकभृत् ॥
सहस्रनयनः श्रीमान्वज्री शक्रश्च पाकहा ॥ 28 ॥
1.128.m: From circumambulating her, the bearer of the Pināka became four-faced, / and Śakra, glorious wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of Pāka, became thousand-eyed.

1.128.s:
śeṣairdevagaṇairdṛṣṭvā bhramadvaktraiḥ pradakṣiṇaiḥ ..
kṛte karmaṇi sā prāptā sūryalokaṃ varāṅganā .. 29 ..
1.128.d:
शेषैर्देवगणैर्दृष्ट्वा भ्रमद्वक्त्रैः प्रदक्षिणैः ॥
कृते कर्मणि सा प्राप्ता सूर्यलोकं वराङ्गना ॥ 29 ॥
1.128.m: Beholding her with revolving faces as they circumambulated, / once her task was completed, that excellent woman attained the world of the Sun.

1.128.s:
ekasthaṃ rūpasaundaryaṃ draṣṭumicchanpitāmahaḥ ..
ahalyāṃ nāma kṛtavāṃstrailokyasyaikasundarīm .. 1.128.30 ..
1.128.d:
एकस्थं रूपसौन्दर्यं द्रष्टुमिच्छन्पितामहः ॥
अहल्यां नाम कृतवांस्त्रैलोक्यस्यैकसुन्दरीम् ॥ 1.128.30 ॥
1.128.m: Desiring to see the perfection of beauty united in one form, the Grandfather / created the one called Ahalyā, the sole beauty of the three worlds.

1.128.s:
gautamāya ca tāṃ prādādbrahmā śubhacaturmukhaḥ ..
yasyāḥ kṛte gautamena śakro nirvṛṣaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ ..31..
1.128.d:
गौतमाय च तां प्रादाद्ब्रह्मा शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥
यस्याः कृते गौतमेन शक्रो निर्वृषणः कृतः ॥31॥
1.128.m: Auspicious four-faced Brahmā gave her to Gautama; / for whose sake Śakra was castrated by Gautama.

1.128.s:
nārāyaṇorusaṃbhūtā tathā caivorvaśī śubhā ..
saṃtyaktamānasā vavre bhartāraṃ budhajaṃ nṛpam .. 32 .. .
1.128.d:
नारायणोरुसंभूता तथा चैवोर्वशी शुभा ॥
संत्यक्तमानसा वव्रे भर्तारं बुधजं नृपम् ॥ 32 ॥ ।
1.128.m: Likewise, the auspicious Urvaśī, born from the thigh of Nārāyaṇa, / with mind detached, chose as husband the king born of Budha,

1.128.s:
purūravasanāmānaṃ rūpeṇāpratimaṃ bhuvi ..
tenaiva sārdhamadyāpi divaṃ prāptā ca tiṣṭhati .. 33 ..
1.128.d:
पुरूरवसनामानं रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि ॥
तेनैव सार्धमद्यापि दिवं प्राप्ता च तिष्ठति ॥ 33 ॥
1.128.m: named Purūravas, matchless in beauty on earth; / together with him, having attained heaven, she remains even today.

1.128.s:
āhūtya iti vikhyātā tathaivāpsarasaḥ śubhā ..
brahmaṇā manasā sṛṣṭā devarāmā manoramāḥ .. 34 ..
1.128.d:
आहूत्य इति विख्याता तथैवाप्सरसः शुभा ॥
ब्रह्मणा मनसा सृष्टा देवरामा मनोरमाः ॥ 34 ॥
1.128.m: The auspicious apsarases celebrated as the Āhūtyas, / lovely divine women, were created by Brahmā with his mind.

1.128.s:
manoḥ sutāḥ śaucavatyo vidyujjālarucaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
bhīravaśca sutā mṛtyorbhūmijātā bhuvaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 35 ..
1.128.d:
मनोः सुताः शौचवत्यो विद्युज्जालरुचः स्मृताः ॥
भीरवश्च सुता मृत्योर्भूमिजाता भुवः स्मृताः ॥ 35 ॥
1.128.m: The daughters of Manu, endowed with purity, are remembered as shining like a network of lightning; / and the fearful daughters of Mṛtyu, born of the earth, are remembered as belonging to the earth.

1.128.s:
amṛtākhyāśca sambhūtāstathaivāmṛtamanthane ..
vahnijātā sudā nāma somādbhekurayāstathā .. 36 ..
1.128.d:
अमृताख्याश्च सम्भूतास्तथैवामृतमन्थने ॥
वह्निजाता सुदा नाम सोमाद्भेकुरयास्तथा ॥ 36 ॥
1.128.m: And those called Amṛtā were born at the churning of the nectar; / those born of fire are named Sudā, and the Bhekurayās are from Soma.

1.128.s:
āyurvatyastathā proktāḥ sūryaraśmisamudbhavāḥ ..
yajñotpannāstathā nāma ṛksāmabhyastatheṣṭayaḥ .. 37 ..
1.128.d:
आयुर्वत्यस्तथा प्रोक्ताः सूर्यरश्मिसमुद्भवाः ॥
यज्ञोत्पन्नास्तथा नाम ऋक्सामभ्यस्तथेष्टयः ॥ 37 ॥
1.128.m: Those originating from the rays of the sun are called Āyurvatīs; / those originating from sacrifice are called Iṣṭis, [born] from the ṛks and sāmans.

1.128.s:
vāyūtpannā sudā nāma devarāmāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
ityete bahusāhasrā vijñeyāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 38 ..
1.128.d:
वायूत्पन्ना सुदा नाम देवरामाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
इत्येते बहुसाहस्रा विज्ञेयाप्सरसां गणाः ॥ 38 ॥
1.128.m: Those born from the wind, named Sudā, are proclaimed as divine women; / thus these hosts of apsarases are to be known in their many thousands.

1.128.s:
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca patnyastā mātaraśca vai ..
sugandhāścāpyaniṣyandā sarvā hyapsarasaḥ śubhāḥ ..39 ..
1.128.d:
देवतानामृषीणां च पत्न्यस्ता मातरश्च वै ॥
सुगन्धाश्चाप्यनिष्यन्दा सर्वा ह्यप्सरसः शुभाः ॥39 ॥
1.128.m: They are the wives and mothers of the gods and sages; / all the auspicious apsarases are fragrant and free from bodily discharge;

1.128.s:
tāsāmāpyāyate sparśādānandaṃ cāśnute mahat ..
vinatā janayāmāsa rudrānvai somapīthinaḥ .. 1.128.40 ..
1.128.d:
तासामाप्यायते स्पर्शादानन्दं चाश्नुते महत् ॥
विनता जनयामास रुद्रान्वै सोमपीथिनः ॥ 1.128.40 ॥
1.128.m: by their touch one is invigorated and experiences great bliss. / Vinatā gave birth to the Rudras, drinkers of soma:

1.128.s:
aṅgārakaṃ tathā sūryaṃ nirṛtiṃ ca khagaṃ tathā ..
ajaikapādāhirbudhnyadhūmaketu dhvajāstathā .. 41 ..
1.128.d:
अङ्गारकं तथा सूर्यं निरृतिं च खगं तथा ॥
अजैकपादाहिर्बुध्न्यधूमकेतु ध्वजास्तथा ॥ 41 ॥
1.128.m: Aṅgāraka, Sūrya, Nirṛti, and Khaga, / Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Dhūmaketu, and Dhvaja,

1.128.s:
havanaṃ nṛśvaraṃ svabhyaṃ kapālamatha kiṅkiṇīm ..
ekādaśaite kathitāstava rudrā mahābalāḥ .. 42 ..
1.128.d:
हवनं नृश्वरं स्वभ्यं कपालमथ किङ्किणीम् ॥
एकादशैते कथितास्तव रुद्रा महाबलाः ॥ 42 ॥
1.128.m: Havana, Nṛśvara, Svabhya, Kapāla, and Kiṅkiṇī; / these eleven mighty Rudras have been declared to you,

1.128.s:
yeṣāṃ ca janayāmāsa dvau putrau yakṣarākṣasau ..
yayoḥ santānasaṃbhūtā rājanvai yakṣarākṣasāḥ .. 43 ..
1.128.d:
येषां च जनयामास द्वौ पुत्रौ यक्षराक्षसौ ॥
ययोः सन्तानसंभूता राजन्वै यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ 43 ॥
1.128.m: to whom she also bore two sons, Yakṣa and Rākṣasa, / from whose lineage, O king, were born the yakṣas and rākṣasas.

1.128.s:
imaṃ ca vaṃśaṃ niyamena yaḥ paṭhenmahātmanāṃ brāhmaṇadevasannidhau ..
apatyalābhaṃ sa labhet puṣkalāṃ śriyaṃ tathā pretya ca śobhanāṃ gatim .. 44 ..
1.128.d:
इमं च वंशं नियमेन यः पठेन्महात्मनां ब्राह्मणदेवसन्निधौ ॥
अपत्यलाभं स लभेत् पुष्कलां श्रियं तथा प्रेत्य च शोभनां गतिम् ॥ 44 ॥
1.128.m: And whoever regularly recites this lineage of the high-souled ones in the presence of brahmins and gods / shall obtain offspring, abundant prosperity, and, after death, an auspicious destiny.

1.129.s:
.. vajra uvāca .. ..
urvaśī ca kathaṃ jātā budhajaṃ pārthivaṃ katham ..
patiṃ kṛtavatī devī mānuṣaṃ tatprakīrtaya .. 1 ..
1.129.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥ ॥
उर्वशी च कथं जाता बुधजं पार्थिवं कथम् ॥
पतिं कृतवती देवी मानुषं तत्प्रकीर्तय ॥ 1 ॥
1.129.m: Vajra said: / How was Urvaśī born, and how did the goddess / make the mortal king born of Budha her husband? Proclaim that.

1.129.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sādhyau dharmasutau proktau naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī ..
yau tau pūrvaṃ mahīpālau tāvubhau yadunandana .. 2 ..
1.129.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
साध्यौ धर्मसुतौ प्रोक्तौ नरनारायणावृषी ॥
यौ तौ पूर्वं महीपालौ तावुभौ यदुनन्दन ॥ 2 ॥
1.129.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The two sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa are declared to be Sādhyas, the sons of Dharma; / both of them were previously kings, O joy of the Yadus.

1.129.s:
viṣṇoraṃśau mahāvīryau tapasyabhiratau sadā ..
tayostadāśramaṃ ramyaṃ sugandhiviṭapadrumam .. 3 ..
1.129.d:
विष्णोरंशौ महावीर्यौ तपस्यभिरतौ सदा ॥
तयोस्तदाश्रमं रम्यं सुगन्धिविटपद्रुमम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.129.m: They are portions of Viṣṇu, of great heroism, ever devoted to austerity. / Their charming hermitage, with fragrant boughs and trees,

1.129.s:
badaryāśramamityuktaṃ mṛdusparśahimaṃ śubham ..
uṣṇatoyavahā gaṅgā śītatoyavahā parā .. 4 ..
1.129.d:
बदर्याश्रममित्युक्तं मृदुस्पर्शहिमं शुभम् ॥
उष्णतोयवहा गङ्गा शीततोयवहा परा ॥ 4 ॥
1.129.m: called the hermitage of Badarī, is auspicious, with snow soft to the touch; / one Gaṅgā carries warm waters, the other carries cold waters,

1.129.s:
suvarṇasikatā ramyā kāñcanotpalamālinī ..
tatra sā badarī ramyā nityapuṣpaphalopagā .. 5 ..
1.129.d:
सुवर्णसिकता रम्या काञ्चनोत्पलमालिनी ॥
तत्र सा बदरी रम्या नित्यपुष्पफलोपगा ॥ 5 ॥
1.129.m: delightful with golden sand, garlanded with golden lotuses; / there stands that charming jujube tree, ever endowed with flowers and fruits.

1.129.s:
tatra tau muniśārdūlau ghoraṃ tapa upāśritau ..
bhavāya sarvalokasya sarvalokeśvarāvubhau .. 6 ..
1.129.d:
तत्र तौ मुनिशार्दूलौ घोरं तप उपाश्रितौ ॥
भवाय सर्वलोकस्य सर्वलोकेश्वरावुभौ ॥ 6 ॥
1.129.m: There, those two tigers among sages, lords of all the worlds, / took refuge in fierce austerity for the welfare of the entire world.

1.129.s:
tayostapasyatorevaṃ mauneyāpsaraso daśa ..
tayostu tapasā vighnaṃ saṃbhūya kṛtaniścayāḥ .. 7 ..
1.129.d:
तयोस्तपस्यतोरेवं मौनेयाप्सरसो दश ॥
तयोस्तु तपसा विघ्नं संभूय कृतनिश्चयाः ॥ 7 ॥
1.129.m: While the two were thus performing tapas, ten apsarases born of Muni / joined together, having resolved [to cause] an obstacle to the tapas of the two.

1.129.s:
taṃ pradeśamanuprāptā nānābharaṇabhūṣaṇāḥ ..
pitāmahānna saumyo'sti kaścidrājañjagattraye .. 8 ..
1.129.d:
तं प्रदेशमनुप्राप्ता नानाभरणभूषणाः ॥
पितामहान्न सौम्योऽस्ति कश्चिद्राजञ्जगत्त्रये ॥ 8 ॥
1.129.m: Adorned with various ornaments, they reached that place. / O king, there was none more charming than them in the three worlds, except the Grandfather [Brahmā].

1.129.s:
tāsāṃ darśanamāsādya naraḥ kāmavaśo bhavet ..
kusumāni vicinvatyo lalantyaśca yathāsukham .. 9 ..
1.129.d:
तासां दर्शनमासाद्य नरः कामवशो भवेत् ॥
कुसुमानि विचिन्वत्यो ललन्त्यश्च यथासुखम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.129.m: Upon beholding them, a man would come under the sway of desire. / Gathering flowers and sporting as they pleased,

1.129.s:
dṛṣṭā nārāyaṇenātha sarvā bālamṛgekṣaṇāḥ ..
tāsāmantargataṃ bhāvaṃ jñātvā vedavidāṃ varaḥ .. 1.129.10 ..
1.129.d:
दृष्टा नारायणेनाथ सर्वा बालमृगेक्षणाः ॥
तासामन्तर्गतं भावं ज्ञात्वा वेदविदां वरः ॥ 1.129.10 ॥
1.129.m: they, all having eyes like young deer, were then seen by Nārāyaṇa. / Knowing their inner intention, the best among the knowers of the Veda,

1.129.s:
jitakrodho mahātejā jitakāmo'rthadharmavit ..
ādāya sahakārasya rasaṃ madanadīpanam .. 11 ..
1.129.d:
जितक्रोधो महातेजा जितकामोऽर्थधर्मवित् ॥
आदाय सहकारस्य रसं मदनदीपनम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.129.m: having conquered anger, endowed with great splendor, having mastered desire, knowing interest and dharma, / took the juice of a mango tree, which kindles love,

1.129.s:
ūrvościtreṇa cārvaṅgīṃ nirmame'psarasaṃ śubhām ..
ūrvoḥ kṛtā sā citreṇa citrākaraṇaśālinī ..12..
1.129.d:
ऊर्वोश्चित्रेण चार्वङ्गीं निर्ममेऽप्सरसं शुभाम् ॥
ऊर्वोः कृता सा चित्रेण चित्राकरणशालिनी ॥12॥
1.129.m: and on his thighs fashioned by painting a fair-limbed, auspicious apsaras. / Made on his thighs by painting, possessing an astonishing form,

1.129.s:
tasminneva kṣaṇe nārī babhūvāyatalocanā ..
na devī na ca gandharvī nāsurī na ca pannagī ..13..
1.129.d:
तस्मिन्नेव क्षणे नारी बभूवायतलोचना ॥
न देवी न च गन्धर्वी नासुरी न च पन्नगी ॥13॥
1.129.m: at that very moment she became a woman with long eyes. / Neither goddess, nor gandharva woman, nor asura woman, nor snake maiden

1.129.s:
tādṛgvidhā triloke'sminyādṛśī sā varāṅganā ..
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vrīḍitāssarvā mauneyāpsaraso daśa .. 14..
1.129.d:
तादृग्विधा त्रिलोकेऽस्मिन्यादृशी सा वराङ्गना ॥
तां दृष्ट्वा व्रीडितास्सर्वा मौनेयाप्सरसो दश ॥ 14॥
1.129.m: in this threefold world was like that excellent woman. / Seeing her, all the ten apsarases born of Muni were ashamed,

1.129.s:
jagmuryathāgataṃ rājam̐stacchuśrāva purandaraḥ..
draṣṭuṃ kautūhalāttāṃ ca badaryāśramamāgataḥ .. 15 ..
1.129.d:
जग्मुर्यथागतं राजम्̐स्तच्छुश्राव पुरन्दरः॥
द्रष्टुं कौतूहलात्तां च बदर्याश्रममागतः ॥ 15 ॥
1.129.m: and went away as they had come, O king. Purandara heard of that; / out of curiosity to see her, he came to the hermitage of Badarī.

1.129.s:
pādayornyapatadvajrī sādhyayordharmanityoḥ ..
dadarśa ca śubhāṅgīṃ tāṃ śriyaṃ devīmivāparām .. 16 ..
1.129.d:
पादयोर्न्यपतद्वज्री साध्ययोर्धर्मनित्योः ॥
ददर्श च शुभाङ्गीं तां श्रियं देवीमिवापराम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.129.m: The wielder of the thunderbolt fell at the feet of the two Sādhyas who were constant in dharma, / and he saw that fair-limbed woman like a second goddess Śrī.

1.129.s:
tamuvāca hasansādhyastadā nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ ..
mamorujātā dharmajña urvaśīyaṃ bhavediti .. 17 ..
1.129.d:
तमुवाच हसन्साध्यस्तदा नारायणः प्रभुः ॥
ममोरुजाता धर्मज्ञ उर्वशीयं भवेदिति ॥ 17 ॥
1.129.m: Smiling, the lord Sādhya Nārāyaṇa then said to him: / "She is born of my thigh (ūru), O knower of dharma, so let her be Urvaśī.

1.129.s:
nayasva tridivaṃ caināṃ bhavatvapsarasāṃ śubhā ..
evamukte mudaṃ prāpya abhivādya ca tāvṛṣī .. 18 ..
1.129.d:
नयस्व त्रिदिवं चैनां भवत्वप्सरसां शुभा ॥
एवमुक्ते मुदं प्राप्य अभिवाद्य च तावृषी ॥ 18 ॥
1.129.m: Take her to heaven; let her be an auspicious [ornament] of the apsarases." / When this was said, filled with joy, having saluted the two sages,

1.129.s:
anayattāṃ tataḥ svargaṃ devīṃ bālamṛgekṣaṇām ..
śiṣyatve pradadau tvenāṃ gandharvasya ca tumburoḥ..19..
1.129.d:
अनयत्तां ततः स्वर्गं देवीं बालमृगेक्षणाम् ॥
शिष्यत्वे प्रददौ त्वेनां गन्धर्वस्य च तुम्बुरोः॥19॥
1.129.m: he then took that fawn-eyed goddess to heaven. / And he gave her into pupilage to the gandharva Tumburu.

1.129.s:
tataḥ kadācicchakrasya nanarta puratastu sā ..
upadeśamatikramya tumbaroścāruhāsinī ..1.129.20..
1.129.d:
ततः कदाचिच्छक्रस्य ननर्त पुरतस्तु सा ॥
उपदेशमतिक्रम्य तुम्बरोश्चारुहासिनी ॥1.129.20॥
1.129.m: Then, on one occasion, that sweet-smiling [maiden] danced before Śakra, / transgressing the instruction of Tumburu.

1.129.s:
tāṃ śaśāpa sa gandharvo mānuṣye vatsyase śubhe ..
devalokamimaṃ tyaktvā mānuṣeṇa sahānaghe .. 21 ..
1.129.d:
तां शशाप स गन्धर्वो मानुष्ये वत्स्यसे शुभे ॥
देवलोकमिमं त्यक्त्वा मानुषेण सहानघे ॥ 21 ॥
1.129.m: That gandharva cursed her: "You shall dwell in the world of mortals, O auspicious one! / Leaving this world of the gods, along with a mortal, O sinless one,

1.129.s:
kañcitkālamupāsyaivaṃ mānuṣaṃ taṃ śucismite ..
āgamya tridive tāvattasmādabhyasyase tataḥ .. 22 ..
1.129.d:
कञ्चित्कालमुपास्यैवं मानुषं तं शुचिस्मिते ॥
आगम्य त्रिदिवे तावत्तस्मादभ्यस्यसे ततः ॥ 22 ॥
1.129.m: having served that mortal thus for some time, O sweet-smiling one, / returning to heaven, you will then practice under him.

1.129.s:
tenaiva sārdhaṃ tridive raṃsyase tvaṃ śubhānanā ..
vaivasvatākhyasya manoryāvadantaramucyate .. 23 ..
1.129.d:
तेनैव सार्धं त्रिदिवे रंस्यसे त्वं शुभानना ॥
वैवस्वताख्यस्य मनोर्यावदन्तरमुच्यते ॥ 23 ॥
1.129.m: Together with him alone you will take pleasure in heaven, O fair-faced one, / for the duration of the period of the Manu called Vaivasvata."

1.129.s:
evaṃ hi śaptā nṛpavarya tena papāta rājanguruṇā nṛloke ..
uvāsa rājñā sahitā tu tasmātsvargaṃ samāsādya tathaiva tena .. 24 .. ..
1.129.d:
एवं हि शप्ता नृपवर्य तेन पपात राजन्गुरुणा नृलोके ॥
उवास राज्ञा सहिता तु तस्मात्स्वर्गं समासाद्य तथैव तेन ॥ 24 ॥ ॥
1.129.m: Thus cursed by her teacher, O best of kings, she fell to the world of men, O king; / but she dwelt together with the king, and then, having reached heaven, [dwelt] likewise with him.

1.130.s:
vajra uvāca ..
nākaṃ tyaktvorvaśī brahmanbudhaputraṃ kathaṃ gatā ..
kva ca sā taṃ narendrendraṃ dṛṣṭavatyaparājitam .. 1 ..
1.130.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
नाकं त्यक्त्वोर्वशी ब्रह्मन्बुधपुत्रं कथं गता ॥
क्व च सा तं नरेन्द्रेन्द्रं दृष्टवत्यपराजितम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.130.m: Vajra said: / Having abandoned heaven, O brahmin, how did Urvaśī go to the son of Budha? / And where did she see that unconquered lord of kings?

1.130.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
mano vaivasvatasyāsya dvāpare prathame purā ..
vṛtte devāsure yuddhe vṛtte cāmṛtamanthane .. 2..
1.130.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
मनो वैवस्वतस्यास्य द्वापरे प्रथमे पुरा ॥
वृत्ते देवासुरे युद्धे वृत्ते चामृतमन्थने ॥ 2॥
1.130.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Long ago, in the first Dvāpara age of this Manu Vaivasvata, / when the war between gods and asuras had taken place, and the churning for nectar had occurred,

1.130.s:
saṃgrāme kṛtakarmāṇaṃ tasminneva narādhipam ..
śakrasyārdhāsana gataṃ rūpeṇāpratimaṃ tadā .. 3 ..
1.130.d:
संग्रामे कृतकर्माणं तस्मिन्नेव नराधिपम् ॥
शक्रस्यार्धासन गतं रूपेणाप्रतिमं तदा ॥ 3 ॥
1.130.m: the long-eyed daughter of Nārāyaṇa then saw that lord of men, / who had performed heroic deeds in that very battle, / sharing half of Śakra's seat, matchless in beauty at that time,

1.130.s:
sampūjyamānaṃ tridaśairdadarśāyatalocanā ..
budhaputraṃ narendendraṃ tadā nārāyaṇātmajā .. 4 ..
1.130.d:
सम्पूज्यमानं त्रिदशैर्ददर्शायतलोचना ॥
बुधपुत्रं नरेन्देन्द्रं तदा नारायणात्मजा ॥ 4 ॥
1.130.m: being worshipped by the thirty [gods]— / the son of Budha, the lord of kings.

1.130.s:
dṛṣṭvā babhūva cāsvasthā kāmamārgaṇatāḍitā ..
tataḥ prabhṛti bhavyeṣu merukuñjeṣu bhāminī .. 5 ..
1.130.d:
दृष्ट्वा बभूव चास्वस्था काममार्गणताडिता ॥
ततः प्रभृति भव्येषु मेरुकुञ्जेषु भामिनी ॥ 5 ॥
1.130.m: Seeing him, struck by the arrows of love, she became unsettled. / From that time on, in the lovely bowers of Meru,

1.130.s:
ākāraṃ gūhamānā sā kālaṃ nayati kāminī ..
cintayantī narendrendraṃ kandarpapratimaṃ sadā .. 6 ..
1.130.d:
आकारं गूहमाना सा कालं नयति कामिनी ॥
चिन्तयन्ती नरेन्द्रेन्द्रं कन्दर्पप्रतिमं सदा ॥ 6 ॥
1.130.m: concealing her appearance, that passionate woman passed the time, / constantly thinking of that lord of kings, who resembled Kandarpa.

1.130.s:
na sā bhuṅkte na svapiti śrāntā svapiti vā yadā ..
tadā paśyati taṃ svapne nīlanīrajalocanā .. 7 ..
1.130.d:
न सा भुङ्क्ते न स्वपिति श्रान्ता स्वपिति वा यदा ॥
तदा पश्यति तं स्वप्ने नीलनीरजलोचना ॥ 7 ॥
1.130.m: She did not eat, nor did she sleep; or when, exhausted, she slept, / then that woman with eyes like blue lotuses saw him in her dream.

1.130.s: manorathām̐śca kurute yām̐śca taṃ prati bhūmipam .. 8 ..
1.130.d: मनोरथाम्̐श्च कुरुते याम्̐श्च तं प्रति भूमिपम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.130.m: And whatever desires she formed toward that ruler of the earth,

1.130.s:
tāni sā paśyati svapne kathañcitsvapnamohitā ..
kadācitkrīḍite rājñā kadācidanunīyate .. 9 ..
1.130.d:
तानि सा पश्यति स्वप्ने कथञ्चित्स्वप्नमोहिता ॥
कदाचित्क्रीडिते राज्ञा कदाचिदनुनीयते ॥ 9 ॥
1.130.m: those she saw in her dream, somehow deluded by sleep: / sometimes she was played with by the king, sometimes she was conciliated;

1.130.s:
suptā kadācidrājendra vadatī pratibuddhyate ..
kaṇṭhe gṛhītā sā rājñā tayā cāsau mahīpatiḥ .. 1.130.10 ..
1.130.d:
सुप्ता कदाचिद्राजेन्द्र वदती प्रतिबुद्ध्यते ॥
कण्ठे गृहीता सा राज्ञा तया चासौ महीपतिः ॥ 1.130.10 ॥
1.130.m: sometimes, asleep, she woke up speaking, O chief of kings, / held by the neck by the king, and she [holding] that lord of the earth.

1.130.s:
evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu sā svapne nidrāmohamupāgatā ..
tathaiva bāhupāśena racitena vibudhyate .. 11 ..
1.130.d:
एवं दृष्ट्वा तु सा स्वप्ने निद्रामोहमुपागता ॥
तथैव बाहुपाशेन रचितेन विबुध्यते ॥ 11 ॥
1.130.m: Having seen thus in a dream, fallen into the stupor of sleep, / she awoke with the snare of her arms bound in that very way.

1.130.s:
svapnasaṃsthaṃ yadā dṛṣṭvā mohamāyāti sā ciram ..
kṛtvā citragataṃ paṭṭe kadācicca nirīkṣate .. 12 ..
1.130.d:
स्वप्नसंस्थं यदा दृष्ट्वा मोहमायाति सा चिरम् ॥
कृत्वा चित्रगतं पट्टे कदाचिच्च निरीक्षते ॥ 12 ॥
1.130.m: When, having seen him present in a dream, she fell into a prolonged swoon, / she would sometimes gaze upon him, having depicted him in a painting on a cloth.

1.130.s:
evaṃ narendre gatasarvabhāvāṃ vijñāya tāṃ cārutarāṅgayaṣṭim ..
āpāṇḍurakṣāmakapolabhittiṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rambhāṃ tvaritaṃ jagāda .. 13 ..
1.130.d:
एवं नरेन्द्रे गतसर्वभावां विज्ञाय तां चारुतराङ्गयष्टिम् ॥
आपाण्डुरक्षामकपोलभित्तिं दृष्ट्वैव रम्भां त्वरितं जगाद ॥ 13 ॥
1.130.m: Knowing that all her affection had thus gone to the lord of kings, seeing her of most lovely, slender form, / with the surface of her cheeks pale and emaciated, Rambhā at once spoke to her:

1.130.s:
yatnena cārvaṅgi nigūhamānā bhāvaṃ mayā tvaṃ viditāsi subhrūḥ ..
tasminnarendre hṛdayaṃ tavedaṃ yo'sau mahātmā samareṣvajeyaḥ .. 14 ..
1.130.d:
यत्नेन चार्वङ्गि निगूहमाना भावं मया त्वं विदितासि सुभ्रूः ॥
तस्मिन्नरेन्द्रे हृदयं तवेदं योऽसौ महात्मा समरेष्वजेयः ॥ 14 ॥
1.130.m: "Though zealously concealing your feeling, O fair-limbed one with beautiful eyebrows, you are understood by me. / Your heart is set on that lord of kings, that great soul who is unconquerable in battles,

1.130.s:
purūravā nāma jagattraye'sminkhyātiṃ gataḥ saccaritairnṛvīraḥ..
rūpeṇa kāmaṃ vyatiricya bhāti śauryeṇa śakrādatiricyate saḥ .. 15 ..
1.130.d:
पुरूरवा नाम जगत्त्रयेऽस्मिन्ख्यातिं गतः सच्चरितैर्नृवीरः॥
रूपेण कामं व्यतिरिच्य भाति शौर्येण शक्रादतिरिच्यते सः ॥ 15 ॥
1.130.m: the heroic man known in this threefold world by the name Purūravas for his virtuous conduct. / Surpassing Kāma in beauty, he shines; he surpasses Śakra in valor.

1.130.s:
dāne samastasya ca nāsti kaścitsa tyepyanaupamyaguṇe nṛvīraḥ ..
devāsure'sminsamare hatāni tenāsurāṇāṃ niyutāni pañca .. 16 ..
1.130.d:
दाने समस्तस्य च नास्ति कश्चित्स त्येप्यनौपम्यगुणे नृवीरः ॥
देवासुरेऽस्मिन्समरे हतानि तेनासुराणां नियुतानि पञ्च ॥ 16 ॥
1.130.m: In generosity, and in incomparable virtue of truthfulness, there is no equal to that heroic man. / In this battle between gods and asuras, five hundred thousand of the asuras were slain by him.

1.130.s:
keśī viśālo madanastathogro mahābalastena tathāpi śastaḥ ..
candrasya pautraśca budhasya putro mātāpi tasyārkasutasya dhātrī .. 17 ..
1.130.d:
केशी विशालो मदनस्तथोग्रो महाबलस्तेन तथापि शस्तः ॥
चन्द्रस्य पौत्रश्च बुधस्य पुत्रो मातापि तस्यार्कसुतस्य धात्री ॥ 17 ॥
1.130.m: Keśin, Viśāla, Madana, and fierce, mighty [asuras] were likewise slain by him. / He is the grandson of Candra and the son of Budha, and his mother is the nurse of the son of Sūrya.

1.130.s:
mānaṃ samutsṛjya viśālanetraṃ taṃ gaccha bāle nṛpatiṃ pratītam ..
tvadāptaye tasya ca nāsti yatnaḥ sudurlabhatvaṃ khalu devatānām .. 18 ..
1.130.d:
मानं समुत्सृज्य विशालनेत्रं तं गच्छ बाले नृपतिं प्रतीतम् ॥
त्वदाप्तये तस्य च नास्ति यत्नः सुदुर्लभत्वं खलु देवतानाम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.130.m: Casting away pride, O girl with broad eyes, go to that renowned king. / For him there is no effort [needed] to obtain you, yet you are very difficult to obtain even for gods!

1.130.s:
manorathānāṃ tvamagamyabhūmiryasmādviśālākṣi surāsurāṇām ..
mṛṇālaśayyā sutanu tvayeva saṃkleśitā candanapaṅkayuktā .. 19 ..
1.130.d:
मनोरथानां त्वमगम्यभूमिर्यस्माद्विशालाक्षि सुरासुराणाम् ॥
मृणालशय्या सुतनु त्वयेव संक्लेशिता चन्दनपङ्कयुक्ता ॥ 19 ॥
1.130.m: For you are beyond the realm of the desires of gods and asuras, O broad-eyed one! / O woman of beautiful body, this bed of lotus-stalks smeared with sandalwood paste has been crushed by you alone.

1.130.s:
tasyāṅkamāruhya bhavasva kānte vimuktatāpā tapanīyavarṇe ..
yāsyāma ehyehi nareśvarasya tasyāśu bho veśma varaprayoge .. 1.130.20 ..
1.130.d:
तस्याङ्कमारुह्य भवस्व कान्ते विमुक्ततापा तपनीयवर्णे ॥
यास्याम एह्येहि नरेश्वरस्य तस्याशु भो वेश्म वरप्रयोगे ॥ 1.130.20 ॥
1.130.m: Climbing upon his lap, O lovely one of golden complexion, become freed from torment! / Come, come, let us go quickly to the dwelling of that ruler of men on an auspicious undertaking,

1.130.s:
puraṃ pratiṣṭhānamiti pratītaṃ mātāmahādyatsamavāpa rājā ..
ityevamuktā tapanīyavarṇā tathyaṃ viditvā trapitā babhūva .. 21 ..
1.130.d:
पुरं प्रतिष्ठानमिति प्रतीतं मातामहाद्यत्समवाप राजा ॥
इत्येवमुक्ता तपनीयवर्णा तथ्यं विदित्वा त्रपिता बभूव ॥ 21 ॥
1.130.m: to the famous city named Pratiṣṭhāna, which the king obtained from his maternal grandfather." / Thus addressed, [Urvaśī] of golden complexion, realizing the truth, became bashful.

1.130.s:
uvāca rambhāṃ sakhi tathyamuktaṃ tvayā mataṃ taducitaṃ bhṛśaṃ me ..
yāsyāva adyaiva nareśvarasya tasyāntikaṃ bālamṛgābhanetre.. 22 ..
1.130.d:
उवाच रम्भां सखि तथ्यमुक्तं त्वया मतं तदुचितं भृशं मे ॥
यास्याव अद्यैव नरेश्वरस्य तस्यान्तिकं बालमृगाभनेत्रे॥ 22 ॥
1.130.m: She said to Rambhā: "Friend, you have spoken the truth; what you think seems very proper to me. / This very day let us both go near that ruler of men, O maiden with eyes like a young fawn!"

1.130.s:
yadyadya taṃ nīlasarojanetraṃ sampūrṇacandrābhamukhaṃ narendram ..
paśyāmi nāhaṃ pṛthudīrghabāhuṃ tato gamiṣyāmyavaśāvasānam .. 23 ..
1.130.d:
यद्यद्य तं नीलसरोजनेत्रं सम्पूर्णचन्द्राभमुखं नरेन्द्रम् ॥
पश्यामि नाहं पृथुदीर्घबाहुं ततो गमिष्याम्यवशावसानम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.130.m: "If today I do not see that king, whose eyes are like blue lotuses, / whose face resembles the full moon, and whose arms are broad and long, then I, helpless, will go to my death."

1.130.s:
pañcaiva kāmasya janaḥ pṛṣatkānyadāha rambhe tadalaṃ mṛṣaiva ..
mamāniśaṃ bāṇabharaistu vidhyanna śāmyate tvakṣinimeṣamātram .. 24 ..
1.130.d:
पञ्चैव कामस्य जनः पृषत्कान्यदाह रम्भे तदलं मृषैव ॥
ममानिशं बाणभरैस्तु विध्यन्न शाम्यते त्वक्षिनिमेषमात्रम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.130.m: "That people say Kāma has only five arrows, Rambhā, is entirely false; / for piercing me incessantly with masses of arrows, he does not pause even for the blinking of an eye."

1.130.s:
kāmāgnimadhye parivartamānaṃ na yāti bhasmatvamidaṃ śarīram ..
tasyaiva rājño vadanendunā tatsaṃrakṣyate me hṛdayasthitena .. 25..
1.130.d:
कामाग्निमध्ये परिवर्तमानं न याति भस्मत्वमिदं शरीरम् ॥
तस्यैव राज्ञो वदनेन्दुना तत्संरक्ष्यते मे हृदयस्थितेन ॥ 25॥
1.130.m: "Tossing about in the midst of the fire of love, this body does not turn to ashes; / it is preserved by the moon-like face of that very king dwelling in my heart."

1.130.s:
nayasva māṃ tasya viśālanetre samīpamadyaiva nareśvarasya ..
ityevamuktā karuṇaṃ hi rambhā pāṇāvupādāya viśālanetrām..26..
1.130.d:
नयस्व मां तस्य विशालनेत्रे समीपमद्यैव नरेश्वरस्य ॥
इत्येवमुक्ता करुणं हि रम्भा पाणावुपादाय विशालनेत्राम्॥26॥
1.130.m: "Lead me this very day, O large-eyed one, into the presence of that king!" / Spoken to thus piteously, Rambhā took the large-eyed one by the hand,

1.130.s: buddhyā samutplutya tato'ntarikṣaṃ jagāma rājño bhavanaṃ prahṛṣṭā .. 27 ..
1.130.d: बुद्ध्या समुत्प्लुत्य ततोऽन्तरिक्षं जगाम राज्ञो भवनं प्रहृष्टा ॥ 27 ॥
1.130.m: and having leapt into the sky with determination, she went delightedly to the king's abode.

1.131.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
urvaśī rambhayā sārddhaṃ jagāma tvaritaṃ tadā ..
kāmārttā siddhamārgeṇa sā dadarśātha nāradam ..1 ..
1.131.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
उर्वशी रम्भया सार्द्धं जगाम त्वरितं तदा ॥
कामार्त्ता सिद्धमार्गेण सा ददर्शाथ नारदम् ॥1 ॥
1.131.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Urvaśī then went swiftly along with Rambhā, / afflicted with love, along the path of the Siddhas; then she beheld Nārada,

1.131.s:
vrajantaṃ siddhamārgeṇa devalokādupāgatama ..
sampūjya nāradaṃ subhrūḥ prayayāveva satvarā..
vrajantaṃ siddhamārgeṇa devalokādupāgatam ..
sampūjya nāradaṃ subhrūḥ prayayāveva satvarā .. 2 ..
1.131.d:
व्रजन्तं सिद्धमार्गेण देवलोकादुपागतम ॥
सम्पूज्य नारदं सुभ्रूः प्रययावेव सत्वरा॥
व्रजन्तं सिद्धमार्गेण देवलोकादुपागतम् ॥
सम्पूज्य नारदं सुभ्रूः प्रययावेव सत्वरा ॥ 2 ॥
1.131.m: proceeding along the path of the Siddhas, arrived from the world of the gods. / Having honoured Nārada, the fair-browed one hastened along; / proceeding along the path of the Siddhas, arrived from the world of the gods, / having honoured Nārada, the fair-browed one hastened along.

1.131.s:
tāmāha nārado rambhe keyaṃ te prasthitā sakhī ..
rambhā śāpabhayāttasyāḥ sarvameva nyavedayat .. 3 ..
1.131.d:
तामाह नारदो रम्भे केयं ते प्रस्थिता सखी ॥
रम्भा शापभयात्तस्याः सर्वमेव न्यवेदयत् ॥ 3 ॥
1.131.m: Nārada said to her: "Rambhā, who is this friend of yours that has set out?" / Out of fear of his curse, Rambhā disclosed everything to him.

1.131.s:
tāmāha nārado bhūyaḥ śṛṇuṣva vacanaṃ mama ..
urvaśī gatabhāveyaṃ mānuṣaṃ taṃ nareśvaram .. 4 ..
1.131.d:
तामाह नारदो भूयः शृणुष्व वचनं मम ॥
उर्वशी गतभावेयं मानुषं तं नरेश्वरम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.131.m: Nārada spoke to her again: "Listen to my words. / Urvaśī, having fallen in love with that human king,

1.131.s:
śāpena tumbarormohāducitaṃ tatra vatsyati ..
yathā śubhaṃ tathā kāryaṃ tvayā me vacanaṃ śubhe ..9..
1.131.d:
शापेन तुम्बरोर्मोहादुचितं तत्र वत्स्यति ॥
यथा शुभं तथा कार्यं त्वया मे वचनं शुभे ॥9॥
1.131.m: will live there properly through the curse of Tumburu, out of infatuation. / As it would be auspicious, so you must carry out my words, O auspicious one.

1.131.s:
samayenorvaśī tasya vasatvasitalocanā ..
samayaścānayā kāryo yo rājñastaṃ nibodha me .. 6..
1.131.d:
समयेनोर्वशी तस्य वसत्वसितलोचना ॥
समयश्चानया कार्यो यो राज्ञस्तं निबोध मे ॥ 6॥
1.131.m: Let dark-eyed Urvaśī dwell [with him] under a condition; / and hear from me what condition she must make with the king:

1.131.s:
meṣadvayaṃ tu putratve purā kṛtavatī śubhā ..
tannityaṃ śayanābhyāśe sthāpanīyaṃ sulocane .. 7..
1.131.d:
मेषद्वयं तु पुत्रत्वे पुरा कृतवती शुभा ॥
तन्नित्यं शयनाभ्याशे स्थापनीयं सुलोचने ॥ 7॥
1.131.m: The auspicious one previously adopted two rams as her sons; / those must always be kept near her bed, O fair-eyed one.

1.131.s:
āhāraṃ ghṛtamātraṃ ca kartavyamanayā tathā ..
na draṣṭavyastathā nagno rājā rambhe purūravāḥ ..8..
1.131.d:
आहारं घृतमात्रं च कर्तव्यमनया तथा ॥
न द्रष्टव्यस्तथा नग्नो राजा रम्भे पुरूरवाः ॥8॥
1.131.m: Her food must consist solely of clarified butter; / and King Purūravas must not be seen naked, O Rambhā.

1.131.s:
na kartavyamakāmāyāstathā tena ca maithunam ..
ekasminnapyatho bhagne samaye cārulocanā ..9..
1.131.d:
न कर्तव्यमकामायास्तथा तेन च मैथुनम् ॥
एकस्मिन्नप्यथो भग्ने समये चारुलोचना ॥9॥
1.131.m: Nor should intercourse be performed by him with her if she is unwilling. / If even one condition is broken, then, O lovely-eyed one,

1.131.s:
yadi vatsyati rājānaṃ śilābhūtā bhaviṣyati ..
urvaśī rambhayā sārdhamevamastviti nāradam .. 1.131.10 ..
1.131.d:
यदि वत्स्यति राजानं शिलाभूता भविष्यति ॥
उर्वशी रम्भया सार्धमेवमस्त्विति नारदम् ॥ 1.131.10 ॥
1.131.m: if she continues to live with the king, she will turn into stone." / Together with Rambhā, Urvaśī, saying "So be it" to Nārada,

1.131.s:
uktvā saṃpūjya ca muniṃ pratasthe punareva ca ..
nārado vyagamadvipraḥ puraṃ vaiśravaṇasya ca .. 11 ....
1.131.d:
उक्त्वा संपूज्य च मुनिं प्रतस्थे पुनरेव च ॥
नारदो व्यगमद्विप्रः पुरं वैश्रवणस्य च ॥ 11 ॥॥
1.131.m: and having honoured the sage, set out once more. / And Nārada, the brahmin, departed for the city of Vaiśravaṇa.

1.131.s:
dadarśa ca pratiṣṭhānaṃ corvaśī rambhayā saha ..
prākāreṇārkavarṇena kāñcanena virājitam .. 12..
1.131.d:
ददर्श च प्रतिष्ठानं चोर्वशी रम्भया सह ॥
प्राकारेणार्कवर्णेन काञ्चनेन विराजितम् ॥ 12॥
1.131.m: And Urvaśī together with Rambhā beheld Pratiṣṭhāna, / radiant with a golden rampart the colour of the sun,

1.131.s:
caturbhirgopuraiśśubhrai rājataiśca virājitam ..
śobhanaṃ ca tathā ramyaṃ vidrumasya ca toraṇaiḥ .. 13..
1.131.d:
चतुर्भिर्गोपुरैश्शुभ्रै राजतैश्च विराजितम् ॥
शोभनं च तथा रम्यं विद्रुमस्य च तोरणैः ॥ 13॥
1.131.m: resplendent with four white, silver city gates, / and beautiful and charming with archways of coral,

1.131.s:
suvibhaktamahāraṇyaṃ mahārājapathaṃ śubham ..
parikhābhirvicitrābhiḥ padminībhiralaṃkṛtam .. 14..
1.131.d:
सुविभक्तमहारण्यं महाराजपथं शुभम् ॥
परिखाभिर्विचित्राभिः पद्मिनीभिरलंकृतम् ॥ 14॥
1.131.m: with great forests well laid out, with an auspicious royal highway, / adorned with varied moats and lotus ponds,

1.131.s:
khamullikhadbhiḥ prāsādaiḥ pāṇḍurairupaśobhitam ..
śūrāḍhyajanabhūyiṣṭhaṃ divyaṃ puruṣasaṃyutam ..15..
1.131.d:
खमुल्लिखद्भिः प्रासादैः पाण्डुरैरुपशोभितम् ॥
शूराढ्यजनभूयिष्ठं दिव्यं पुरुषसंयुतम् ॥15॥
1.131.m: graced with pale palaces scraping the sky, / filled with heroes and wealthy people, furnished with divine men,

1.131.s:
vaṇigbhirupasaṃkīrṇa nānāpaṇyavibhūṣitam ..
airāvatakulotpannaiścalatparvatasannibhaiḥ ..16..
1.131.d:
वणिग्भिरुपसंकीर्ण नानापण्यविभूषितम् ॥
ऐरावतकुलोत्पन्नैश्चलत्पर्वतसन्निभैः ॥16॥
1.131.m: crowded with merchants, adorned with varied commodities, / with elephants born from the lineage of Airāvata resembling moving mountains,

1.131.s:
kuñjarairbahusāhasraissaṃyutaṃ sumanoharaiḥ ..
turagairvahnijātaiśca pavanasya samairjave .. 17 ||
1.131.d:
कुञ्जरैर्बहुसाहस्रैस्संयुतं सुमनोहरैः ॥
तुरगैर्वह्निजातैश्च पवनस्य समैर्जवे ॥ 17 ॥
1.131.m: furnished with many thousands of very enchanting elephants, / and with horses born of fire, equal to the wind in speed,

1.131.s:
pānamattairnarairyuktamudyāneṣu tatastataḥ ..
śaṅkhabherīmṛdaṅgānāṃ paṭahānāṃ ca niḥsvanaiḥ ..18..
1.131.d:
पानमत्तैर्नरैर्युक्तमुद्यानेषु ततस्ततः ॥
शङ्खभेरीमृदङ्गानां पटहानां च निःस्वनैः ॥18॥
1.131.m: filled with men intoxicated with drink in the gardens here and there, / with the sounds of conches, bherī-drums, mṛdaṅgas, and paṭahas,

1.131.s:
vividhānāṃ ca vādyānāṃ vāditraṃ sarvaveśmagam ..
brahmaghoṣaṃ mahāghoṣaṃ vīṇāveṇunināditam ..19..
1.131.d:
विविधानां च वाद्यानां वादित्रं सर्ववेश्मगम् ॥
ब्रह्मघोषं महाघोषं वीणावेणुनिनादितम् ॥19॥
1.131.m: the music of various instruments echoing through every mansion, / resounding with the recitation of the Veda, with great clamour, and with the sounds of vīṇās and flutes,

1.131.s:
hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇaṃ sarvabādhāvivarjitam ..
padmakiñjalkavarṇābhiryutaṃ strībhiḥ sahasraśaḥ..1.131.20..
1.131.d:
हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णं सर्वबाधाविवर्जितम् ॥
पद्मकिञ्जल्कवर्णाभिर्युतं स्त्रीभिः सहस्रशः॥1.131.20॥
1.131.m: thronged with joyful, thriving people, free from all afflictions, / filled with thousands of women of the hue of lotus filaments,

1.131.s:
śyāmābhiśca mahārāja kāṇḍagaurībhireva ca .. ..
nānāveṣadharairyuktaṃ nānādeśodbhavaistathā ..21..
1.131.d:
श्यामाभिश्च महाराज काण्डगौरीभिरेव च ॥ ॥
नानावेषधरैर्युक्तं नानादेशोद्भवैस्तथा ॥21॥
1.131.m: and with dark-complexioned women, O great king, and fair ones; / filled with people wearing various attire and born in diverse regions,

1.131.s:
narairanekarūpaiśca śilpajñaiśca hyanekaśaḥ ..
purasya tasya madhye sā dadarśa nṛpatergṛham .22 ..
1.131.d:
नरैरनेकरूपैश्च शिल्पज्ञैश्च ह्यनेकशः ॥
पुरस्य तस्य मध्ये सा ददर्श नृपतेर्गृहम् .22 ॥
1.131.m: with men of manifold forms and many skilled in crafts. / In the centre of that city, she saw the palace of the king,

1.131.s:
madhye himācalasyeva kailāsaṃ parvatottamam ..
śrīmadbhiḥ saṃyutaṃ ramyairgṛhamedhaiḥ sahasraśaḥ..23..
1.131.d:
मध्ये हिमाचलस्येव कैलासं पर्वतोत्तमम् ॥
श्रीमद्भिः संयुतं रम्यैर्गृहमेधैः सहस्रशः॥23॥
1.131.m: like Mount Kailāsa, the best of mountains, in the midst of the Himālaya, / furnished with thousands of splendid and charming householders' dwellings,

1.131.s:
sudhāvadātairvipulaiścandraraśmisamaprabhaiḥ ..
kvacidrātnaiḥ kvacidraukmaiḥ kvacidbhūpāla rājataiḥ ..24..
1.131.d:
सुधावदातैर्विपुलैश्चन्द्ररश्मिसमप्रभैः ॥
क्वचिद्रात्नैः क्वचिद्रौक्मैः क्वचिद्भूपाल राजतैः ॥24॥
1.131.m: broad, white as plaster, of lustre equal to moonbeams, / here made of jewels, there made of gold, and here of silver, O protector of the earth,

1.131.s:
maṇividrumasopānairmuktājālavibhūṣitaiḥ ..
kvacicca puṣpadāmāḍhyairvaijayantīyutaiḥ kvacit .. 25 ..
1.131.d:
मणिविद्रुमसोपानैर्मुक्ताजालविभूषितैः ॥
क्वचिच्च पुष्पदामाढ्यैर्वैजयन्तीयुतैः क्वचित् ॥ 25 ॥
1.131.m: with stairways of gems and coral, decorated with strings of pearls, / here rich with garlands of flowers, there accompanied by victory banners.

1.131.s:
tasyāvidūre vipulaṃ vanaṃ caitrarathopamam ..
rājñaḥ krīḍāvanaṃ ramyaṃ dadarśa vipulekṣaṇā .. 26..
1.131.d:
तस्याविदूरे विपुलं वनं चैत्ररथोपमम् ॥
राज्ञः क्रीडावनं रम्यं ददर्श विपुलेक्षणा ॥ 26॥
1.131.m: Not far from it, the large-eyed one beheld a vast forest resembling Caitraratha, / the delightful pleasure garden of the king,

1.131.s:
drumairbahuvidhairyuktaṃ puṣpapūgaphalopagaiḥ ...
padminībhirvicitrābhiḥ krīḍāśailairmanoharaiḥ .. 27 ..
1.131.d:
द्रुमैर्बहुविधैर्युक्तं पुष्पपूगफलोपगैः ॥।
पद्मिनीभिर्विचित्राभिः क्रीडाशैलैर्मनोहरैः ॥ 27 ॥
1.131.m: furnished with trees of many kinds bearing flowers, areca nuts, and fruits, / with varied lotus pools and charming pleasure hills,

1.131.s:
prāsādaiśca tathā ramyai ramyairmaṇigaṇaistathā ..
tattu rambhāvanaṃ dṛṣṭvā sakhī vacanamabravīt .. 28 ..
1.131.d:
प्रासादैश्च तथा रम्यै रम्यैर्मणिगणैस्तथा ॥
तत्तु रम्भावनं दृष्ट्वा सखी वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 28 ॥
1.131.m: and with delightful palaces and charming masses of gems. / Having seen that grove, Rambhā said these words to her friend:

1.131.s:
rājñaḥ krīḍāvane ramye gahane'sminsulocane ..
māyācchannā nivatsyāvo yāvadastamayaṃ raveḥ .. 29 ..
1.131.d:
राज्ञः क्रीडावने रम्ये गहनेऽस्मिन्सुलोचने ॥
मायाच्छन्ना निवत्स्यावो यावदस्तमयं रवेः ॥ 29 ॥
1.131.m: "In this charming, dense pleasure garden of the king, O fair-eyed one, / let us dwell hidden by magic until the setting of the sun.

1.131.s:
tato gatvā narendraṃ taṃ coktvā tava cikīrṣitam..
ahaṃ tvāṃ tu nayiṣyāmi savidhe tasya bhūpateḥ ..
evamuktvā sakhī vākyaṃ nodayāmāsa corvaśī .. 1.131.30 ..
1.131.d:
ततो गत्वा नरेन्द्रं तं चोक्त्वा तव चिकीर्षितम्॥
अहं त्वां तु नयिष्यामि सविधे तस्य भूपतेः ॥
एवमुक्त्वा सखी वाक्यं नोदयामास चोर्वशी ॥ 1.131.30 ॥
1.131.m: Then, having gone and told that king your desire, / I will lead you into the presence of that ruler of the earth." / Having thus spoken the words, the friend urged Urvaśī on.

1.131.s:
krīḍāvanaṃ te ca tato'vatīrṇe taddevarāme sumanobhirāmam ..
krīḍāvane tatra tathorvaśī sā sūryāstakālaṃ manasā samaicchat .. 31 ..
1.131.d:
क्रीडावनं ते च ततोऽवतीर्णे तद्देवरामे सुमनोभिरामम् ॥
क्रीडावने तत्र तथोर्वशी सा सूर्यास्तकालं मनसा समैच्छत् ॥ 31 ॥
1.131.m: And then the two of them descended into the pleasure garden, which was pleasing to the mind like the garden of the gods; / and in that pleasure garden Urvaśī inwardly longed for the time of sunset.

1.132.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sūryāstamayamicchantī jñātvā rambhā tathorvaśīm ..
vinodārthaṃ hi tasyāśca darśayāmāsa tadvanam ..1..
1.132.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
सूर्यास्तमयमिच्छन्ती ज्ञात्वा रम्भा तथोर्वशीम् ॥
विनोदार्थं हि तस्याश्च दर्शयामास तद्वनम् ॥1॥
1.132.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Knowing Urvaśī to be thus longing for sunset, / Rambhā, for her diversion, showed her that forest:

1.132.s:
cāruprasūnaṃ paśyemaṃ subhage campakadrumam ..
tvadgātravarṇasadṛśaiḥ samantātkusumaiścitam ..2..
1.132.d:
चारुप्रसूनं पश्येमं सुभगे चम्पकद्रुमम् ॥
त्वद्गात्रवर्णसदृशैः समन्तात्कुसुमैश्चितम् ॥2॥
1.132.m: "Behold, fortunate one, this campaka tree with beautiful blossoms, / covered all around with flowers resembling the colour of your limbs!

1.132.s:
imaṃ ca dāḍimaṃ paśya puṣpitaṃ vāmalocane ..
yo'yaṃ bibhartti kusumaistvadīyāmadharaśriyam..3..
1.132.d:
इमं च दाडिमं पश्य पुष्पितं वामलोचने ॥
योऽयं बिभर्त्ति कुसुमैस्त्वदीयामधरश्रियम्॥3॥
1.132.m: "And behold this blossoming pomegranate tree, O fair-eyed one, / which with its blossoms bears the beauty of your lower lip!"

1.132.s:
paśya kāmaśarākāraṃ sahakāraṃ manoramam ..
yatra cātmasamutpannā rūḍhāstasya mahātmanaḥ .. 4 ..
1.132.d:
पश्य कामशराकारं सहकारं मनोरमम् ॥
यत्र चात्मसमुत्पन्ना रूढास्तस्य महात्मनः ॥ 4 ॥
1.132.m: Look at the delightful mango tree, shaped like Kāma's arrow, / on which have grown [creepers] produced from that great one itself.

1.132.s:
śriyaṃ kapolayostubhyamādadānairmanoramaiḥ ..
puṣpairupetā cārvaṅgi madhūkaṃ paśya śobhane..5..
1.132.d:
श्रियं कपोलयोस्तुभ्यमाददानैर्मनोरमैः ॥
पुष्पैरुपेता चार्वङ्गि मधूकं पश्य शोभने॥5॥
1.132.m: Endowed with delightful flowers that borrow / the splendour of your cheeks, O fair-limbed, lovely lady, behold the madhūka.

1.132.s:
tvatpayodharasaṃkāśai ramyairupacitaṃ phalaiḥ .....
paśya tāladrumaṃ saumye manasaḥ prītivardhanam ..6..
1.132.d:
त्वत्पयोधरसंकाशै रम्यैरुपचितं फलैः ॥॥।
पश्य तालद्रुमं सौम्ये मनसः प्रीतिवर्धनम् ॥6॥
1.132.m: Abounding with charming fruits resembling your breasts, / behold, gentle lady, the palmyra tree that enhances the heart’s delight.

1.132.s:
stambhaistvadūrusaṃkāśaiḥ kadalīṃ paśya śobhane ..
suvarṇā cārusarvāṅgī nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā .. 7 ...
1.132.d:
स्तम्भैस्त्वदूरुसंकाशैः कदलीं पश्य शोभने ॥
सुवर्णा चारुसर्वाङ्गी निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा ॥ 7 ॥।
1.132.m: With stems resembling your thighs, behold the plantain, O fair one, / of golden hue and beautiful in every limb, fashioned by Viśvakarman.

1.132.s:
paśyāvimuktakalatāṃ kusumāḍhyāṃ manoharām ..
tvatkeśapāśasaṃkāśairbhramarairupaśobhitām .. 8 ..
1.132.d:
पश्याविमुक्तकलतां कुसुमाढ्यां मनोहराम् ॥
त्वत्केशपाशसंकाशैर्भ्रमरैरुपशोभिताम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.132.m: Behold the avimukta creeper, rich in blossoms and enchanting, / adorned with bees that resemble your braid of hair.

1.132.s:
paśyemaṃ kundaviṭapaṃ tvaddantasadṛśaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
samantācchobhitaṃ puṣpairviśālākṣi manoharaiḥ .. 9 ..
1.132.d:
पश्येमं कुन्दविटपं त्वद्दन्तसदृशैः शुभैः ॥
समन्ताच्छोभितं पुष्पैर्विशालाक्षि मनोहरैः ॥ 9 ॥
1.132.m: Behold this kunda shrub, O large-eyed lady, / completely adorned with lovely, auspicious flowers resembling your teeth.

1.132.s:
paśya cotpalinīmetāmutpalairuśobhitām ..
tvannetrasadṛśaiḥ phullairmanohṛdayanandanaiḥ ..1.132.10 ..
1.132.d:
पश्य चोत्पलिनीमेतामुत्पलैरुशोभिताम् ॥
त्वन्नेत्रसदृशैः फुल्लैर्मनोहृदयनन्दनैः ॥1.132.10 ॥
1.132.m: And behold this lotus pond, beautified by blue water lilies / that resemble your eyes, full-blown and delighting the mind and heart.

1.132.s:
nalinīṃ subhage paśya kamalaiḥ puṣpitairyutām..
tava niḥśvāsagandhāḍhyaiḥ sauvarṇairvajrakesaraiḥ..11..
1.132.d:
नलिनीं सुभगे पश्य कमलैः पुष्पितैर्युताम्॥
तव निःश्वासगन्धाढ्यैः सौवर्णैर्वज्रकेसरैः॥11॥
1.132.m: Behold, fortunate lady, the lotus lake filled with blossoming lotuses / rich with the fragrance of your breath, golden with hard filaments.

1.132.s:
rājahaṃsānimānpaśya nalinītīragocarān..
gamanaṃ sumanohāri tvadīyamiva śikṣitān .. 12 ..
1.132.d:
राजहंसानिमान्पश्य नलिनीतीरगोचरान्॥
गमनं सुमनोहारि त्वदीयमिव शिक्षितान् ॥ 12 ॥
1.132.m: Behold these royal swans frequenting the banks of the lotus lake, / as if trained in your enchanting gait.

1.132.s:
tvatkarāgravidhānsaumye dhārayadbhiśca pallavān ..
krīḍāśailamimaṃ paśya yuktaṃ vahuvidhairdrumaiḥ .. 13 ..
1.132.d:
त्वत्कराग्रविधान्सौम्ये धारयद्भिश्च पल्लवान् ॥
क्रीडाशैलमिमं पश्य युक्तं वहुविधैर्द्रुमैः ॥ 13 ॥
1.132.m: And bearing shoots resembling your fingertips, O gentle lady, / behold this pleasure-hill furnished with diverse kinds of trees.

1.132.s:
krīḍāśaile cūtagataḥ kokilaḥ kāmavardhanaḥ ..
kūjatyayaṃ manohāri svanena sadṛśena te..14..
1.132.d:
क्रीडाशैले चूतगतः कोकिलः कामवर्धनः ॥
कूजत्ययं मनोहारि स्वनेन सदृशेन ते॥14॥
1.132.m: Perched on a mango tree upon the pleasure-hill, the cuckoo, increasing desire, / coos enchantingly with a voice resembling yours.

1.132.s:
krīḍāśaile nadīṃ paśya niḥsṛtāṃ śītalodakām ..
tulyaṃ te manasā saumye vahantīṃ nirmalaṃ jalam..15..
1.132.d:
क्रीडाशैले नदीं पश्य निःसृतां शीतलोदकाम् ॥
तुल्यं ते मनसा सौम्ये वहन्तीं निर्मलं जलम्॥15॥
1.132.m: Upon the pleasure-hill, behold the river flowing forth with cool water, / carrying limpid water equal to your mind, O gentle one.

1.132.s:
bahvāścaryayutaṃ saumyaṃ darśanīyaṃ vanaṃ bahu ..
kiṃ nu paśya viśālākṣi sūryo'stamupagacchati..16..
1.132.d:
बह्वाश्चर्ययुतं सौम्यं दर्शनीयं वनं बहु ॥
किं नु पश्य विशालाक्षि सूर्योऽस्तमुपगच्छति॥16॥
1.132.m: Full of many wonders, pleasant and lovely to see is this vast forest. / But why—look, O large-eyed lady, the sun is setting!

1.132.s:
tvāṃ tu kāmavaśāṃ jñātvā kṛpayeva divākaraḥ ..
saṃvṛttāṃśudharo devastvastamāyāti bhāmini ...17..
1.132.d:
त्वां तु कामवशां ज्ञात्वा कृपयेव दिवाकरः ॥
संवृत्तांशुधरो देवस्त्वस्तमायाति भामिनि ॥.17॥
1.132.m: Knowing you to be subject to desire, as if out of pity, / the radiant god, contracting his rays, has set, O passionate lady.

1.132.s:
kaṭhorāṇyapi patrāṇi pallavānīva sundari ..
astatāpānuraktāni rājante śākhināṃ bhṛśam .. 18 ..
1.132.d:
कठोराण्यपि पत्राणि पल्लवानीव सुन्दरि ॥
अस्ततापानुरक्तानि राजन्ते शाखिनां भृशम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.132.m: Even the coarse leaves, reddened by the glow of sunset / like tender sprouts, O beautiful woman, shine intensely on the trees.

1.132.s:
girīṇāṃ śikharānraktānkarotyeva divākaraḥ ..
jagāmāstaṃ viśālākṣi kṛtakarmā dinakṣaye .. 19 ..
1.132.d:
गिरीणां शिखरान्रक्तान्करोत्येव दिवाकरः ॥
जगामास्तं विशालाक्षि कृतकर्मा दिनक्षये ॥ 19 ॥
1.132.m: The sun, reddening the peaks of the mountains, / having finished his task at the end of day, has set, O large-eyed lady.

1.132.s:
sandhyākālena raktena pratīcī paśya śobhane ..
āliṅgamānāṃ sahasā kāminīmiva kāminīm .. 1.132.20 ..
1.132.d:
सन्ध्याकालेन रक्तेन प्रतीची पश्य शोभने ॥
आलिङ्गमानां सहसा कामिनीमिव कामिनीम् ॥ 1.132.20 ॥
1.132.m: Behold, O lovely one, the western quarter / swiftly embracing the red twilight, like a passionate woman embracing a passionate man.

1.132.s:
sāṃprataṃ niyamopetā dvijā dvijavarodbhave ..
sandhyākālamupāsante satāṃ mārgamanuvratāḥ .. 21 ..
1.132.d:
सांप्रतं नियमोपेता द्विजा द्विजवरोद्भवे ॥
सन्ध्याकालमुपासन्ते सतां मार्गमनुव्रताः ॥ 21 ॥
1.132.m: Now, observing vows and following the path of the virtuous, / twice-born men worship the twilight, O daughter of the best of the twice-born.

1.132.s:
anuyātā raviṃ sandhyā gatamastamapi prabhum ..
sādhvīva vanitā kānte kṛlajātā manasvinī .. 22 ..
1.132.d:
अनुयाता रविं सन्ध्या गतमस्तमपि प्रभुम् ॥
साध्वीव वनिता कान्ते कृलजाता मनस्विनी ॥ 22 ॥
1.132.m: Twilight has followed the sun, though her lord has set, / like a faithful, high-minded woman [following her husband], O lovely one, overcome with bashfulness.

1.132.s:
yāsyamānaṃ sunāsoru tamasā paśya bhūtalam ..
bhṛṅgodaratamālānāṃ tulyena varavarṇini .. 23 ..
1.132.d:
यास्यमानं सुनासोरु तमसा पश्य भूतलम् ॥
भृङ्गोदरतमालानां तुल्येन वरवर्णिनि ॥ 23 ॥
1.132.m: O lady with fair nose and lovely thighs, behold the surface of the earth about to be overwhelmed / by darkness resembling the belly of a bee or tamāla leaves, O woman of excellent complexion.

1.132.s:
vyāptaṃ hi tamasā sarvaṃ na virājati kiñcana ..
malinenāya tāpāṅgi jagatsarvaṃ samīkṛtam .. 24 ..
1.132.d:
व्याप्तं हि तमसा सर्वं न विराजति किञ्चन ॥
मलिनेनाय तापाङ्गि जगत्सर्वं समीकृतम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.132.m: For everything is pervaded by darkness; nothing shines. / By this dark [cover], O hot-limbed lady, the entire world has been made uniform.

1.132.s:
asyāṃ hi sakhi velāyāṃ madanena vaśīkṛtāḥ ..
nīlāmbaradharāḥ kāntā yānti kāntānalaṅkṛtāḥ ..25..
1.132.d:
अस्यां हि सखि वेलायां मदनेन वशीकृताः ॥
नीलाम्बरधराः कान्ता यान्ति कान्तानलङ्कृताः ॥25॥
1.132.m: At this hour indeed, my friend, subjugated by love, / wearing blue garments, decorated beloved women go to their lovers.

1.132.s:
paśyoditaṃ ca subhage subhagaṃ candramaṇḍalam ..
pānamattapurandhrīṇāṃ vadanena samatviṣam .. 26 ..
1.132.d:
पश्योदितं च सुभगे सुभगं चन्द्रमण्डलम् ॥
पानमत्तपुरन्ध्रीणां वदनेन समत्विषम् ॥ 26 ॥
1.132.m: And behold risen, O fortunate lady, the lovely orb of the moon, / equal in radiance to the face of women intoxicated by drink.

1.132.s:
kiñcidākramya gaganaṃ śvetatāṃ tu gataṃ sakhi ..
paśya candramasaṃ subhru nayanānandakārakam .. 27 ..
1.132.d:
किञ्चिदाक्रम्य गगनं श्वेततां तु गतं सखि ॥
पश्य चन्द्रमसं सुभ्रु नयनानन्दकारकम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.132.m: Having mounted slightly into the sky, it has turned white, my friend; / behold the moon, O fair-browed one, that brings delight to the eyes.

1.132.s:
jagato'sya tamo gatvā śaśāṅkaḥ sattvasannibhaḥ ..
virājatyamalaḥ saumye gagane sitasuprabhe..28..
1.132.d:
जगतोऽस्य तमो गत्वा शशाङ्कः सत्त्वसन्निभः ॥
विराजत्यमलः सौम्ये गगने सितसुप्रभे॥28॥
1.132.m: Dispelling the darkness of this world, the hare-marked moon, resembling pure being, / shines spotless, O gentle lady, in the sky of white radiance.

1.132.s:
kāmabāṇahatāyāste sadṛśaṃ gaṇḍayoḥ śriyā ..
bibhartyubhayataścandro jyotsnājālaṃ samutsṛjan .. 29 ..
1.132.d:
कामबाणहतायास्ते सदृशं गण्डयोः श्रिया ॥
बिभर्त्युभयतश्चन्द्रो ज्योत्स्नाजालं समुत्सृजन् ॥ 29 ॥
1.132.m: Resembling the splendour of the cheeks of you struck by Kāma's arrow, / the moon, casting out a web of moonlight on both sides, shines.

1.132.s:
candrarājatakumbhena diśeyaṃ varavarṇini ..
jyotsnācchalena kṣmā devī rājatīva virājate .. 1.132.30 ..
1.132.d:
चन्द्रराजतकुम्भेन दिशेयं वरवर्णिनि ॥
ज्योत्स्नाच्छलेन क्ष्मा देवी राजतीव विराजते ॥ 1.132.30 ॥
1.132.m: By means of the silver pitcher of the moon, O fair-complexioned lady, / the divine earth shines forth in this quarter, as if silvered under the guise of moonlight.

1.132.s:
candramasyudite paśya phullāṃ kumudinīṃ śubhe ..
tvadīyahāsasaṃkāśaiḥ kusumairupaśobhitām .. .. 31 ..
1.132.d:
चन्द्रमस्युदिते पश्य फुल्लां कुमुदिनीं शुभे ॥
त्वदीयहाससंकाशैः कुसुमैरुपशोभिताम् ॥ ॥ 31 ॥
1.132.m: Now that the moon has risen, behold the blossoming night-lotus pond, O auspicious lady, / adorned with flowers that resemble your smile.

1.132.s:
virahī cakravāko'yaṃ raktāmutpalinīṃ śubhe ..
sitāmiva sudukhārto viśatyāyatalocane .. 32 ..
1.132.d:
विरही चक्रवाकोऽयं रक्तामुत्पलिनीं शुभे ॥
सितामिव सुदुखार्तो विशत्यायतलोचने ॥ 32 ॥
1.132.m: This cakravāka separated from his mate, afflicted with deep sorrow, / enters the red lotus bed as if it were white, O large-eyed one.

1.132.s:
candrakāntagṛhādasmāccandraraśmi samaprabhā ..
candraraśmiparāmṛṣṭāḥ patantyudakabindavaḥ .. 33 ..
1.132.d:
चन्द्रकान्तगृहादस्माच्चन्द्ररश्मि समप्रभा ॥
चन्द्ररश्मिपरामृष्टाः पतन्त्युदकबिन्दवः ॥ 33 ॥
1.132.m: From this moonstone mansion, drops of water, equal in splendour to moonbeams / and touched by the moon's rays, fall down.

1.132.s:
āliṅgitā candramasā jahau rāttristamaḥpaṭam ..
kāmineva viśālākṣi kāminī vasanaṃ śubhā .. 34 ..
1.132.d:
आलिङ्गिता चन्द्रमसा जहौ रात्त्रिस्तमःपटम् ॥
कामिनेव विशालाक्षि कामिनी वसनं शुभा ॥ 34 ॥
1.132.m: Embraced by the moon, the night has cast off her garment of darkness, / like an auspicious passionate woman casting off her robe [when embraced] by her lover, O large-eyed one.

1.132.s:
candrodaye candrasamānavaktre narendracandre pramadāvane'smin ..
paśya tvamāśaṃsa ca jīvitāśāṃ tvadbhāgyanunnaṃ sahasā praviṣṭam .. 35 ..
1.132.d:
चन्द्रोदये चन्द्रसमानवक्त्रे नरेन्द्रचन्द्रे प्रमदावनेऽस्मिन् ॥
पश्य त्वमाशंस च जीविताशां त्वद्भाग्यनुन्नं सहसा प्रविष्टम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.132.m: At moonrise, O moon-faced lady, behold the moon among kings who has entered this pleasure grove, / impelled suddenly by your good fortune, and take hope for your life.

1.133.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityuktā rambhayā vākyaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānamāgatam ..
hṛṣṭā sasādhvasā devī babhūvātha tathorvaśī .. 1 ..
1.133.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्युक्ता रम्भया वाक्यं दृष्ट्वा राजानमागतम् ॥
हृष्टा ससाध्वसा देवी बभूवाथ तथोर्वशी ॥ 1 ॥
1.133.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Thus addressed by the words of Rambhā, upon seeing the king arrived, / the divine Urvaśī became both delighted and trembling with apprehension.

1.133.s:
atyāścaryamabhūddṛṣṭe rājñi tasyāḥ śubhānane ..
romāñcitatanutvaṃ ca saprasvedaṃ samābabhau .. 2 ..
1.133.d:
अत्याश्चर्यमभूद्दृष्टे राज्ञि तस्याः शुभानने ॥
रोमाञ्चिततनुत्वं च सप्रस्वेदं समाबभौ ॥ 2 ॥
1.133.m: When the king was seen, an extraordinary wonder came over that fair-faced lady; / and horripilation on her body along with perspiration appeared.

1.133.s:
tāmuvāca tato rambhā śṛṇūrvaśi vaco mama .
nehāgame'sya nṛpateḥ kāryamalpaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 3 ..
1.133.d:
तामुवाच ततो रम्भा शृणूर्वशि वचो मम ।
नेहागमेऽस्य नृपतेः कार्यमल्पं भविष्यति ॥ 3 ॥
1.133.m: Then Rambhā said to her: “Listen, Urvaśī, to my words: / the business of this king in coming here will be of no small matter.

1.133.s:
rājā sukhāsahāyo'yaṃ praviṣṭo niśi kānanam ..
pracchanne śṛṇuvastāvadasya vākyāni bhūpateḥ .. 4 ..
1.133.d:
राजा सुखासहायोऽयं प्रविष्टो निशि काननम् ॥
प्रच्छन्ने शृणुवस्तावदस्य वाक्यानि भूपतेः ॥ 4 ॥
1.133.m: This king, attended only by an intimate friend, has entered the forest at night. / Let us listen in concealment to the words of this ruler of the earth.”

1.133.s:
evamastvityuvācātha rambhāṃ nārāyaṇātmajā ..
māyācchannaśarīre te tataścāyayaturnṛpam .. 5 ..
1.133.d:
एवमस्त्वित्युवाचाथ रम्भां नारायणात्मजा ॥
मायाच्छन्नशरीरे ते ततश्चाययतुर्नृपम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.133.m: “So be it,” then said the daughter of Nārāyaṇa to Rambhā. / Then the two of them, their bodies concealed by magic, approached the king.

1.133.s:
rājānaṃ cārusarvāṅgaṃ papraccha tu tadā sakhā ..
rājño bahumato nityaṃ guṇavām̐ścātidhārmikaḥ .. 6 ..
1.133.d:
राजानं चारुसर्वाङ्गं पप्रच्छ तु तदा सखा ॥
राज्ञो बहुमतो नित्यं गुणवाम्̐श्चातिधार्मिकः ॥ 6 ॥
1.133.m: His friend then questioned the king who was handsome in every limb— / a virtuous and deeply righteous man, always held in high esteem by the king.

1.133.s:
sakhovāca ..
yataḥ prabhṛti rājendra tridivāttvamihāgataḥ ..
tataḥ prabhṛti cāsvastho mayā dṛṣṭo'si mānada ..7..
1.133.d:
सखोवाच ॥
यतः प्रभृति राजेन्द्र त्रिदिवात्त्वमिहागतः ॥
ततः प्रभृति चास्वस्थो मया दृष्टोऽसि मानद ॥7॥
1.133.m: The friend said: / “Ever since you arrived here from heaven, O king of kings, / from that time on I have seen you unwell, O giver of honour.

1.133.s:
tadasvāsthyaṃ kāmakṛtaṃ jñātavānasmi te nṛpa ..
tanmamācakṣva te guhyaṃ na cennaravarottama .. 8 ..
1.133.d:
तदस्वास्थ्यं कामकृतं ज्ञातवानस्मि ते नृप ॥
तन्ममाचक्ष्व ते गुह्यं न चेन्नरवरोत्तम ॥ 8 ॥
1.133.m: I know that this ailment of yours is caused by love, O king; / disclose that to me if it is not a secret, O best of men.”

1.133.s:
purūravā uvāca ..
tava guhyaṃ na me kiñcitkadācidapi vidyate ..
asvāsthyakāraṇaṃ saumya tava vakṣyāmyathātmanaḥ .. 9 ..
1.133.d:
पुरूरवा उवाच ॥
तव गुह्यं न मे किञ्चित्कदाचिदपि विद्यते ॥
अस्वास्थ्यकारणं सौम्य तव वक्ष्याम्यथात्मनः ॥ 9 ॥
1.133.m: Purūravas said: / “There is nothing of mine that is ever a secret from you. / I shall tell you, gentle friend, the cause of my indisposition.

1.133.s:
nārāyaṇasutā kāntā rūpeṇāpratimā śubhā ..
urvaśīnāmataḥ khyātā mayā dṛṣṭā varāpsarāḥ..1.133.10..
1.133.d:
नारायणसुता कान्ता रूपेणाप्रतिमा शुभा ॥
उर्वशीनामतः ख्याता मया दृष्टा वराप्सराः॥1.133.10॥
1.133.m: The lovely daughter of Nārāyaṇa, matchless in beauty and auspicious, / the excellent apsaras known by the name of Urvaśī, was seen by me.

1.133.s:
yataḥ prabhṛti cārvaṅgī tataḥ prabhṛti me sakhe ..
kāmenāloḍyate cittaṃ na ca śāmyati me tathā .. 11 ..
1.133.d:
यतः प्रभृति चार्वङ्गी ततः प्रभृति मे सखे ॥
कामेनालोड्यते चित्तं न च शाम्यति मे तथा ॥ 11 ॥
1.133.m: Ever since [I saw] that fair-limbed lady, my friend, from that time / my mind has been agitated by desire, and it does not find peace.”

1.133.s:
na copāyaṃ prapaśyāmi tasyā lābhe dvijottama ..
devatānāmapi śubhā durlabhā sā varāṅganā .. 12 ..
1.133.d:
न चोपायं प्रपश्यामि तस्या लाभे द्विजोत्तम ॥
देवतानामपि शुभा दुर्लभा सा वराङ्गना ॥ 12 ॥
1.133.m: And I see no means to win her, O best of the twice-born; / that auspicious, excellent woman is difficult to obtain even for the gods.

1.133.s:
evaṃ duḥkhaparītasya sakhe kālo gato mama ..
upabhuktā mayā svapne sādya cārvasitekṣaṇā .. 13 ..
1.133.d:
एवं दुःखपरीतस्य सखे कालो गतो मम ॥
उपभुक्ता मया स्वप्ने साद्य चार्वसितेक्षणा ॥ 13 ॥
1.133.m: Thus my time has passed, overcome by sorrow, my friend; / today she of lovely dark eyes was enjoyed by me in a dream.

1.133.s:
candrakāntagṛhe hyasminkāmamārgaṇatāḍitā ..
candrodaye cārumukhī trailokyasyaikasundarī .. 14 ..
1.133.d:
चन्द्रकान्तगृहे ह्यस्मिन्काममार्गणताडिता ॥
चन्द्रोदये चारुमुखी त्रैलोक्यस्यैकसुन्दरी ॥ 14 ॥
1.133.m: In this very moonstone palace, struck by love's arrows, / at moonrise, that lovely-faced woman, the sole beauty of the three worlds.

1.133.s:
vinodanārthaṃ hi sakhe manaso'ti manoharam ..
candrodaye tataḥ prāptaṃ candrakāntaśilāgṛham .. 15 ..
1.133.d:
विनोदनार्थं हि सखे मनसोऽति मनोहरम् ॥
चन्द्रोदये ततः प्राप्तं चन्द्रकान्तशिलागृहम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.133.m: Indeed, to entertain my mind, my friend, / at moonrise I have come to this exceedingly charming house of moonstone.

1.133.s:
tadehi tvasti saumya praviśya ruciraṃ gṛham ..
vinodayāmi hṛdayaṃ manmathena vaśīkṛtam .. 16 ..
1.133.d:
तदेहि त्वस्ति सौम्य प्रविश्य रुचिरं गृहम् ॥
विनोदयामि हृदयं मन्मथेन वशीकृतम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.133.m: So come, gentle friend; having entered this delightful pavilion, / I will divert my heart, which has been subjugated by Love.

1.133.s:
sakhovāca ..
yathā dṛṣṭaṃ tvayā svapne tathādya bhavitā dhuvam ..
sāpi kāmaparītāṅgī tvāmupeśyati bhāminī .. 17 ..
1.133.d:
सखोवाच ॥
यथा दृष्टं त्वया स्वप्ने तथाद्य भविता धुवम् ॥
सापि कामपरीताङ्गी त्वामुपेश्यति भामिनी ॥ 17 ॥
1.133.m: The friend said: / Just as it was seen by you in the dream, so it will certainly come to pass today; / she too, her limbs overcome by love, that passionate woman, will approach you.

1.133.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktvā viveśātha candrakāntaśilāgṛham ..
āsāñcakre tadā tasminmadanena vaśīkṛtaḥ .. 18 ...
1.133.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा विवेशाथ चन्द्रकान्तशिलागृहम् ॥
आसाञ्चक्रे तदा तस्मिन्मदनेन वशीकृतः ॥ 18 ॥।
1.133.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, he then entered the house of moonstone; / he sat down in it then, overcome by love.

1.133.s:
urvaśī rambhayā sārdhaṃ tacchrutvā harṣamāgatā ..
ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa rambhāpi nṛpatestadā .. 19 ..
1.133.d:
उर्वशी रम्भया सार्धं तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षमागता ॥
आत्मानं दर्शयामास रम्भापि नृपतेस्तदा ॥ 19 ॥
1.133.m: Urvaśī together with Rambhā, hearing that, felt joy; / Rambhā too then showed herself to the king.

1.133.s:
jayetyuktvā mahīnāthaṃ rambhā kāmavaśāttadā ...
babhūva puratastasya śobhayantīva tadgṛham .. 1.133.20..
1.133.d:
जयेत्युक्त्वा महीनाथं रम्भा कामवशात्तदा ॥।
बभूव पुरतस्तस्य शोभयन्तीव तद्गृहम् ॥ 1.133.20॥
1.133.m: Saying “Victory!” to the lord of the earth, Rambhā then, impelled by desire, / stood before him, as if illuminating that palace.

1.133.s:
tāmuvāca tato rājā svāgataṃ te varānane ..
alaṅkuruṣva cārvaṅgi ratnāsanamidaṃ śubham .. 21 ..
1.133.d:
तामुवाच ततो राजा स्वागतं ते वरानने ॥
अलङ्कुरुष्व चार्वङ्गि रत्नासनमिदं शुभम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.133.m: Then the king said to her: “Welcome to you, O fair-faced woman; / grace this auspicious jeweled seat, O lovely-limbed one.”

1.133.s:
ratnāsanopaviṣṭāyāṃ tadāgamanavismitaḥ ..
tadā rājīvaraktākṣastāmuvāca varānanām ..22..
1.133.d:
रत्नासनोपविष्टायां तदागमनविस्मितः ॥
तदा राजीवरक्ताक्षस्तामुवाच वराननाम् ॥22॥
1.133.m: When she was seated upon the jeweled seat, astonished at her arrival, / then the red-lotus-eyed king said to that fair-faced woman:

1.133.s:
śakrasya nagaraṃ rambhe rājate nityaśastvayā ..
paurṇamāsyā yathā rātriḥ śaśāṅkeneva bhāmini .. 23 ..
1.133.d:
शक्रस्य नगरं रम्भे राजते नित्यशस्त्वया ॥
पौर्णमास्या यथा रात्रिः शशाङ्केनेव भामिनि ॥ 23 ॥
1.133.m: “The city of Śakra is ever resplendent through you, O Rambhā, / as is the full-moon night through the moon, O passionate woman.

1.133.s:
tvaṃ sabhāmaṇḍanaṃ tasya sacchiṣyā tvaṃ ca tumburoḥ ..
tvayābhibhūtāssakalāḥ striyaḥ suptāḥ suśobhane .. 24 ..
1.133.d:
त्वं सभामण्डनं तस्य सच्छिष्या त्वं च तुम्बुरोः ॥
त्वयाभिभूतास्सकलाः स्त्रियः सुप्ताः सुशोभने ॥ 24 ॥
1.133.m: You are the ornament of his assembly, and you are the good disciple of Tumburu; / all the sleeping women have been surpassed by you, O exceedingly splendid one.

1.133.s:
tvayābhibhūtāḥ sakalāḥ striyaḥ svarge suśobhane ..
tava netrasahasreṇa paśyannapi tu pākahā .. 25 ..
1.133.d:
त्वयाभिभूताः सकलाः स्त्रियः स्वर्गे सुशोभने ॥
तव नेत्रसहस्रेण पश्यन्नपि तु पाकहा ॥ 25 ॥
1.133.m: All the women in heaven have been surpassed by you, O exceedingly splendid one; / even gazing with a thousand eyes upon you, the slayer of Pāka

1.133.s:
sarvatra cārusarvāṃgi na tṛpyati śubhānane ..
tanmamācakṣva subhage ihāgamanakāraṇam .. 26 ..
1.133.d:
सर्वत्र चारुसर्वांगि न तृप्यति शुभानने ॥
तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुभगे इहागमनकारणम् ॥ 26 ॥
1.133.m: is never satiated, O fair-faced woman whose every limb is lovely everywhere. / Therefore, tell me, O fortunate woman, the reason for your coming here.”

1.133.s:
rambhovāca ..
śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājanmamāgamanakāraṇam ..
śrutvā tacca narendrendra kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama .. 27 ..
1.133.d:
रम्भोवाच ॥
शृणुष्वावहितो राजन्ममागमनकारणम् ॥
श्रुत्वा तच्च नरेन्द्रेन्द्र कुरुष्व वचनं मम ॥ 27 ॥
1.133.m: Rambhā said: / “Listen attentively, O king, to the reason for my coming, / and having heard it, O Indra among kings, do my bidding.

1.133.s:
nārāyaṇasutā devī tatra trailokyasundarī ..
urvaśī nāma cārvaṅgī bhūmipāla sakhī mama .. 28 ..
1.133.d:
नारायणसुता देवी तत्र त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी ॥
उर्वशी नाम चार्वङ्गी भूमिपाल सखी मम ॥ 28 ॥
1.133.m: The goddess, daughter of Nārāyaṇa, the beauty of the three worlds, / named Urvaśī, of lovely limbs, O protector of the earth, is my friend.

1.133.s:
sā tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahendrasya sadane kāmamohitā ..
na śarma labhate bālā hāheti vadatī muhuḥ .. 29 ..
1.133.d:
सा त्वां दृष्ट्वा महेन्द्रस्य सदने काममोहिता ॥
न शर्म लभते बाला हाहेति वदती मुहुः ॥ 29 ॥
1.133.m: Having seen you in the abode of great Indra, bewitched by love, / the maiden finds no peace, crying repeatedly, ‘Alas! Alas!’

1.133.s:
sā tvadarthamanaṃgena mārgaṇairbhṛśapīḍitā ..
lāvaṇya śeṣā saṃvṛttā dinaiḥ katipayaiḥ śubhā .. 1.133.30 ..
1.133.d:
सा त्वदर्थमनंगेन मार्गणैर्भृशपीडिता ॥
लावण्य शेषा संवृत्ता दिनैः कतिपयैः शुभा ॥ 1.133.30 ॥
1.133.m: Severely afflicted by the bodiless god with his arrows for your sake, / in a few days that auspicious woman has been reduced to sheer loveliness alone.

1.133.s:
kṣāmakṣāmakapolā sā tvatsamarpitamānasā ..
madanenābhitaptāṃgī mānamutsṛjya bhāminī .. 31 ..
1.133.d:
क्षामक्षामकपोला सा त्वत्समर्पितमानसा ॥
मदनेनाभितप्तांगी मानमुत्सृज्य भामिनी ॥ 31 ॥
1.133.m: Her cheeks grown extremely wasted, her mind surrendered to you, / her limbs scorched by love, that proud woman, abandoning her pride,

1.133.s:
prasthitā sā mayā sārddhaṃ tava darśanalālasā ..
antarā nāradenoktā yatra tvaṃ prasthitā śubhe .. 32 ..
1.133.d:
प्रस्थिता सा मया सार्द्धं तव दर्शनलालसा ॥
अन्तरा नारदेनोक्ता यत्र त्वं प्रस्थिता शुभे ॥ 32 ॥
1.133.m: set out together with me, longing for the sight of you. / On the way, she was told by Nārada: ‘Where you have set out, O auspicious one,

1.133.s:
tatra tvayā tu vastavyaṃ samayena varānane ..
meṣadvayaṃ tu putratve yattvayā parikalpitam .. 33 ..
1.133.d:
तत्र त्वया तु वस्तव्यं समयेन वरानने ॥
मेषद्वयं तु पुत्रत्वे यत्त्वया परिकल्पितम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.133.m: there you must dwell only under a condition, O fair-faced woman: / the two rams which you have regarded as your sons,

1.133.s:
tattu te śayanābhyāśe sthāpayetsatataṃ yadi ..
sa rājā cārusarvāṅgi nagno nekṣeta bhāmini ..34..
1.133.d:
तत्तु ते शयनाभ्याशे स्थापयेत्सततं यदि ॥
स राजा चारुसर्वाङ्गि नग्नो नेक्षेत भामिनि ॥34॥
1.133.m: if he always keeps them near your bed; / and if that king, O fair in every limb, does not see you naked, O passionate woman;

1.133.s:
maithunaṃ cāpyakāmāyā nāsau te kartumarhati ..
ghṛtāhārā tathā tatra vasa tvaṃ subhage sadā .. 35 ..
1.133.d:
मैथुनं चाप्यकामाया नासौ ते कर्तुमर्हति ॥
घृताहारा तथा तत्र वस त्वं सुभगे सदा ॥ 35 ॥
1.133.m: nor should he engage in intercourse with you against your will; / and subsisting on ghee, dwell there always, O fortunate woman.

1.133.s:
ekasminnapyatikrānte samaye yadi pārthivam ..
na tyakṣyasi tadā saumye śilābhūtā bhaviṣyasi .. 36 ..
1.133.d:
एकस्मिन्नप्यतिक्रान्ते समये यदि पार्थिवम् ॥
न त्यक्ष्यसि तदा सौम्ये शिलाभूता भविष्यसि ॥ 36 ॥
1.133.m: If even a single condition is broken, and you do not abandon / the king, then, gentle one, you shall turn to stone.’

1.133.s:
etāni samayānyuktā nāradena sakhī mama..
tāni tvaṃ pratipadyasva bhajasva ca śubhānanām..37...
1.133.d:
एतानि समयान्युक्ता नारदेन सखी मम॥
तानि त्वं प्रतिपद्यस्व भजस्व च शुभाननाम्॥37॥।
1.133.m: These conditions were spoken by Nārada to my friend; / accept them and unite with that fair-faced woman.”

1.133.s:
purūravā uvāca ..
rambhe tavādya vākyena amṛteneva bhāmini ..
mṛtyorvaśamanuprāpto jīvito'smi śubhānane .. 38 ..
1.133.d:
पुरूरवा उवाच ॥
रम्भे तवाद्य वाक्येन अमृतेनेव भामिनि ॥
मृत्योर्वशमनुप्राप्तो जीवितोऽस्मि शुभानने ॥ 38 ॥
1.133.m: Purūravas said: / “Rambhā, by your word today, like nectar, O passionate one, / having fallen into the power of death, I have been revived, O fair-faced woman.

1.133.s:
mamāpi tatkṛte rambhe madanaḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ ..
dunoti hadayaṃ subhrūrdivārātramatandritaḥ .. 39 ..
1.133.d:
ममापि तत्कृते रम्भे मदनः शरवृष्टिभिः ॥
दुनोति हदयं सुभ्रूर्दिवारात्रमतन्द्रितः ॥ 39 ॥
1.133.m: For her sake, O Rambhā, Love with showers of arrows / torments my heart day and night without ceasing, O fair-browed one.

1.133.s:
sā tvaṃ jīvaya māṃ śīghraṃ darśayasva varāṅganām ..
sthāsyāmi samaye tasminyasminmāṃ vakṣyase śubhe .. 1.133.40..
1.133.d:
सा त्वं जीवय मां शीघ्रं दर्शयस्व वराङ्गनाम् ॥
स्थास्यामि समये तस्मिन्यस्मिन्मां वक्ष्यसे शुभे ॥ 1.133.40॥
1.133.m: Therefore, revive me quickly; show me that excellent woman; / I shall abide by whatever condition you tell me, O auspicious one.

1.133.s:
kṛtaṃ taṃ samayaṃ viddhi nāradena yadīritam..
anākrande nimagnasya mama kāmamahodadhau ..41..
1.133.d:
कृतं तं समयं विद्धि नारदेन यदीरितम्॥
अनाक्रन्दे निमग्नस्य मम काममहोदधौ ॥41॥
1.133.m: Know that agreement to be accepted, which was spoken by Nārada; / for me, submerged in the great ocean of desire without a protector,

1.133.s:
plavo bhava viśālākṣi prāṇadā bhava sundari ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. evamuktā narendreṇa rambhā cāntardadhe tadā .. 42 ..
1.133.d:
प्लवो भव विशालाक्षि प्राणदा भव सुन्दरि ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ एवमुक्ता नरेन्द्रेण रम्भा चान्तर्दधे तदा ॥ 42 ॥
1.133.m: be a raft, O wide-eyed one; be a giver of life, O beautiful lady.” / Mārkaṇḍeya said: Addressed thus by the king, Rambhā then vanished.

1.133.s:
urvaśīsahitā cātha darśayāmāsa sā nṛpam ..
jayetyuktvā narendraṃ tu tadā nārāyaṇātmajā .. 43 ..
1.133.d:
उर्वशीसहिता चाथ दर्शयामास सा नृपम् ॥
जयेत्युक्त्वा नरेन्द्रं तु तदा नारायणात्मजा ॥ 43 ॥
1.133.m: And then, accompanied by Urvaśī, she showed the king to her; / then saying “Victory!” to the king, that daughter of Nārāyaṇa,

1.133.s:
vrīḍitā puratastasthau tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ ..
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā prītimāpātha sa narendro mahādyutiḥ .. 44 ..
1.133.d:
व्रीडिता पुरतस्तस्थौ तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः ॥
तां दृष्ट्वा प्रीतिमापाथ स नरेन्द्रो महाद्युतिः ॥ 44 ॥
1.133.m: bashful, stood before that great-souled king. / Having seen her, that king of great splendor was filled with joy;

1.133.s:
pulakāṃcita sarvāṅgo varṇituṃ sā na śakyate ..
pāṇāvādāya trapitāmutsaṅge copaveśayat .. 45 ..
1.133.d:
पुलकांचित सर्वाङ्गो वर्णितुं सा न शक्यते ॥
पाणावादाय त्रपितामुत्सङ्गे चोपवेशयत् ॥ 45 ॥
1.133.m: all his limbs bristled with horripilation; she could not be adequately described. / Taking the bashful lady by the hand, he seated her on his lap.

1.133.s:
ratnāsanaṃ tathā bheje rambhāpi sumanoharam ..
tataścovāca vacanaṃ rājā muditamānasaḥ ..46..
1.133.d:
रत्नासनं तथा भेजे रम्भापि सुमनोहरम् ॥
ततश्चोवाच वचनं राजा मुदितमानसः ॥46॥
1.133.m: Rambhā also took a jeweled seat that was exceedingly delightful; / and then the king, his heart gladdened, spoke these words:

1.133.s:
purūravā uvāca ..
kāmadevaḥ prasanno'dya mamorvaśi varāvane ..
adya vedūmyadhikaṃ subhrūḥ śakrādātmānamātmanā..47..
1.133.d:
पुरूरवा उवाच ॥
कामदेवः प्रसन्नोऽद्य ममोर्वशि वरावने ॥
अद्य वेदूम्यधिकं सुभ्रूः शक्रादात्मानमात्मना॥47॥
1.133.m: Purūravas said: / “The god of love is pleased today with me, O Urvaśī, O fair-faced one; / today I deem myself superior even to Śakra, O fair-browed lady.

1.133.s:
trailokyarājyalābhe'pi kutaḥ sā me śubhe ratiḥ ..
ājñākāritvamāsādya yā tavādya sulocane .. 48 ..
1.133.d:
त्रैलोक्यराज्यलाभेऽपि कुतः सा मे शुभे रतिः ॥
आज्ञाकारित्वमासाद्य या तवाद्य सुलोचने ॥ 48 ॥
1.133.m: Even upon obtaining the sovereignty of the three worlds, whence would I find such delight, / O auspicious one, as I have today upon having become obedient to your command, O fair-eyed lady?”

1.133.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evaṃ vadati bhūpāle yayau rambhā varānanā ..
kṣaṇena meṣasahitā punaḥ prāptā nṛpāntikam .. 49 ..
1.133.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवं वदति भूपाले ययौ रम्भा वरानना ॥
क्षणेन मेषसहिता पुनः प्राप्ता नृपान्तिकम् ॥ 49 ॥
1.133.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / While the king was speaking thus, fair-faced Rambhā departed; / in a moment, accompanied by two rams, she returned to the king's presence.

1.133.s:
meṣau dattvā narendrasya rājānaṃ vākyamabravīt ..
rambhovāca ..
yāsyāmi laṅkāṃ rājendra tatra prāṇeśvaro mama ..1.133.50..
1.133.d:
मेषौ दत्त्वा नरेन्द्रस्य राजानं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
रम्भोवाच ॥
यास्यामि लङ्कां राजेन्द्र तत्र प्राणेश्वरो मम ॥1.133.50॥
1.133.m: Having given the two rams to the king, she spoke these words to the monarch; / Rambhā said: / “I shall go to Laṅkā, O king of kings; there is my life's lord,

1.133.s:
matpratīkṣaḥ sthitaḥ śrīmāndhanadasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ ..
nalakūbaranāmāsau trailokyaviditaḥ prabho ..51 ..
1.133.d:
मत्प्रतीक्षः स्थितः श्रीमान्धनदस्यात्मसंभवः ॥
नलकूबरनामासौ त्रैलोक्यविदितः प्रभो ॥51 ॥
1.133.m: the glorious son of Dhanada, waiting for me; / he is named Nalakūbara, renowned across the three worlds, O lord.

1.133.s:
yathā ceyaṃ sakhī mahyaṃ notkaṇṭhāṃ kurute śubhā ..
sakhījanasya svargyasya tathā kāryaṃ tvayānagha .. 52 ..
1.133.d:
यथा चेयं सखी मह्यं नोत्कण्ठां कुरुते शुभा ॥
सखीजनस्य स्वर्ग्यस्य तथा कार्यं त्वयानघ ॥ 52 ॥
1.133.m: And you must act, O sinless one, in such a way that this auspicious friend of mine / does not feel longing for her friends in heaven.”

1.133.s:
purūravā uvāca ..
yatiṣye'haṃ tathā kartuṃ nirvṛtā bhava mānade ..
ratnānyetānyupādāya nirgacchasva yathāsukham .. 53 ..
1.133.d:
पुरूरवा उवाच ॥
यतिष्येऽहं तथा कर्तुं निर्वृता भव मानदे ॥
रत्नान्येतान्युपादाय निर्गच्छस्व यथासुखम् ॥ 53 ॥
1.133.m: Purūravas said: / “I shall endeavor to do so; be at ease, O respectful lady; / taking these jewels, depart as you please.”

1.133.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktā tato rambhā nṛpateḥ prītikāraṇāt ..
ratnānyupādāya yayau khena laṅkāṃ mahāpurīm ..54..
1.133.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्ता ततो रम्भा नृपतेः प्रीतिकारणात् ॥
रत्नान्युपादाय ययौ खेन लङ्कां महापुरीम् ॥54॥
1.133.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having been spoken to thus, Rambhā then, to please the king, / took the jewels and went through the sky to the great city of Laṅkā.

1.133.s:
labdhvorvaśīṃ narendro'pi reme sa sahitastayā ..
yathā śacyā surārighno balavānpākaśāsanaḥ .. 55 ..
1.133.d:
लब्ध्वोर्वशीं नरेन्द्रोऽपि रेमे स सहितस्तया ॥
यथा शच्या सुरारिघ्नो बलवान्पाकशासनः ॥ 55 ॥
1.133.m: Having obtained Urvaśī, that lord of men also disported with her, / just as the mighty slayer of Pāka, slayer of the enemies of the gods, did with Śacī.

1.133.s:
saṃnyastabhāraḥ sa tu mantrimukhye reme tayā yādavasiṃhamukhya..
lakṣmyā sameto bhagavānananto yathā sa devo bhuvanasya goptā .. 56 ..
1.133.d:
संन्यस्तभारः स तु मन्त्रिमुख्ये रेमे तया यादवसिंहमुख्य॥
लक्ष्म्या समेतो भगवाननन्तो यथा स देवो भुवनस्य गोप्ता ॥ 56 ॥
