1.133.m: Having consigned his burden to his chief minister, he disported with her, O chief lion of the Yādavas, / just as the blessed, endless God, protector of the world, does united with Lakṣmī.

1.134.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
prāsādeṣu vicitreṣu tathā maṇigṛheṣu ca ..
puṣpaveśmasu ramyeṣu tathā vastragṛheṣu ca .. 1 ..
1.134.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
प्रासादेषु विचित्रेषु तथा मणिगृहेषु च ॥
पुष्पवेश्मसु रम्येषु तथा वस्त्रगृहेषु च ॥ 1 ॥
1.134.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / In variegated mansions, and likewise in jeweled houses, / in charming flower-pavilions, and likewise in cloth pavilions,

1.134.s:
ratnaveśmasu mukhyeṣu tathā citragṛheṣu ca ..
parvatānāṃ ca durgeṣu nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca .. 2 ..
1.134.d:
रत्नवेश्मसु मुख्येषु तथा चित्रगृहेषु च ॥
पर्वतानां च दुर्गेषु नदीनां पुलिनेषु च ॥ 2 ॥
1.134.m: in choice gem-pavilions, and likewise in painted houses, / in the mountain strongholds, and on the sandbanks of rivers,

1.134.s:
padminīṣu ca phullāsu tathā cotpalinīṣu ca ..
śayyāsu ca parārdhyāsu puṣpaśayyāsu cāpyatha.. 3..
1.134.d:
पद्मिनीषु च फुल्लासु तथा चोत्पलिनीषु च ॥
शय्यासु च परार्ध्यासु पुष्पशय्यासु चाप्यथ॥ 3॥
1.134.m: in blooming lotus pools, and likewise in blue-lotus pools, / and upon supreme couches, as well as couches of flowers,

1.134.s:
ramayāmāsa tāṃ devīṃ tathā viraciteṣu ca ..
gṛheṣu bahuratneṣu dhūpodgāriṣu pārthiva ..4..
1.134.d:
रमयामास तां देवीं तथा विरचितेषु च ॥
गृहेषु बहुरत्नेषु धूपोद्गारिषु पार्थिव ॥4॥
1.134.m: he delighted that goddess, and likewise in houses / fashioned with many jewels, sending forth incense, O king.

1.134.s:
reme sa tu tayā sārdhaṃ mānaseṣu punaḥpunaḥ ..
ramayam̐stāṃ varārohāṃ na tṛpyati sa nityaśaḥ .. 5 ..
1.134.d:
रेमे स तु तया सार्धं मानसेषु पुनःपुनः ॥
रमयम्̐स्तां वरारोहां न तृप्यति स नित्यशः ॥ 5 ॥
1.134.m: He disported with her again and again in their minds; / delighting that woman of lovely hips, he was never satiated.

1.134.s:
niśāsu ca sacandrāsu candrakāntataraṃ mukham ..
papau tasyā yathākāmaṃ narendraḥ sa narādhipa..6..
1.134.d:
निशासु च सचन्द्रासु चन्द्रकान्ततरं मुखम् ॥
पपौ तस्या यथाकामं नरेन्द्रः स नराधिप॥6॥
1.134.m: On moonlit nights, that lord of men, that king of mortals, / drank according to his desire her face that was lovelier than the moon.

1.134.s:
niśāsu naṣṭacandrāsu tanmukho dyotitaprabhe ..
deśe tāṃ ramayāmāsa rājā rājīvalocanaḥ..7..
1.134.d:
निशासु नष्टचन्द्रासु तन्मुखो द्योतितप्रभे ॥
देशे तां रमयामास राजा राजीवलोचनः॥7॥
1.134.m: On moonless nights, in places illuminated by the splendor of her face, / the lotus-eyed king delighted her.

1.134.s:
varṣayantī narendrasya sā tu kāmaṃ dinedine ..
adṛṣṭapūrveva śubhā bhavatyāyatalocanā ..8..
1.134.d:
वर्षयन्ती नरेन्द्रस्य सा तु कामं दिनेदिने ॥
अदृष्टपूर्वेव शुभा भवत्यायतलोचना ॥8॥
1.134.m: Raining desire upon the lord of men day after day, / that auspicious, large-eyed woman seemed as if never seen before.

1.134.s:
rājño dṛḍhaṃ sā dayitā tasyāśca dviguṇo nṛpaḥ ..
tayā'sau prīyate rājā tena sāpi varāṅganā .. 9 ..
1.134.d:
राज्ञो दृढं सा दयिता तस्याश्च द्विगुणो नृपः ॥
तयाऽसौ प्रीयते राजा तेन सापि वराङ्गना ॥ 9 ॥
1.134.m: She was deeply beloved of the king, and doubly so was the king of her; / the king was delighted by her, and that excellent woman was also [delighted] by him.

1.134.s:
varacandanadigdhāṅgau nānābharaṇabhūṣitau ..
remāte dampatī hṛṣṭau nānāratnāvabhūṣitau .. 1.134.10 ..
1.134.d:
वरचन्दनदिग्धाङ्गौ नानाभरणभूषितौ ॥
रेमाते दम्पती हृष्टौ नानारत्नावभूषितौ ॥ 1.134.10 ॥
1.134.m: Their limbs smeared with choice sandalwood, adorned with various ornaments, / the joyful couple disported, adorned with various jewels.

1.134.s:
alaṅkaroti tāṃ rājā svayameva kadācana ..
tayā'laṃkriyamāṇaśca prītimāpnotyanuttamām .. 11 ..
1.134.d:
अलङ्करोति तां राजा स्वयमेव कदाचन ॥
तयाऽलंक्रियमाणश्च प्रीतिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.134.m: Sometimes the king would adorn her himself, / and being adorned by her, he attained unsurpassed joy.

1.134.s:
vareṣu tau vicitreṣu remāte muditau bhṛśam ..
keśānsaṃśobhayantau tau kusumaistu parasparam .. 12 ..
1.134.d:
वरेषु तौ विचित्रेषु रेमाते मुदितौ भृशम् ॥
केशान्संशोभयन्तौ तौ कुसुमैस्तु परस्परम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.134.m: In choice, variegated [places], the two disported, greatly delighted, / adorning each other's hair with flowers.

1.134.s:
urvaśyabhyuditaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā ca grathitaṃ punaḥ ..
dhārayāmāsa śirasā premṇā pārthivasattamaḥ.. 13..
1.134.d:
उर्वश्यभ्युदितं पुष्पं तथा च ग्रथितं पुनः ॥
धारयामास शिरसा प्रेम्णा पार्थिवसत्तमः॥ 13॥
1.134.m: The flower presented and also woven by Urvaśī, / the best of kings wore on his head with love.

1.134.s:
patracchedena yām̐ścakre tilakānsa narādhipaḥ ..
tām̐śca sā dhārayāmāsa lalāṭe cāruhāsinī .. 14..
1.134.d:
पत्रच्छेदेन याम्̐श्चक्रे तिलकान्स नराधिपः ॥
ताम्̐श्च सा धारयामास ललाटे चारुहासिनी ॥ 14॥
1.134.m: The forehead-marks that the king made with leaf-patterns, / the sweet-smiling woman wore upon her forehead.

1.134.s:
evaṃ saṃkrīḍato rājñastayā saha sumadhyayā ..
babhūvustanayāḥ pañca nāmatastānnibodha me .. 15 ..
1.134.d:
एवं संक्रीडतो राज्ञस्तया सह सुमध्यया ॥
बभूवुस्तनयाः पञ्च नामतस्तान्निबोध मे ॥ 15 ॥
1.134.m: While the king thus sported with that slender-waisted woman, / five sons were born; learn them from me by name:
Āyu was the eldest, then the wise [Amāvasu], and after him another, Anāmaya; / Ayutāyu was the fourth, and Śatāyu was the fifth.

1.134.s: evaṃ tasyāḥ prasūtā vai yāti kāle manohare .. 17 ..
1.134.d: एवं तस्याः प्रसूता वै याति काले मनोहरे ॥ 17 ॥
1.134.m: As delightful time passed, she indeed gave birth [to them].

1.134.s:
gandharvamukhyāstu tadā sametā tayā vihīnā bhṛśamutsukāstu ..
tadāgamāyātha surendraloke yatra tadā cakruradīnasattvāḥ .. 18 ..
1.134.d:
गन्धर्वमुख्यास्तु तदा समेता तया विहीना भृशमुत्सुकास्तु ॥
तदागमायाथ सुरेन्द्रलोके यत्र तदा चक्रुरदीनसत्त्वाः ॥ 18 ॥
1.134.m: Then the foremost Gandharvas, having gathered, were exceedingly longing without her; / and those beings of undaunted spirit then made an effort in the world of the lord of gods for her return.

1.135.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
urvaśyāgamane yatnaṃ cakruste mantramuttamam ..
gandharvastūgrasenākhyastadā mantramabhāṣata .. 1 ..
1.135.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
उर्वश्यागमने यत्नं चक्रुस्ते मन्त्रमुत्तमम् ॥
गन्धर्वस्तूग्रसेनाख्यस्तदा मन्त्रमभाषत ॥ 1 ॥
1.135.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / They formulated an excellent plan to bring about Urvaśī's return. / Then the Gandharva named Ugrasena spoke a counsel:

1.135.s:
ugrasena uvāca ..
samayevasthitā tasminnurvaśī cārubhūṣaṇā ..
vyutkrāntasamayaṃ sā tu rājānaṃ tyakṣyate ca tam ..2 ..
1.135.d:
उग्रसेन उवाच ॥
समयेवस्थिता तस्मिन्नुर्वशी चारुभूषणा ॥
व्युत्क्रान्तसमयं सा तु राजानं त्यक्ष्यते च तम् ॥2 ॥
1.135.m: Ugrasena said: / Urvaśī of beautiful ornaments stands bound by an agreement; / she will abandon that king if he breaches the agreement.

1.135.s:
tamahaṃ vedmi samayaṃ tatra yāsyāmi cānagha ..
yuṣmatkāryaṃ kariṣyāmi sasahāyo na saṃśayaḥ .. 3 ..
1.135.d:
तमहं वेद्मि समयं तत्र यास्यामि चानघ ॥
युष्मत्कार्यं करिष्यामि ससहायो न संशयः ॥ 3 ॥
1.135.m: I know that agreement; and I shall go there, O sinless one. / With companions, I shall accomplish your purpose, without a doubt.

1.135.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktvā yayau tatra yatrāsau nṛpatiḥ sthitaḥ ..
rātrau jahāra meṣaṃ ca māyayā sa narādhipa .. 4 ..
1.135.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा ययौ तत्र यत्रासौ नृपतिः स्थितः ॥
रात्रौ जहार मेषं च मायया स नराधिप ॥ 4 ॥
1.135.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, he went to where that king was staying; / and at night, O ruler of men, he carried off a ram by means of illusion.

1.135.s:
meṣaṃ jñātvā hṛtaṃ devī rājānamidamabravīt ..
meṣo hṛto mahīpāla kenāpyaddhā suto mama .. 5 ..
1.135.d:
मेषं ज्ञात्वा हृतं देवी राजानमिदमब्रवीत् ॥
मेषो हृतो महीपाल केनाप्यद्धा सुतो मम ॥ 5 ॥
1.135.m: Knowing the ram had been taken, the goddess said this to the king: / 'The ram, indeed my son, has been carried off by someone, O protector of the earth!

1.135.s:
dvitīyaśca hṛto rājam̐stamānaya sutaṃ mama ..
evamuktastayā rājā nagna evātha saṃbhramāt .. 6 ..
1.135.d:
द्वितीयश्च हृतो राजम्̐स्तमानय सुतं मम ॥
एवमुक्तस्तया राजा नग्न एवाथ संभ्रमात् ॥ 6 ॥
1.135.m: And the second one has been carried off, O king! Bring back my son!' / Addressed thus by her, the king, in his haste, [went] naked as he was;

1.135.s:
utthāyānveṣaṇaṃ cakre meṣayoḥ puruṣarṣabha ..
athāpaśyata sā nagnaṃ rājānamasitekṣaṇā .. 7 ..
1.135.d:
उत्थायान्वेषणं चक्रे मेषयोः पुरुषर्षभ ॥
अथापश्यत सा नग्नं राजानमसितेक्षणा ॥ 7 ॥
1.135.m: rising up, he made a search for the two rams, O bull among men. / Then the dark-eyed woman saw the king naked.

1.135.s:
saṃsmṛtya nāradavacastirobhūtā babhūva sā ..
gandharvāṇāṃ yayau sāpi samīpaṃ duḥkhitā tadā .. 8 ..
1.135.d:
संस्मृत्य नारदवचस्तिरोभूता बभूव सा ॥
गन्धर्वाणां ययौ सापि समीपं दुःखिता तदा ॥ 8 ॥
1.135.m: Remembering Nārada's words, she vanished; / and she, sorrowful then, went near the Gandharvas.

1.135.s:
svargaṃ prāpya viśālākṣī nityaṃ nṛpaparāyaṇā ..
kāmanunnaśarīrāpi kālaṃ nayati sundarī .. 9..
1.135.d:
स्वर्गं प्राप्य विशालाक्षी नित्यं नृपपरायणा ॥
कामनुन्नशरीरापि कालं नयति सुन्दरी ॥ 9॥
1.135.m: Having reached heaven, the wide-eyed woman, ever devoted to the king, / spent her time, her body stricken with desire, lovely as she was.

1.135.s:
ṛṣiśāpabhayādbhītā madanena vaśīkṛtā ..
nityamāsa varārohā niḥśvāsaparamā satī . 1.135.10 ..
1.135.d:
ऋषिशापभयाद्भीता मदनेन वशीकृता ॥
नित्यमास वरारोहा निःश्वासपरमा सती । 1.135.10 ॥
1.135.m: Terrified by fear of the sage's curse, subdued by love, / that virtuous woman of lovely hips remained constantly given to deep sighs.

1.135.s:
aprāpya meṣayugalaṃ vinivṛtto narādhipaḥ ..
nāpaśyacchayane devīṃ sasmāra samayaṃ tadā ..11..
1.135.d:
अप्राप्य मेषयुगलं विनिवृत्तो नराधिपः ॥
नापश्यच्छयने देवीं सस्मार समयं तदा ॥11॥
1.135.m: Not finding the pair of rams, the lord of men returned; / he did not see the goddess on the couch, and then he remembered the agreement.

1.135.s:
viditvā tyaktamātmānaṃ smṛtvā samayamātmanaḥ ..
kāmabāṇārdito rājā tathāpi vijane vane..12..
1.135.d:
विदित्वा त्यक्तमात्मानं स्मृत्वा समयमात्मनः ॥
कामबाणार्दितो राजा तथापि विजने वने॥12॥
1.135.m: Knowing himself abandoned, remembering his own agreement, / the king, tormented by the arrows of desire, nonetheless in the desolate forest

1.135.s:
tāṃ mārgati varārohāmunmatta iva sarvataḥ ..
ekākī vijane rājā priyayā rahitastadā .. 13 ..
1.135.d:
तां मार्गति वरारोहामुन्मत्त इव सर्वतः ॥
एकाकी विजने राजा प्रियया रहितस्तदा ॥ 13 ॥
1.135.m: sought that woman of lovely hips everywhere like one mad. / Alone in the desolate place, deprived of his beloved,

1.135.s:
vilalāpa mahāsattvaḥ kusattva iva kaścana ..
purūravā uvāca ..
kva gatāsi viśālākṣi vihāya vijanetra mām..14..
1.135.d:
विललाप महासत्त्वः कुसत्त्व इव कश्चन ॥
पुरूरवा उवाच ॥
क्व गतासि विशालाक्षि विहाय विजनेत्र माम्॥14॥
1.135.m: the king of great courage lamented like someone of weak spirit: / Purūravas said: / 'Where have you gone, O wide-eyed one, abandoning me here in the desolate place?

1.135.s:
kathaṃ pravekṣyāmi puraṃ pratiṣṭhānaṃ vinā tvayā ..
prāṇāstyaktvā gamiṣyanti śarīraṃ mama sundari .. 15 ..
1.135.d:
कथं प्रवेक्ष्यामि पुरं प्रतिष्ठानं विना त्वया ॥
प्राणास्त्यक्त्वा गमिष्यन्ति शरीरं मम सुन्दरि ॥ 15 ॥
1.135.m: How shall I enter the city of Pratiṣṭhāna without you? / Abandoning my body, my life-breaths will depart, O beautiful one!

1.135.s:
anugantuṃ śarīreṇa na śaknomi varānane ..
tvaṃ hi me capalāpāṅgi prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī .. 16 ..
1.135.d:
अनुगन्तुं शरीरेण न शक्नोमि वरानने ॥
त्वं हि मे चपलापाङ्गि प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी ॥ 16 ॥
1.135.m: I cannot follow you with my body, O fair-faced one! / For to me, O woman with glancing eyes, you are dearer than life itself.

1.135.s:
tvayā tyakto dhruvaṃ prāṇām̐styakṣyāmi varavarṇini ..
kvāsi kvāhaṃ gamiṣyāmi kiṃ karomi vrajāmi kām .. 17 ..
1.135.d:
त्वया त्यक्तो ध्रुवं प्राणाम्̐स्त्यक्ष्यामि वरवर्णिनि ॥
क्वासि क्वाहं गमिष्यामि किं करोमि व्रजामि काम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.135.m: Abandoned by you, I shall surely abandon my life-breaths, O woman of excellent complexion! / Where are you? Where shall I go? What shall I do? To whom shall I turn?

1.135.s:
śaraṇaṃ kāmataptasya ko me saṃdarśayetpriyām ..
kaṃ svitpṛcchāmi vijane kasya sā viditā bhavet .. 18 ..
1.135.d:
शरणं कामतप्तस्य को मे संदर्शयेत्प्रियाम् ॥
कं स्वित्पृच्छामि विजने कस्य सा विदिता भवेत् ॥ 18 ॥
1.135.m: Who will show my beloved to me, afflicted by desire, seeking refuge? / Whom indeed shall I ask in this desolate place? To whom might she be known?

1.135.s:
kṣemo vā mama kasya syādyo me saṃdarśayetpriyām ..
priyāvirahitasyaiṣa niśāśeṣo gato mama .. 39 ..
1.135.d:
क्षेमो वा मम कस्य स्याद्यो मे संदर्शयेत्प्रियाम् ॥
प्रियाविरहितस्यैष निशाशेषो गतो मम ॥ 39 ॥
1.135.m: Or from whom could safety come to me, who would show my beloved to me? / Deprived of my beloved, this remainder of the night has passed for me.

1.135.s:
antardhānaṃ gatāstārā yathā devī mamorvaśī ..
devo'ruṇakarasparśācchobhāṃ tyajati candramāḥ .. 1.135.20 ..
1.135.d:
अन्तर्धानं गतास्तारा यथा देवी ममोर्वशी ॥
देवोऽरुणकरस्पर्शाच्छोभां त्यजति चन्द्रमाः ॥ 1.135.20 ॥
1.135.m: The stars have vanished, just as my goddess Urvaśī has; / touched by the rays of the dawn, the divine moon loses its splendor,

1.135.s:
niśākṣaye kṣāmavapuryathāhaṃ tadvinākṛtaḥ ..
eṣā hyāvartate pūrvā sandhyā snātvā dvijātayaḥ .. 21 ..
1.135.d:
निशाक्षये क्षामवपुर्यथाहं तद्विनाकृतः ॥
एषा ह्यावर्तते पूर्वा सन्ध्या स्नात्वा द्विजातयः ॥ 21 ॥
1.135.m: with an emaciated form at the end of night, just as I, deprived of her. / For this eastern twilight returns; having bathed, the twice-born

1.135.s:
nūnaṃ niyamasaṃyuktāstiṣṭhanti vijitendriyāḥ ..
ayaṃ hyudayamāyāti savitā raktamaṇḍalaḥ .. 22 ..
1.135.d:
नूनं नियमसंयुक्तास्तिष्ठन्ति विजितेन्द्रियाः ॥
अयं ह्युदयमायाति सविता रक्तमण्डलः ॥ 22 ॥
1.135.m: surely stand observing their vows, with their senses subdued. / For here rises the sun with its crimson disc.'

1.135.s:
sarvasattvasamo devaḥ sarveṣāṃ pāpanāśanaḥ ..
uditaścāpyayaṃ sūryo vibhāti vimalembare .. 23 ..
1.135.d:
सर्वसत्त्वसमो देवः सर्वेषां पापनाशनः ॥
उदितश्चाप्ययं सूर्यो विभाति विमलेम्बरे ॥ 23 ॥
1.135.m: The god who is impartial to all beings, the destroyer of sins for all, / and now this sun has risen and shines in the clear sky,

1.135.s:
ekaṃ phullaṃ mahāpadmaṃ sarasīvāmale yathā ..
uditaṃ bhāskaraṃ jñātvā nalinīpadmalocanā .. 24 ..
1.135.d:
एकं फुल्लं महापद्मं सरसीवामले यथा ॥
उदितं भास्करं ज्ञात्वा नलिनीपद्मलोचना ॥ 24 ॥
1.135.m: like a single, great blooming lotus in a clear lake. / Having known that the sun has risen, lotus-eyed woman, the lotus cluster,

1.135.s:
unmīlyālokate sarvaṃ vinā tena nimīlitā ..
tīkṣṇārkaḥ saṃpravṛtto'yaṃ divasaḥ kāmavardhanaḥ .. 25 ..
1.135.d:
उन्मील्यालोकते सर्वं विना तेन निमीलिता ॥
तीक्ष्णार्कः संप्रवृत्तोऽयं दिवसः कामवर्धनः ॥ 25 ॥
1.135.m: opening, beholds everything; without him, she is closed. / This day of the fierce sun has begun, increasing love.

1.135.s:
naidāgho māṃ viśeṣeṇa santāpayati tāṃ vinā ..
kaṃ pṛcchāmi varārohāṃ saṃtaptakanakaprabhām .. 26 ..
1.135.d:
नैदाघो मां विशेषेण सन्तापयति तां विना ॥
कं पृच्छामि वरारोहां संतप्तकनकप्रभाम् ॥ 26 ॥
1.135.m: The summer heat torments me especially, without her. / Whom shall I ask about the fair-hipped woman, radiant as molten gold?

1.135.s:
dṛṣṭā mayeti sā devī ko māṃ vakṣyati kānane ..
karīndrastvayamabhyeti tatkucābhau samudvahan .. 27 ..
1.135.d:
दृष्टा मयेति सा देवी को मां वक्ष्यति कानने ॥
करीन्द्रस्त्वयमभ्येति तत्कुचाभौ समुद्वहन् ॥ 27 ॥
1.135.m: 'She has been seen by me,' who will tell me thus of that lady in the forest? / Here comes the lordly elephant, bearing [two frontal globes] resembling her breasts,

1.135.s:
kumbhau kaṭhorau sumukhaṃ pṛcchāmyenaṃ mataṅgajam ..
tvaddantayugalaprakhyaṃ yadūruyugalaṃ hyabhūt .. 28 ..
1.135.d:
कुम्भौ कठोरौ सुमुखं पृच्छाम्येनं मतङ्गजम् ॥
त्वद्दन्तयुगलप्रख्यं यदूरुयुगलं ह्यभूत् ॥ 28 ॥
1.135.m: two firm frontal lobes; I ask this handsome-faced elephant: / 'Her pair of thighs was indeed like your pair of tusks;

1.135.s:
gatāṃ tāṃ yadi jānīṣe kathayasva mamorvaśīm ..
eṣa hastī gatastrāsātsiṃhasyāsya mahātmanaḥ .. 29..
1.135.d:
गतां तां यदि जानीषे कथयस्व ममोर्वशीम् ॥
एष हस्ती गतस्त्रासात्सिंहस्यास्य महात्मनः ॥ 29॥
1.135.m: if you know where she has gone, tell me of my Urvaśī.' / This elephant has fled out of fear from this mighty lion.

1.135.s:
adattvaivottaraṃ mahyaṃ siṃhaṃ pṛcchāmyahaṃ vane ..
madhyastvadupamastasyāḥ kva sā samprati kesarin ..1.135.30..
1.135.d:
अदत्त्वैवोत्तरं मह्यं सिंहं पृच्छाम्यहं वने ॥
मध्यस्त्वदुपमस्तस्याः क्व सा सम्प्रति केसरिन् ॥1.135.30॥
1.135.m: Without giving me any answer at all! I will ask the lion in the forest: / 'Her waist is like yours; where is she now, O maned beast?

1.135.s:
urvaśī dayitā mahyaṃ yadi jānāsi kathyatām ..
adattvaivottaraṃ siṃhaḥ kathameṣa gato mama .. 31 ..
1.135.d:
उर्वशी दयिता मह्यं यदि जानासि कथ्यताम् ॥
अदत्त्वैवोत्तरं सिंहः कथमेष गतो मम ॥ 31 ॥
1.135.m: If you know of Urvaśī, my beloved, let it be told!' / Without giving me any answer, how has this lion departed?

1.135.s:
dṛṣṭā kathaya he bimba devīṃ bimbaphalādharām ..
anenāpi na cākhyātā pṛṣṭena sudatī mama .. 32 ..
1.135.d:
दृष्टा कथय हे बिम्ब देवीं बिम्बफलाधराम् ॥
अनेनापि न चाख्याता पृष्टेन सुदती मम ॥ 32 ॥
1.135.m: Tell me, O bimba fruit, have you seen the lady whose lips are like a bimba fruit? / Even questioned by me, he too has not told me of my sweet-toothed love.

1.135.s:
mayūra yadi jānīṣe bālāṃ bālamṛgekṣaṇām ..
urvaśīṃ kathayasvādya kva priyā mama vartate .. 33 ..
1.135.d:
मयूर यदि जानीषे बालां बालमृगेक्षणाम् ॥
उर्वशीं कथयस्वाद्य क्व प्रिया मम वर्तते ॥ 33 ॥
1.135.m: O peacock, if you know the young maiden with eyes like a young deer, / tell me today of Urvaśī: where does my beloved dwell?

1.135.s:
antaḥśarīraṃ kāmāgnirbahirdahati bhāskaraḥ ..
tāpārttā niḥśvasantyete siṃhā giriguhāgatāḥ .. 34 ..
1.135.d:
अन्तःशरीरं कामाग्निर्बहिर्दहति भास्करः ॥
तापार्त्ता निःश्वसन्त्येते सिंहा गिरिगुहागताः ॥ 34 ॥
1.135.m: The fire of love burns within my body; the sun burns outside. / Tormented by the heat, these lions residing in mountain caves gasp for breath,

1.135.s:
nirastajihvāḥ srastāṅgā vivṛtāsyā muhurmuhuḥ ..
yūthāni mahiṣīṇāṃ ca śerate nalinījale .. 35 ..
1.135.d:
निरस्तजिह्वाः स्रस्ताङ्गा विवृतास्या मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
यूथानि महिषीणां च शेरते नलिनीजले ॥ 35 ॥
1.135.m: with tongues hanging out, limbs limp, mouths gaping repeatedly. / And herds of buffalo cows lie in the lotus-covered water;

1.135.s:
sūryoddhatajalāsvanye paṅkaśeṣā su śerate ..
gaganaṃ cātakaścāyaṃ tṛṣṇārto lokate muhuḥ .. 36 ..
1.135.d:
सूर्योद्धतजलास्वन्ये पङ्कशेषा सु शेरते ॥
गगनं चातकश्चायं तृष्णार्तो लोकते मुहुः ॥ 36 ॥
1.135.m: others lie where the water has been dried up by the sun, where only mud remains. / And this cātaka bird, afflicted with thirst, gazes repeatedly at the sky,

1.135.s:
su bhṛśaṃ toyapānārthī urvaśyarthe yathā tvaham ..
yāntyete padminī khaṇḍānkuñjarāstāparūṣitāḥ .. 37 ..
1.135.d:
सु भृशं तोयपानार्थी उर्वश्यर्थे यथा त्वहम् ॥
यान्त्येते पद्मिनी खण्डान्कुञ्जरास्तापरूषिताः ॥ 37 ॥
1.135.m: greatly longing to drink water, just as I yearn for Urvaśī. / Smeared with the heat, these elephants go to clumps of lotuses;

1.135.s:
suhastamuktaiśca jalaiḥ siṃcantyātmānamātmanā ..
mahādrumāṇāṃ skandheṣu viṣaṇṇāścāpare gajāḥ .. 38 ..
1.135.d:
सुहस्तमुक्तैश्च जलैः सिंचन्त्यात्मानमात्मना ॥
महाद्रुमाणां स्कन्धेषु विषण्णाश्चापरे गजाः ॥ 38 ॥
1.135.m: with waters released by their trunks, they sprinkle themselves by themselves. / And other dejected elephants at the trunks of great trees

1.135.s:
tāpaṃ nayanti madhyāhne muñcantaḥ śīkaraṃ muhuḥ ..
śākhāparṇāntarāṇyete vihagāstāpatāpitāḥ .. 39 ..
1.135.d:
तापं नयन्ति मध्याह्ने मुञ्चन्तः शीकरं मुहुः ॥
शाखापर्णान्तराण्येते विहगास्तापतापिताः ॥ 39 ॥
1.135.m: endure the heat at midday, repeatedly discharging spray. / Scorched by the heat, these birds

1.135.s:
viśanti caiva trāṇārthaṃ madhyāhnasamaye bhṛśam ..
drumaśākhāgatā hyete vihagānāṃ ca bālakāḥ .. 1.135.40 ..
1.135.d:
विशन्ति चैव त्राणार्थं मध्याह्नसमये भृशम् ॥
द्रुमशाखागता ह्येते विहगानां च बालकाः ॥ 1.135.40 ॥
1.135.m: enter the space between the leafy branches exceedingly for protection at midday. / Resting upon the branches of trees, these young of birds,

1.135.s:
raktāntacakrāḥ subhṛśaṃ viśantīha muhurmuhuḥ ..
tyaktāhārakriyāścaite mṛgayūthā mahāvane .. 41 ..
1.135.d:
रक्तान्तचक्राः सुभृशं विशन्तीह मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
त्यक्ताहारक्रियाश्चैते मृगयूथा महावने ॥ 41 ॥
1.135.m: having circles with red edges, enter here repeatedly in great numbers. / And abandoning the act of grazing, these herds of deer in the great forest

1.135.s:
drumacchāyāsu tiṣṭhanti romanthaṃ kurvuto muhuḥ ..
anveṣamāṇo dayitāṃ śrīto'smi vijaye bhṛśam .. 42 ..
1.135.d:
द्रुमच्छायासु तिष्ठन्ति रोमन्थं कुर्वुतो मुहुः ॥
अन्वेषमाणो दयितां श्रीतोऽस्मि विजये भृशम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.135.m: stand in the shade of the trees, chewing the cud again and again. / Searching for my beloved, I am exceedingly exhausted in my quest.

1.135.s:
chāyāyāṃ viśramiṣyāmi śirīṣasyāsya sāmpratam ..
tadgātrasukumārāṇi puṣpāṇyasya vanaspateḥ .. 43 ..
1.135.d:
छायायां विश्रमिष्यामि शिरीषस्यास्य साम्प्रतम् ॥
तद्गात्रसुकुमाराणि पुष्पाण्यस्य वनस्पतेः ॥ 43 ॥
1.135.m: I shall rest now in the shade of this śirīṣa tree; / the flowers of this lord of the forest are as delicate as her limbs.

1.135.s:
śirīṣavṛkṣo ramyo'yaṃ manohṛdayanandanaḥ..
kintu māṃ pīḍayatyeṣa śirīṣastadvinākṛtam .. 44 ..
1.135.d:
शिरीषवृक्षो रम्योऽयं मनोहृदयनन्दनः॥
किन्तु मां पीडयत्येष शिरीषस्तद्विनाकृतम् ॥ 44 ॥
1.135.m: This charming śirīṣa tree brings delight to mind and heart; / but this śirīṣa torments me who am deprived of her.

1.135.s:
sūryaścāstamupāyāti kva gamiṣyāmi śarvarīm ..
astaṃ yātaḥ sahasrāṃśurniśā prāptā sudāruṇā..45..
1.135.d:
सूर्यश्चास्तमुपायाति क्व गमिष्यामि शर्वरीम् ॥
अस्तं यातः सहस्रांशुर्निशा प्राप्ता सुदारुणा॥45॥
1.135.m: And the sun goes to setting; where shall I spend the night? / The thousand-rayed one has set; the very dreadful night has arrived.

1.135.s:
rātrimenāṃ vivatsyāmi nyagrodhe'sminmahādrume ..
urvaśyā ṛddhiracite varaveśmani pārthivaḥ .. 46 ..
1.135.d:
रात्रिमेनां विवत्स्यामि न्यग्रोधेऽस्मिन्महाद्रुमे ॥
उर्वश्या ऋद्धिरचिते वरवेश्मनि पार्थिवः ॥ 46 ॥
1.135.m: I will spend this night in this great banyan tree. / In the excellent palace fashioned by Urvaśī's supernatural power, the king

1.135.s:
sa krīḍati tayā sārdhaṃ sarvakāmaiḥ supūjitaḥ ..
nūnaṃ māṃ sa jano vetti pratiṣṭhānapure tu me .. 47 ..
1.135.d:
स क्रीडति तया सार्धं सर्वकामैः सुपूजितः ॥
नूनं मां स जनो वेत्ति प्रतिष्ठानपुरे तु मे ॥ 47 ॥
1.135.m: plays with her, thoroughly honoured with all desired pleasures: / surely those people in my city of Pratiṣṭhāna think of me [in that way].

1.135.s:
etāmavasthāṃ kaścinme na vijānāti sāmpratam ..
pauro jānapadaḥ kaścijjano me dayitaḥ sadā .. 48 ..
1.135.d:
एतामवस्थां कश्चिन्मे न विजानाति साम्प्रतम् ॥
पौरो जानपदः कश्चिज्जनो मे दयितः सदा ॥ 48 ॥
1.135.m: No one now knows this state of mine— / whether citizen or countryman, who are always dear to me.

1.135.s:
nidre bhajasva mannetre dhruvaṃ svapne varānanāma ..
tāṃ tu prāpsyāmyahaṃ saumyāṃ manasaḥ prītivardhinīm .. 49 ..
1.135.d:
निद्रे भजस्व मन्नेत्रे ध्रुवं स्वप्ने वराननाम ॥
तां तु प्राप्स्याम्यहं सौम्यां मनसः प्रीतिवर्धिनीम् ॥ 49 ॥
1.135.m: O Sleep, visit my eyes! Surely in a dream that fair-faced lady, / gentle, increasing the delight of my mind, will be reached by me.

1.135.s:
kathamabhyuditaścandraḥ pīḍāṃ janayate mama ..
tadvaktravijitaḥ pūrvaṃ vikarotyadhunā mayi .. 1.135.50 ..
1.135.d:
कथमभ्युदितश्चन्द्रः पीडां जनयते मम ॥
तद्वक्त्रविजितः पूर्वं विकरोत्यधुना मयि ॥ 1.135.50 ॥
1.135.m: How is it that the risen moon produces torment in me? / Conquered by her face formerly, he now wreaks hostility upon me.

1.135.s:
tuda candra yathākāmaṃ mama dehaṃ vinākṛtam ..
tvayā tu nāthaṃ saṃprāpya sāpatnyaṃ mama darśaya .. 51 ..
1.135.d:
तुद चन्द्र यथाकामं मम देहं विनाकृतम् ॥
त्वया तु नाथं संप्राप्य सापत्न्यं मम दर्शय ॥ 51 ॥
1.135.m: Pierce, O moon, at will, my body that is bereft [of her]! / Having found a protector in you, show your rivalry towards me!

1.135.s:
hā hato'smi vinaṣṭo'smi urvaśyā rahito vane ..
candra pautre kuru dayāṃ darśayasva mama priyām .. 52 ..
1.135.d:
हा हतोऽस्मि विनष्टोऽस्मि उर्वश्या रहितो वने ॥
चन्द्र पौत्रे कुरु दयां दर्शयस्व मम प्रियाम् ॥ 52 ॥
1.135.m: Alas, I am undone! I am ruined, bereft of Urvaśī in the forest! / O moon, show mercy to your grandson; show me my beloved!

1.135.s:
śaśāṅka deva śītāṃśo nṛṇāṃ dṛṣṭimanohara ..
ākrandāmi tavādyāhaṃ darśayasva priyāṃ mama .. 53 ..
1.135.d:
शशाङ्क देव शीतांशो नृणां दृष्टिमनोहर ॥
आक्रन्दामि तवाद्याहं दर्शयस्व प्रियां मम ॥ 53 ॥
1.135.m: O god Moon, cool-rayed one, captivating the sight of men! / I cry out to you today: show me my beloved!

1.135.s:
atṛpta darśanasyaiva sā gatā sundarī mama ..
antardhānaṃ viśālākṣī tāṃ darśaya mamorvaśīm ..54 ..
1.135.d:
अतृप्त दर्शनस्यैव सा गता सुन्दरी मम ॥
अन्तर्धानं विशालाक्षी तां दर्शय ममोर्वशीम् ॥54 ॥
1.135.m: While my sight was yet unsated, that beautiful woman of mine vanished, / the large-eyed one! Show me that Urvaśī of mine!

1.135.s:
kadā'dhararasaṃ tasyāḥ pāsyāmyamṛtasannibham ..
kadā draṣṭāsmi tāṃ bhūyaḥ kamalodarasannibhām ..55..
1.135.d:
कदाऽधररसं तस्याः पास्याम्यमृतसन्निभम् ॥
कदा द्रष्टास्मि तां भूयः कमलोदरसन्निभाम् ॥55॥
1.135.m: When shall I drink the nectar of her lip, which is like ambrosia? / When shall I see her again, whose colour is like the interior of a lotus?

1.135.s:
mṛṇālabāhuyugalāṃ padmavaktrāṃ kadā priyām ..
nīlotpalākṣīmāliṅgya tāpaṃ tyakṣyāmyanaṅgajam..56..
1.135.d:
मृणालबाहुयुगलां पद्मवक्त्रां कदा प्रियाम् ॥
नीलोत्पलाक्षीमालिङ्ग्य तापं त्यक्ष्याम्यनङ्गजम्॥56॥
1.135.m: When, embracing my beloved who has lotus-stalk arms, / a lotus face, and eyes like blue water-lilies, shall I cast off the heat born of the Bodiless One?

1.135.s:
anaṅgaśaranunnasya bāle bhava gatirmama ..
dadasva darśanaṃ subhrūḥ kā mamānyā gatirbhavet ..57 ..
1.135.d:
अनङ्गशरनुन्नस्य बाले भव गतिर्मम ॥
ददस्व दर्शनं सुभ्रूः का ममान्या गतिर्भवेत् ॥57 ॥
1.135.m: O young woman, be the refuge of me struck by the arrows of the Bodiless One! / Grant your sight, O fair-browed one! What other refuge could there be for me?

1.135.s:
kāmamohagṛhītasya tvamevābhūrgatirmama ..
bhūyastvameva subhage gatirbhava mamānaghe .. 58 ..
1.135.d:
काममोहगृहीतस्य त्वमेवाभूर्गतिर्मम ॥
भूयस्त्वमेव सुभगे गतिर्भव ममानघे ॥ 58 ॥
1.135.m: For me seized by the infatuation of love, you alone were my refuge. / Once more, O fortunate one, be my refuge, O faultless lady!

1.135.s:
eṣā viralitā rātrirmama varṣaśatopamā ..
anveṣṭuṃ kva gamiṣyāmi nirghṛṇāṃ tāṃ mamopari .. 59 ..
1.135.d:
एषा विरलिता रात्रिर्मम वर्षशतोपमा ॥
अन्वेष्टुं क्व गमिष्यामि निर्घृणां तां ममोपरि ॥ 59 ॥
1.135.m: This night has faded, which was like a hundred years to me. / Where shall I go to search for her who is pitiless toward me?

1.135.s:
yasyāḥ kopaṃ na jānāmi svapne'pi varavarṇini ..
daivenopahatasyādya tyaktā sā subhagā gatā .. 1.135.60 ..
1.135.d:
यस्याः कोपं न जानामि स्वप्नेऽपि वरवर्णिनि ॥
दैवेनोपहतस्याद्य त्यक्ता सा सुभगा गता ॥ 1.135.60 ॥
1.135.m: Whose anger I did not know even in a dream, O fair-complexioned one! / Struck down by fate today, that lovely woman has left and gone.

1.135.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evaṃ sa vilapanrājā tyaktāhāraḥ paribhraman .
āsasāda kurukṣetraṃ dvādaśāhena pārthiva..61..
1.135.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवं स विलपन्राजा त्यक्ताहारः परिभ्रमन् ।
आससाद कुरुक्षेत्रं द्वादशाहेन पार्थिव॥61॥
1.135.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Thus that king, lamenting, giving up food, wandering about, / reached Kurukṣetra in twelve days, O ruler of the earth.

1.135.s:
puṣkariṇyāstaṭaplakṣe puṣkarairupaśobhite .
niṣasāda tadā śrāntaḥ kṣutpipāsāsamanvitaḥ..
vilalāpa sa tatrāpi madanena vaśīkṛtaḥ .. 62 ..
1.135.d:
पुष्करिण्यास्तटप्लक्षे पुष्करैरुपशोभिते ।
निषसाद तदा श्रान्तः क्षुत्पिपासासमन्वितः॥
विललाप स तत्रापि मदनेन वशीकृतः ॥ 62 ॥
1.135.m: On the plakṣa tree on the bank of a lotus pond, adorned with blue lotuses, / he sat down then, exhausted, beset with hunger and thirst; / there too he lamented, overpowered by love:

1.135.s:
kadā nu taccandramaso'nukānti mukhaṃ smitaṃ cāruvilocanāyāḥ..
unnāmya pāsyāmyadharaṃ tṛṣārto vārīva pānthaḥ pathi kṛcchralabhyam .. 63 ..
1.135.d:
कदा नु तच्चन्द्रमसोऽनुकान्ति मुखं स्मितं चारुविलोचनायाः॥
उन्नाम्य पास्याम्यधरं तृषार्तो वारीव पान्थः पथि कृच्छ्रलभ्यम् ॥ 63 ॥
1.135.m: "When indeed, having lifted up the smiling face resembling the beauty of the moon of that lady of lovely eyes, / shall I, afflicted by thirst, drink her lower lip, as a traveler on a path drinks water obtained with difficulty?"

1.136.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
urvaśyapi varārohā madanenābhipīḍitā ..
jagāda nāradasyātha svāmavasthāṃ nṛpaṃ vinā .. 1 ..
1.136.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
उर्वश्यपि वरारोहा मदनेनाभिपीडिता ॥
जगाद नारदस्याथ स्वामवस्थां नृपं विना ॥ 1 ॥
1.136.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Urvaśī also, the fair-hipped lady, intensely tormented by love, / then spoke of her own condition without the king to Nārada:

1.136.s:
tatastāṃ nāradaḥ prāha subhage gaccha pārthivam ..
tasyāpyavasthā mahatī tvadvihīnasya sundari ..2 ..
1.136.d:
ततस्तां नारदः प्राह सुभगे गच्छ पार्थिवम् ॥
तस्याप्यवस्था महती त्वद्विहीनस्य सुन्दरि ॥2 ॥
1.136.m: Then Nārada said to her: "O fortunate woman, go to the king. / Great also is his plight, deprived of you, O beautiful woman.

1.136.s:
ekāṃ rātriṃ narendreṇa sahoṣya varavarṇini ..
svargalokamupāgaccha śreyaḥ prāpsyasi vai tataḥ .. 3 ..
1.136.d:
एकां रात्रिं नरेन्द्रेण सहोष्य वरवर्णिनि ॥
स्वर्गलोकमुपागच्छ श्रेयः प्राप्स्यसि वै ततः ॥ 3 ॥
1.136.m: Having spent one night with the lord of men, O fair-complexioned woman, / return to heaven; thence you will surely attain the highest good."

1.136.s:
nāradenaivamuktā sā sakhībhirbahubhirvṛtā ..
puṣkariṇyāstaruplakṣe yayau snātuṃ varānanā .. 4 ..
1.136.d:
नारदेनैवमुक्ता सा सखीभिर्बहुभिर्वृता ॥
पुष्करिण्यास्तरुप्लक्षे ययौ स्नातुं वरानना ॥ 4 ॥
1.136.m: Spoken to thus by Nārada, that fair-faced woman, surrounded by many companions, / went to bathe in a lotus pool beside a plakṣa tree.

1.136.s:
etasminneva kāle tu nidrayopahṛto nṛpaḥ ..
apsarobhiravajñātastatra suṣvāpa pārthiva .. 5 ..
1.136.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु निद्रयोपहृतो नृपः ॥
अप्सरोभिरवज्ञातस्तत्र सुष्वाप पार्थिव ॥ 5 ॥
1.136.m: At that very time, the king, overcome by sleep, / disregardful of the apsarases, slept there, O ruler of the earth.

1.136.s:
adya yāsyāmi rājānamiti hṛṣṭā tadorvaśī..
krīḍantyatra jale tasminsakhīgaṇavṛtā tadā .. 6 ..
1.136.d:
अद्य यास्यामि राजानमिति हृष्टा तदोर्वशी॥
क्रीडन्त्यत्र जले तस्मिन्सखीगणवृता तदा ॥ 6 ॥
1.136.m: Joyful that 'Today I will go to the king', Urvaśī then, / playing in that water, surrounded by her troop of friends,

1.136.s:
tyaktanidro narendro'pi vilalāpa ciraṃ punaḥ ..
śuśrāva vilapantaṃ sā sakhībhiḥ sahitā nṛpam .. 7 ..
1.136.d:
त्यक्तनिद्रो नरेन्द्रोऽपि विललाप चिरं पुनः ॥
शुश्राव विलपन्तं सा सखीभिः सहिता नृपम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.136.m: Waking from sleep, the lord of men lamented again for a long time. / Accompanied by her companions, she heard the king lamenting.

1.136.s:
darśayāmāma cātmānaṃ pārthivasya śubhā tataḥ ..
uvāca ca varārohā nāradoktamaśeṣataḥ .. 8 ..
1.136.d:
दर्शयामाम चात्मानं पार्थिवस्य शुभा ततः ॥
उवाच च वरारोहा नारदोक्तमशेषतः ॥ 8 ॥
1.136.m: Then the auspicious woman showed herself to the king, / and the shapely woman related everything spoken by Nārada without omission.

1.136.s:
tatraivovāsa tāṃ rātriṃ saha tena varānanā ..
rātrikṣaye visaṃjñaṃ sā rājānaṃ vākyamabravīt .. 9 ..
1.136.d:
तत्रैवोवास तां रात्रिं सह तेन वरानना ॥
रात्रिक्षये विसंज्ञं सा राजानं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 9 ॥
1.136.m: Right there that fair-faced woman spent that night with him. / At the end of the night, she spoke these words to the unconscious king:

1.136.s:
urvaśyuvāca ..
ārādhayasva gandharvānmohaṃ tyaktvā nareśvara ..
teṣāṃ prārthaya māṃ saumya tataḥ prāpsyasi mā ciram .. 1.136.10..
1.136.d:
उर्वश्युवाच ॥
आराधयस्व गन्धर्वान्मोहं त्यक्त्वा नरेश्वर ॥
तेषां प्रार्थय मां सौम्य ततः प्राप्स्यसि मा चिरम् ॥ 1.136.10॥
1.136.m: Urvaśī said: / "Worship the Gandharvas, casting off delusion, O lord of men! / Ask them for me, gentle one; then you will attain me without delay."

1.136.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktvā yayau svargaṃ rājā tatraiva pārthiva ..
tapaḥ sa vipulaṃ cakre tadgatenaiva cetasā ..11 ..
1.136.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा ययौ स्वर्गं राजा तत्रैव पार्थिव ॥
तपः स विपुलं चक्रे तद्गतेनैव चेतसा ॥11 ॥
1.136.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, she went to heaven. Right there, O ruler of the earth, / the king performed severe asceticism with his mind fixed solely on her.

1.136.s:
atha saṃvatsare pūrṇe sūryasyodayanaṃ prati ..
nāradaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā gandharvā darśanaṃ daduḥ ..12..
1.136.d:
अथ संवत्सरे पूर्णे सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ॥
नारदं पुरतः कृत्वा गन्धर्वा दर्शनं ददुः ॥12॥
1.136.m: Then, when a full year had passed, toward the rising of the sun, / having placed Nārada at their head, the Gandharvas revealed themselves.

1.136.s:
gandharvā ūcuḥ ..
varaṃ varaya rājendra yadicchasi mahābhuja ..
vayaṃ hi tava dāsyāmaḥ sarva evāmaraprabhāḥ .. 13 ..
1.136.d:
गन्धर्वा ऊचुः ॥
वरं वरय राजेन्द्र यदिच्छसि महाभुज ॥
वयं हि तव दास्यामः सर्व एवामरप्रभाः ॥ 13 ॥
1.136.m: The Gandharvas said: / "Choose a boon, O chief of kings, whatever you desire, O mighty-armed one! / For all of us, possessing the splendour of immortals, will grant it to you."

1.136.s:
purūravā uvāca ..
bhavantaścetprasannā me yadi me rocate varam ..
urvaśī seha cārvaṅgī bhavadbhirmama dīyatām..14..
1.136.d:
पुरूरवा उवाच ॥
भवन्तश्चेत्प्रसन्ना मे यदि मे रोचते वरम् ॥
उर्वशी सेह चार्वङ्गी भवद्भिर्मम दीयताम्॥14॥
1.136.m: Purūravas said: / "If you are pleased with me, if my boon pleases you, / let that lovely-limbed Urvaśī here be given to me by you."

1.136.s:
gandharvā ūcuḥ ..
sthālīṃ pūrṇāmimāṃ rājangṛhāṇāgnermahābhuja ..
asmādagniṃ tridhā kṛtvā yajasva vigatajvaraḥ .. 15 ..
1.136.d:
गन्धर्वा ऊचुः ॥
स्थालीं पूर्णामिमां राजन्गृहाणाग्नेर्महाभुज ॥
अस्मादग्निं त्रिधा कृत्वा यजस्व विगतज्वरः ॥ 15 ॥
1.136.m: The Gandharvas said: / "Take this vessel full of fire, O king, O mighty-armed one! / Dividing the fire from this into three parts, sacrifice, freed from anxiety.

1.136.s:
vedoktena vidhānena gandharvatvamavāpsyasi ..
tretāgnipūrvasya vidherasminmanvantare bhavān ..16..
1.136.d:
वेदोक्तेन विधानेन गन्धर्वत्वमवाप्स्यसि ॥
त्रेताग्निपूर्वस्य विधेरस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे भवान् ॥16॥
1.136.m: By the rite prescribed in the Veda, you will attain the state of a Gandharva. / In this manvantara, you will be the revealer

1.136.s:
bhavitā darśitā loke guruśca jagatīpatiḥ ..
gandharvatvamavāpyātha rājanprāpsyasyathorvaśīm .. 17 ..
1.136.d:
भविता दर्शिता लोके गुरुश्च जगतीपतिः ॥
गन्धर्वत्वमवाप्याथ राजन्प्राप्स्यस्यथोर्वशीम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.136.m: and the teacher in the world of the rite preceded by the three fires, O ruler of the earth. / Having attained the state of a Gandharva, O king, you will then obtain Urvaśī.

1.136.s:
manvantaramimaṃ sarvaṃ rantā ca tvaṃ tayā saha ..
manvantare gate rājannurvaśyā sahito bhavān .. 18 ..
1.136.d:
मन्वन्तरमिमं सर्वं रन्ता च त्वं तया सह ॥
मन्वन्तरे गते राजन्नुर्वश्या सहितो भवान् ॥ 18 ॥
1.136.m: And you will delight with her through this entire manvantara. / When the manvantara has passed, O king, together with Urvaśī

1.136.s:
pravekṣyati niśānāthaṃ somaṃ śītāṃśumujvalam ..
ādhāraṃ sarvalokasya pitṝṇāṃ sthānamuttamam .. 19 ..
1.136.d:
प्रवेक्ष्यति निशानाथं सोमं शीतांशुमुज्वलम् ॥
आधारं सर्वलोकस्य पितॄणां स्थानमुत्तमम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.136.m: you will enter the bright, cool-rayed Soma, the lord of the night, / the support of all the worlds, the supreme abode of the ancestors."

1.136.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
agnisthālīṃ nṛpe dattvā gandharvāstridivaṃ yayuḥ ...
athā''jagāma taṃ deśaṃ bālamādāya corvaśī .. 1.136.20 ..
1.136.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अग्निस्थालीं नृपे दत्त्वा गन्धर्वास्त्रिदिवं ययुः ॥।
अथा'ऽजगाम तं देशं बालमादाय चोर्वशी ॥ 1.136.20 ॥
1.136.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having given the vessel of fire to the king, the Gandharvas went to heaven. / Then Urvaśī came to that place, bringing a boy.

1.136.s:
urvaśyuvāca ..
tasminsamāgame saumya jāto'yaṃ tanayaḥ prabho ..
tamādāya pratiṣṭhānaṃ vraja pārthiva māciram .. 21 ..
1.136.d:
उर्वश्युवाच ॥
तस्मिन्समागमे सौम्य जातोऽयं तनयः प्रभो ॥
तमादाय प्रतिष्ठानं व्रज पार्थिव माचिरम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.136.m: Urvaśī said: / "From that union, O gentle one, this son was born, O lord. / Taking him, go to Pratiṣṭhāna without delay, O king.

1.136.s:
kṛtaṃ nāmāsya gandharvairviśvāyurati bhūmipa ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evaṃ dattvā nṛpe bālaṃ sā prayātā triviṣṭapam .. 22 ..
1.136.d:
कृतं नामास्य गन्धर्वैर्विश्वायुरति भूमिप ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवं दत्त्वा नृपे बालं सा प्रयाता त्रिविष्टपम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.136.m: His name, Viśvāyus, was given by the Gandharvas, O ruler of the earth." / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having thus given the boy to the king, she departed for heaven.

1.136.s:
ekākī cintayāmāsa budhaputropyanantaram ..
kinnu bālamupādāya gamiṣyāmi puraṃ svakam ..23..
1.136.d:
एकाकी चिन्तयामास बुधपुत्रोप्यनन्तरम् ॥
किन्नु बालमुपादाय गमिष्यामि पुरं स्वकम् ॥23॥
1.136.m: Alone, the son of Budha then thought: / 'Shall I take the boy and go to my own city,

1.136.s:
athādāya gamiṣyāmi sthālīmetāṃ vibhāvasoḥ..
śvāpadebhyo bhayaṃ ghoraṃ bālasyeha bhaviṣyati .. 24 ..
1.136.d:
अथादाय गमिष्यामि स्थालीमेतां विभावसोः॥
श्वापदेभ्यो भयं घोरं बालस्येह भविष्यति ॥ 24 ॥
1.136.m: or shall I take this vessel of fire and go? / For the boy there will be dreadful fear of wild beasts here.

1.136.s:
mayā vihīnasya bhayaṃ nāsti kiñcidvibhāvasoḥ ..
evaṃ sa niścayaṃ kṛtvā bālamādāya satvaraḥ. .. 25 ..
1.136.d:
मया विहीनस्य भयं नास्ति किञ्चिद्विभावसोः ॥
एवं स निश्चयं कृत्वा बालमादाय सत्वरः॥। 25 ॥
1.136.m: Left without me, there is no fear at all for the fire.' / Making this decision, he took the boy and quickly

1.136.s:
jagāma svapuraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ sasainyaścāgamatpunaḥ ..
sthālīṃ dadarśa hīnāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā mohamupāgataḥ .. 26 ..
1.136.d:
जगाम स्वपुरं हृष्टः ससैन्यश्चागमत्पुनः ॥
स्थालीं ददर्श हीनां तु दृष्ट्वा मोहमुपागतः ॥ 26 ॥
1.136.m: went rejoicing to his city, and returned again with his army. / But he saw the vessel was empty; seeing it, he fell into delusion.

1.136.s:
tridivādetya gandharvā mūḍhaṃ pārthivasattamam ..
utthāpayitvā vacanamūcustaddhitakāṅkṣiṇaḥ .. 27 ..
1.136.d:
त्रिदिवादेत्य गन्धर्वा मूढं पार्थिवसत्तमम् ॥
उत्थापयित्वा वचनमूचुस्तद्धितकाङ्क्षिणः ॥ 27 ॥
1.136.m: Descending from heaven, the Gandharvas, wishing for his welfare, / raised up the bewildered, best of kings and spoke these words:

1.136.s:
rājannasmiñchamīgarbhe praviṣṭaḥ sa hutāśanaḥ ..
asmāttvamaraṇiṃ kṛtvā janayasva hutāśanam .. 28 ..
1.136.d:
राजन्नस्मिञ्छमीगर्भे प्रविष्टः स हुताशनः ॥
अस्मात्त्वमरणिं कृत्वा जनयस्व हुताशनम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.136.m: "O king, that fire has entered into the womb of this śamī tree. / Having made a kindling stick from this, generate the fire.

1.136.s:
tridhā kṛtvā tu taṃ vīra yajasva vidhivattadā ..
tamiṣṭvā prāpsyase vīra gandharvatmasaṃśayam .. 29 ..
1.136.d:
त्रिधा कृत्वा तु तं वीर यजस्व विधिवत्तदा ॥
तमिष्ट्वा प्राप्स्यसे वीर गन्धर्वत्मसंशयम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.136.m: Dividing it into three parts, O hero, sacrifice then according to the rule. / Having offered that, O hero, you will attain the state of a Gandharva, without doubt.

1.136.s:
tretāgniṃ te narendreha hoṣyanti satataṃ dvijāḥ ..
saptavarṣāṇi te'pyevaṃ yāsyatyasmatsalokatām .. 1.136.30 ..
1.136.d:
त्रेताग्निं ते नरेन्द्रेह होष्यन्ति सततं द्विजाः ॥
सप्तवर्षाणि तेऽप्येवं यास्यत्यस्मत्सलोकताम् ॥ 1.136.30 ॥
1.136.m: The twice-born will constantly sacrifice into the three fires for you here, O lord of men. / In seven years, [your time] will pass thus to dwell in the same realm as us.

1.136.s:
trayo'gnayaścopasadaṃ tava rājanprakīrtitāḥ ..
agnirāhavanīyastu vāsudevo narādhipa .. 31 ..
1.136.d:
त्रयोऽग्नयश्चोपसदं तव राजन्प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
अग्निराहवनीयस्तु वासुदेवो नराधिप ॥ 31 ॥
1.136.m: Three fires and the upasada rite are proclaimed for you, O king: / The āhavanīya fire, O ruler of men, is Vāsudeva.

1.136.s:
dakṣiṇāgnistathā jñeyo nityaṃ saṃkarṣaṇo budhaiḥ ..
tathā ca gārhapatyo'gniḥ pradyumnaḥ paripaṭhyate ..32..
1.136.d:
दक्षिणाग्निस्तथा ज्ञेयो नित्यं संकर्षणो बुधैः ॥
तथा च गार्हपत्योऽग्निः प्रद्युम्नः परिपठ्यते ॥32॥
1.136.m: The dakṣiṇa fire should be known constantly by the wise as Saṃkarṣaṇa. / And likewise the gārhapatya fire is recited as Pradyumna.

1.136.s:
tathaivaupasado rājannaniruddhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
tasmādeva varo viṣṇuścaturātmā narādhipa .. 33 ..
1.136.d:
तथैवौपसदो राजन्ननिरुद्धः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
तस्मादेव वरो विष्णुश्चतुरात्मा नराधिप ॥ 33 ॥
1.136.m: Likewise, the upasada fire, O king, is proclaimed as Aniruddha. / Therefore, Viṣṇu, who has four forms, is the supreme giver of boons, O ruler of men.

1.136.s:
phalābhisandhānahuto gandharvatvaṃ prayacchati ..
kāmaṃ vināgnihotreṇa huto rājañjanārdanaḥ .. 34 ..
1.136.d:
फलाभिसन्धानहुतो गन्धर्वत्वं प्रयच्छति ॥
कामं विनाग्निहोत्रेण हुतो राजञ्जनार्दनः ॥ 34 ॥
1.136.m: Sacrificed to with longing for fruits, he grants the state of a Gandharva. / Sacrificed to without desire through the agnihotra, O king, Janārdana

1.136.s:
prayacchati paraṃ sthānamamṛtaṃ śāśvataṃ dhruvam ..
agnihotrādṛte rājangandharvatvaṃ na vidyate .. 35 ..
1.136.d:
प्रयच्छति परं स्थानममृतं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम् ॥
अग्निहोत्रादृते राजन्गन्धर्वत्वं न विद्यते ॥ 35 ॥
1.136.m: bestows the supreme, immortal, eternal, and firm state. / Without the agnihotra, O king, the state of a Gandharva cannot be found.

1.136.s:
suhutenāgnihotreṇa prāpyate saṃśayaṃ vinā ..
evamuktvā yayuḥ sarve gandharvāstridivaṃ tataḥ .. 36 ..
1.136.d:
सुहुतेनाग्निहोत्रेण प्राप्यते संशयं विना ॥
एवमुक्त्वा ययुः सर्वे गन्धर्वास्त्रिदिवं ततः ॥ 36 ॥
1.136.m: Through the properly offered agnihotra it is attained without doubt." / Having spoken thus, all the Gandharvas then went to heaven.

1.136.s:
rājāpyaraṇimādāya śamīgarbhādgṛhaṃ yayau..
tataḥ prabhṛti rājendra śamīgarbhāddhutāśanam...
janayanti dvijaśreṣṭhāstatra sannihitastvasau .. 37 ..
1.136.d:
राजाप्यरणिमादाय शमीगर्भाद्गृहं ययौ॥
ततः प्रभृति राजेन्द्र शमीगर्भाद्धुताशनम्॥।
जनयन्ति द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तत्र सन्निहितस्त्वसौ ॥ 37 ॥
1.136.m: The king also, taking the fire-drill from the womb of the śamī tree, went home. / From that time forth, O chief of kings, the foremost of the twice-born / generate fire from the womb of the śamī tree, for it is present there.

1.136.s:
eko'gnirāsīnnṛpavarya pūrvaṃ vaivasvatasyāsya tathāntare'smin ..
tridhākṛtastena mahānubhāva saṃmaṃtrivipraiḥ kratuśāstravijñaiḥ .. 38 ..
1.136.d:
एकोऽग्निरासीन्नृपवर्य पूर्वं वैवस्वतस्यास्य तथान्तरेऽस्मिन् ॥
त्रिधाकृतस्तेन महानुभाव संमंत्रिविप्रैः क्रतुशास्त्रविज्ञैः ॥ 38 ॥
1.136.m: Formerly there was one fire, O best of kings, in this period of Vaivasvata; / it was made threefold by that noble one, consulting with brahmins skilled in the sacrificial treatises.

1.136.s: iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde tretāgnyutpattirnāma ṣaṭtriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 136 ..
1.136.d: इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे त्रेताग्न्युत्पत्तिर्नाम षट्त्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 136 ॥
1.136.m: Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-sixth chapter, entitled 'The Origin of the Three Fires', in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the first book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.

1.137.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
tataḥ sa svapuraṃ prāpya cāgnyupāsanatatparaḥ ..
īje bahuvidhairyajñaiḥ prajā dharmeṇa pālayan .. 1 ..
1.137.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
ततः स स्वपुरं प्राप्य चाग्न्युपासनतत्परः ॥
ईजे बहुविधैर्यज्ञैः प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन् ॥ 1 ॥
1.137.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, having reached his city, dedicated to the worship of fire, / he sacrificed with diverse sacrifices, protecting his subjects with dharma.

1.137.s:
aśvamedhaśatairiṣṭvā vājapeyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ ..
agniṣṭomaiścātirātrairdvādaśāhaiḥ punaḥpunaḥ .. 2 ..
1.137.d:
अश्वमेधशतैरिष्ट्वा वाजपेयैः सहस्रशः ॥
अग्निष्टोमैश्चातिरात्रैर्द्वादशाहैः पुनःपुनः ॥ 2 ॥
1.137.m: Having sacrificed with hundreds of horse sacrifices, with thousands of Vājapeyas, / with Agniṣṭomas, Atirātras, and twelve-day sacrifices again and again,

1.137.s:
saptadvīpasamudrāyāṃ pṛthivyāmekarāḍ babhau ..
amānuṣairvṛtaḥ sattvaiḥ sa vijigye mahītalam .. 3 ..
1.137.d:
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्रायां पृथिव्यामेकराड् बभौ ॥
अमानुषैर्वृतः सत्त्वैः स विजिग्ये महीतलम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.137.m: he shone as sole sovereign over the earth with its seven continents and oceans. / Surrounded by non-human beings, he conquered the terrestrial world.

1.137.s:
durbhikṣaṃ maraṇaṃ vyādhirnābhavatkasyacitkvacit ..
sarvo dharmaparo lokaḥ sarva eva sukhī janaḥ .. 4 ..
1.137.d:
दुर्भिक्षं मरणं व्याधिर्नाभवत्कस्यचित्क्वचित् ॥
सर्वो धर्मपरो लोकः सर्व एव सुखी जनः ॥ 4 ॥
1.137.m: Famine, death, or disease did not befall anyone anywhere. / All people were devoted to dharma; everyone was happy.

1.137.s:
sarve caiva samṛddhārthāstasmiñjanapadeśvare ..
nāsītpaśuvadhārhāṇāṃ vadhastasminvṛthā tadā .. 5 ..
1.137.d:
सर्वे चैव समृद्धार्थास्तस्मिञ्जनपदेश्वरे ॥
नासीत्पशुवधार्हाणां वधस्तस्मिन्वृथा तदा ॥ 5 ॥
1.137.m: And all people had abundant wealth when he was lord of the realm; / no slaughter of animals deserving to be killed was done in vain at that time.

1.137.s:
sarvabhūtāni rājānaṃ bhāvenopagatāni tam ..
sarvasya ca jananyāsītsa rājā pitṛsannibhaḥ ..6..
1.137.d:
सर्वभूतानि राजानं भावेनोपगतानि तम् ॥
सर्वस्य च जनन्यासीत्स राजा पितृसन्निभः ॥6॥
1.137.m: All living beings approached that king with devotion; / and that king, like a father, was like a mother to everyone.

1.137.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ bhūpatiṃ svapne prasīdanti janāstadā ..
yadā niryātyasau rājā caturaṅgabalānvitaḥ ..7..
1.137.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं भूपतिं स्वप्ने प्रसीदन्ति जनास्तदा ॥
यदा निर्यात्यसौ राजा चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः ॥7॥
1.137.m: Seeing that ruler of the earth even in a dream, the people rejoiced then, / whenever that king set forth endowed with his fourfold army.

1.137.s:
gṛhacaryāratā nāryastadā paśyanti taṃ sadā ..
puṣpaiścandanadhūpaiśca tathaiva vikiranti tam .. 8 ..
1.137.d:
गृहचर्यारता नार्यस्तदा पश्यन्ति तं सदा ॥
पुष्पैश्चन्दनधूपैश्च तथैव विकिरन्ति तम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.137.m: Women engaged in household duties constantly watched him then, / and they scattered flowers, sandalwood, and incense over him.

1.137.s:
urvaśī kṛtapuṇyā sā devī nārāyaṇātmajā ..
yayā krīḍitamasyāṅke vadantyevaṃ ca yoṣitaḥ .. 9 ..
1.137.d:
उर्वशी कृतपुण्या सा देवी नारायणात्मजा ॥
यया क्रीडितमस्याङ्के वदन्त्येवं च योषितः ॥ 9 ॥
1.137.m: “Blessed is that divine Urvaśī, daughter of Nārāyaṇa, / who has played on his lap!” Thus the women spoke.

1.137.s:
ayamāyātyasau rājā yadā śṛṇvanti yoṣitaḥ ..
gṛhakāryāṇyapi tyaktvā tadā yānti ,gavākṣakān .. 1.137.10 ..
1.137.d:
अयमायात्यसौ राजा यदा शृण्वन्ति योषितः ॥
गृहकार्याण्यपि त्यक्त्वा तदा यान्ति ,गवाक्षकान् ॥ 1.137.10 ॥
1.137.m: When the women heard, “Here comes the king!”, / abandoning even their household chores, they ran to the latticed windows.

1.137.s:
abhrāṇi śāradānīva bahucandrāṇi yoṣitām ..
mukhai rājanti veśmāni niryāte pṛthivīśvare .. 11 ..
1.137.d:
अभ्राणि शारदानीव बहुचन्द्राणि योषिताम् ॥
मुखै राजन्ति वेश्मानि निर्याते पृथिवीश्वरे ॥ 11 ॥
1.137.m: Like autumnal clouds containing many moons, / the mansions shone with the faces of the women when the lord of the earth went forth.

1.137.s:
yā na paśyati taṃ yāntaṃ sā taṃ jñātvā tirohitam ..
muṣitaṃ caiva sā''tmānaṃ vetti nindati sā bhṛśam .. 12 ..
1.137.d:
या न पश्यति तं यान्तं सा तं ज्ञात्वा तिरोहितम् ॥
मुषितं चैव सा'ऽत्मानं वेत्ति निन्दति सा भृशम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.137.m: She who did not see him passing by, knowing that he had disappeared from sight, / considered herself robbed and blamed herself intensely.

1.137.s:
yā ca paśyati taṃ yāntaṃ kandarpasadṛśaṃ nṛpam ..
tadgatena hradā sāpi śūnyā tiṣṭhati veśmani .. 13 ..
1.137.d:
या च पश्यति तं यान्तं कन्दर्पसदृशं नृपम् ॥
तद्गतेन ह्रदा सापि शून्या तिष्ठति वेश्मनि ॥ 13 ॥
1.137.m: And she who saw the king passing by, looking like Kandarpa, / remained in her house with an empty mind, her heart fixed on him.

1.137.s:
yadā yajati yajñaiśca tadā śūnyā vasundharā ..
sarvā bhavati rājānaṃ tadā gacchati vai janaḥ .. .. 14 ..
1.137.d:
यदा यजति यज्ञैश्च तदा शून्या वसुन्धरा ॥
सर्वा भवति राजानं तदा गच्छति वै जनः ॥ ॥ 14 ॥
1.137.m: When he performed sacrifices, the whole earth became empty; / everyone then went to the king.

1.137.s:
yaśca yāti janastasya yajñe rājño mahātmanaḥ ..
kimicchakaistadā rājñā sarvaḥ saṃpūjyate tadā .. 15 ..
1.137.d:
यश्च याति जनस्तस्य यज्ञे राज्ञो महात्मनः ॥
किमिच्छकैस्तदा राज्ञा सर्वः संपूज्यते तदा ॥ 15 ॥
1.137.m: And whichever person went to the sacrifice of that great-souled king, / everyone was honored by the king with whatever they desired.

1.137.s:
sabhāsaṃsthasya vai rājñaḥ pratīhāro dine dine ..
udghoṣayati kāryārthī tasya rājye kathaṃcana .. 16 ..
1.137.d:
सभासंस्थस्य वै राज्ञः प्रतीहारो दिने दिने ॥
उद्घोषयति कार्यार्थी तस्य राज्ये कथंचन ॥ 16 ॥
1.137.m: Day after day, as the king sat in his assembly hall, the doorkeeper / would proclaim [to see] if anyone in his kingdom had any petition.

1.137.s:
ityevaṃ śāsato rājyaṃ gataḥ kālo mahīpateḥ ..
sa kadāciddvijānāha darśayadhvaṃ mamorvaśīm .. 17 ..
1.137.d:
इत्येवं शासतो राज्यं गतः कालो महीपतेः ॥
स कदाचिद्द्विजानाह दर्शयध्वं ममोर्वशीम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.137.m: As he ruled the kingdom in this way, time passed for the ruler of the earth. / Once, he said to the twice-born: “Show me Urvaśī!”

1.137.s:
drakṣyase tāṃ svayaṃ rājanna vayaṃ darśayāmahe ..
tatasteṣāṃ dhane lobhaṃ cakre kāmanipīḍitaḥ .. 18 ..
1.137.d:
द्रक्ष्यसे तां स्वयं राजन्न वयं दर्शयामहे ॥
ततस्तेषां धने लोभं चक्रे कामनिपीडितः ॥ 18 ॥
1.137.m: “You will see her yourself, O King; we cannot show her.” / Thereupon, tormented by lust, he coveted their wealth.

1.137.s:
hriyamāṇe dhane vipraiḥ śaptaḥ pañcatvamāgataḥ ..
jīvitaścāparairviprairgataroṣairmahīpatiḥ .. 19 ..
1.137.d:
ह्रियमाणे धने विप्रैः शप्तः पञ्चत्वमागतः ॥
जीवितश्चापरैर्विप्रैर्गतरोषैर्महीपतिः ॥ 19 ॥
1.137.m: As their wealth was being seized, he was cursed by the vipras and died; / and he was brought back to life by other vipras whose anger had passed.

1.137.s:
ātmānaṃ garhayitvā'sau labdhasaṃjño mahīpatiḥ ..
āyuṃ rājye'bhiṣicyaiva pratiṣṭhānapure svake .. 1.137.20 ..
1.137.d:
आत्मानं गर्हयित्वाऽसौ लब्धसंज्ञो महीपतिः ॥
आयुं राज्येऽभिषिच्यैव प्रतिष्ठानपुरे स्वके ॥ 1.137.20 ॥
1.137.m: Rebuking himself, the ruler of the earth regained consciousness, / consecrated Āyu to the kingdom in his city of Pratiṣṭhāna,

1.137.s:
sāgnihotrastato rājā yayau nārāyaṇāśramam ..
tasyāśrame tapaścakre rājā saṃvatsaratrayam .. 21 ..
1.137.d:
साग्निहोत्रस्ततो राजा ययौ नारायणाश्रमम् ॥
तस्याश्रमे तपश्चक्रे राजा संवत्सरत्रयम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.137.m: and then the king, taking his sacred fires, went to the hermitage of Nārāyaṇa. / In his hermitage, the king performed austerities for three years.

1.137.s:
tato nārāyaṇaḥ prāha taṃ nṛpaṃ tapasi sthitam ..
adya prāpsyasi tāṃ rājanyatkṛte paritapyase .. 22 ..
1.137.d:
ततो नारायणः प्राह तं नृपं तपसि स्थितम् ॥
अद्य प्राप्स्यसि तां राजन्यत्कृते परितप्यसे ॥ 22 ॥
1.137.m: Then Nārāyaṇa spoke to the king who was engaged in austerity: / “Today you shall obtain her for whose sake you suffer, O King.

1.137.s:
saśarīro'dya gantāsi tridivaṃ rājasattama ..
evaṃ dvijendre vadati vimānaṃ pratyadṛśyata .. 23 ..
1.137.d:
सशरीरोऽद्य गन्तासि त्रिदिवं राजसत्तम ॥
एवं द्विजेन्द्रे वदति विमानं प्रत्यदृश्यत ॥ 23 ॥
1.137.m: In your own body, O best of kings, you shall go to heaven today.” / As the foremost of the twice-born was speaking thus, a celestial chariot appeared,

1.137.s:
urvaśyadhiṣṭhitaṃ ramyaṃ gandharvaiśca sahasraśaḥ ..
yasminyuktaṃ turaṅgāṇāṃ sahasraṃ candravarcasām .. 24 ..
1.137.d:
उर्वश्यधिष्ठितं रम्यं गन्धर्वैश्च सहस्रशः ॥
यस्मिन्युक्तं तुरङ्गाणां सहस्रं चन्द्रवर्चसाम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.137.m: occupied by Urvaśī, delightful, and attended by Gandharvas in their thousands, / yoked with a thousand horses possessing the splendour of the moon.

1.137.s:
vimānādavaruhyātha gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ..
urvaśī ca vavandainamṛṣiṃ jvalanatejasam .. 25 ..
1.137.d:
विमानादवरुह्याथ गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ॥
उर्वशी च ववन्दैनमृषिं ज्वलनतेजसम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.137.m: Then, having descended from the celestial chariot, the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases / and Urvaśī bowed to that sage of blazing splendour.

1.137.s:
anujñāto'tha ṛṣiṇā tadā rājā purūravāḥ ..
kṛtvāgnihotramātmasthaṃ vimānaṃ taṃ samāsthitaḥ .. 26 ..
1.137.d:
अनुज्ञातोऽथ ऋषिणा तदा राजा पुरूरवाः ॥
कृत्वाग्निहोत्रमात्मस्थं विमानं तं समास्थितः ॥ 26 ॥
1.137.m: Permitted then by the sage, King Purūravas / took his sacred fires within himself and boarded that celestial chariot.

1.137.s:
ṛṣiṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tridivaṃ sa nṛpo gataḥ ..
saśarīro nṛpaḥ svargaṃ tadā prāpya sudurlabham .. 57 ..
1.137.d:
ऋषिं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य त्रिदिवं स नृपो गतः ॥
सशरीरो नृपः स्वर्गं तदा प्राप्य सुदुर्लभम् ॥ 57 ॥
1.137.m: Having circumambulated the sage, the king went to heaven. / Having attained heaven, very difficult to reach in bodily form, the king

1.137.s:
śakreṇābhyarcitaḥ kāle vijahāra yathāsukham..
devodyāneṣu sarveṣu urvaśyā sahitastadā .. 28 ..
1.137.d:
शक्रेणाभ्यर्चितः काले विजहार यथासुखम्॥
देवोद्यानेषु सर्वेषु उर्वश्या सहितस्तदा ॥ 28 ॥
1.137.m: was honored by Śakra at the proper time and sported as he pleased / in all the divine gardens together with Urvaśī.

1.137.s:
nāsau viyujyate sākṣātkadācidapi pārthivaḥ ..
amāvasyāmamāvasyāṃ niyataṃ candrabhāskarau .. 29 ..
1.137.d:
नासौ वियुज्यते साक्षात्कदाचिदपि पार्थिवः ॥
अमावस्याममावस्यां नियतं चन्द्रभास्करौ ॥ 29 ॥
1.137.m: That king is never separated [from her] in bodily form. / On every new-moon day, the moon and the sun invariably

1.137.s:
draṣṭuṃ yātau mahīpālamekarāśigatau sadā ..
urvaśyā sahitaṃ pautraṃ yadā paśyati candramāḥ ..1.137.30..
1.137.d:
द्रष्टुं यातौ महीपालमेकराशिगतौ सदा ॥
उर्वश्या सहितं पौत्रं यदा पश्यति चन्द्रमाः ॥1.137.30॥
1.137.m: come together in a single zodiacal sign to see the ruler of the earth. / When the Moon sees his grandson accompanied by Urvaśī,

1.137.s:
tadā sudhārasaṃ devaḥ snehātsravati mānada ..
sudhāmṛtarasaṃ taṃ ca pibanti pitaraḥ sadā .. 31 ..
1.137.d:
तदा सुधारसं देवः स्नेहात्स्रवति मानद ॥
सुधामृतरसं तं च पिबन्ति पितरः सदा ॥ 31 ॥
1.137.m: then out of affection, O bestower of honor, the god exudes the nectar of immortality; / and the ancestors constantly drink that essence of nectar.

1.137.s:
śrāddhakālastadāpyukto nṛṇāṃ nṛpavarottama ..
tadā śrāddhaṃ hi yaddattaṃ sudhārasavimiśritam .. 32 ..
1.137.d:
श्राद्धकालस्तदाप्युक्तो नृणां नृपवरोत्तम ॥
तदा श्राद्धं हि यद्दत्तं सुधारसविमिश्रितम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.137.m: That is also declared to be the time of śrāddha for men, O best of excellent kings; / for the śrāddha that is offered then is mixed with the essence of nectar.

1.137.s:
tadaśnanti mahīpāla pitaro'mṛtasannibham ..
amāvasyāmamāvasyāṃ tadā śrāddhaṃ prayatnataḥ .. .. 33 ..
1.137.d:
तदश्नन्ति महीपाल पितरोऽमृतसन्निभम् ॥
अमावस्याममावस्यां तदा श्राद्धं प्रयत्नतः ॥ ॥ 33 ॥
1.137.m: The ancestors consume that, O ruler of the earth, as equivalent to nectar. / Therefore, diligently perform the śrāddha / on every new-moon day,

1.137.s:
kuruṣva bhūmipaśreṣṭha sarvānkāmānavāpsyasi ..
ye'pi śrāddhaṃ kariṣyanti tadā cānye narādhipa .. 34 ..
1.137.d:
कुरुष्व भूमिपश्रेष्ठ सर्वान्कामानवाप्स्यसि ॥
येऽपि श्राद्धं करिष्यन्ति तदा चान्ये नराधिप ॥ 34 ॥
1.137.m: O best of kings, and you will obtain all desired objects. / And whatever other men perform the śrāddha then, O ruler of men,

1.137.s:
teṣāmāyuryaśaḥ saukhyaṃ dāsyanti prapitāmahāḥ ..
devakāryādapi śreṣṭhaṃ pitṛkāryaṃ pracakṣate .. 35 ..
1.137.d:
तेषामायुर्यशः सौख्यं दास्यन्ति प्रपितामहाः ॥
देवकार्यादपि श्रेष्ठं पितृकार्यं प्रचक्षते ॥ 35 ॥
1.137.m: their great-grandfathers will grant them long life, fame, and happiness. / The rite for the ancestors is declared to be even superior to the rite for the gods.

1.137.s:
pitaro nāma rājendra devānāmapi devatāḥ ..
rājyakāmaḥ svargakāmaḥ puṣṭikāmastathaiva ca .. 336 ..
1.137.d:
पितरो नाम राजेन्द्र देवानामपि देवताः ॥
राज्यकामः स्वर्गकामः पुष्टिकामस्तथैव च ॥ 336 ॥
1.137.m: The ancestors, O king of kings, are indeed the deities even of the gods. / One who desires a kingdom, one who desires heaven, and likewise one who desires prosperity,

1.137.s:
pitṝnsantarpayecchrāddhe candrasūryasamāgame ..
vasanti satataṃ rājanpitaraścandramaṇḍale .. 37 ..
1.137.d:
पितॄन्सन्तर्पयेच्छ्राद्धे चन्द्रसूर्यसमागमे ॥
वसन्ति सततं राजन्पितरश्चन्द्रमण्डले ॥ 37 ॥
1.137.m: should gratify the ancestors with a śrāddha at the conjunction of the sun and moon. / The ancestors constantly dwell, O King, in the lunar orb.

1.137.s:
teṣāṃ māsamahorātraṃ vibhāgaṃ tatra me śṛṇu ..
kṛṣṇapakṣāṣṭamī madhye teṣāmudayate raviḥ .. 38 ..
1.137.d:
तेषां मासमहोरात्रं विभागं तत्र मे शृणु ॥
कृष्णपक्षाष्टमी मध्ये तेषामुदयते रविः ॥ 38 ॥
1.137.m: Hear from me their division of day and night through the month: / for them, the sun rises in the middle of the eighth day of the dark fortnight;

1.137.s:
śuklāṣṭamyāṃ tathaivāstaṃ teṣāṃ yāti divākaraḥ ..
amāvasyā tadā teṣāṃ madhyāhnaṃ jāyate nṛpa ..
tasmācchrāddhāni deyāni tasminkāle prayatnataḥ .. 39..
1.137.d:
शुक्लाष्टम्यां तथैवास्तं तेषां याति दिवाकरः ॥
अमावस्या तदा तेषां मध्याह्नं जायते नृप ॥
तस्माच्छ्राद्धानि देयानि तस्मिन्काले प्रयत्नतः ॥ 39॥
1.137.m: likewise, the sun sets for them on the eighth day of the bright fortnight. / The new-moon day then becomes their midday, O King; / therefore, offerings of śrāddha should be made at that time with great effort.

1.137.s:
etāvaduktaṃ nṛpavarya tasya dharmātmajasyā'pratimasya vṛttam ...
dhanyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ripunāśanaṃ ca saubhāgyadaṃ pāpaharaṃ sukhañca .. 1.137.40 ..
1.137.d:
एतावदुक्तं नृपवर्य तस्य धर्मात्मजस्याऽप्रतिमस्य वृत्तम् ॥।
धन्यं यशस्यं रिपुनाशनं च सौभाग्यदं पापहरं सुखञ्च ॥ 1.137.40 ॥
1.137.m: This much has been told, O best of kings, of the life of that peerless son of Dharma, / which brings prosperity, fame, destroys enemies, grants good fortune, removes sin, and brings happiness.

1.138.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
vartante pitaraḥ svarge keṣāṃcinnarake tathā ..
narakasthāḥ phalaṃ dātuṃ kathaṃ śaktā vadasva me .. 1 ..
1.138.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
वर्तन्ते पितरः स्वर्गे केषांचिन्नरके तथा ॥
नरकस्थाः फलं दातुं कथं शक्ता वदस्व मे ॥ 1 ॥
1.138.m: Vajra said: / The ancestors reside in heaven, and some in hell; / tell me, how are those residing in hell able to grant results?

1.138.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
pitṝṇāṃ tu gaṇāḥ sapta nāmatastānnibodha me ..
trayo'mūrtimataścaiṣāṃ catvāraśca samūrtayaḥ .. 2 ..
1.138.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
पितॄणां तु गणाः सप्त नामतस्तान्निबोध मे ॥
त्रयोऽमूर्तिमतश्चैषां चत्वारश्च समूर्तयः ॥ 2 ॥
1.138.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / There are seven groups of ancestors; learn them from me by name: / three of them are formless, and four have form.

1.138.s:
subhāsurā barhiṣado'gniṣvāttāstathaiva ca ..
trayo mūrtimataścaiṣāṃ catvāraścāpyamūrtayaḥ .. 3 ..
1.138.d:
सुभासुरा बर्हिषदोऽग्निष्वात्तास्तथैव च ॥
त्रयो मूर्तिमतश्चैषां चत्वारश्चाप्यमूर्तयः ॥ 3 ॥
1.138.m: The Subhāsvaras, the Barhiṣads, and likewise the Agniṣvāttas; / three of them have form, and four are formless.

1.138.s:
kravyādāścopahūtāśca ājyapāśca sukālinaḥ ..
mūrtimantaḥ pitṛgaṇāścatvāraśca prakīrtitāḥ .. 4 ..
1.138.d:
क्रव्यादाश्चोपहूताश्च आज्यपाश्च सुकालिनः ॥
मूर्तिमन्तः पितृगणाश्चत्वारश्च प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 4 ॥
1.138.m: The Kravyāds, the Upahūtas, the Ājyapas, and the Sukālins / are proclaimed to be the four groups of ancestors who have form.

1.138.s:
subhāsvarā brahmasutāḥ somamāpyāyayanti ye ..
brahmalokacarā rājannityaṃ mūrtivivarjitāḥ ..5..
1.138.d:
सुभास्वरा ब्रह्मसुताः सोममाप्याययन्ति ये ॥
ब्रह्मलोकचरा राजन्नित्यं मूर्तिविवर्जिताः ॥5॥
1.138.m: The Subhāsvaras are sons of Brahmā, who cause Soma to swell; / moving in the world of Brahmā, O King, they are eternally devoid of form.

1.138.s:
tathā barhiṣado nāma rājaputrā marīcinaḥ ..
āpyāyayanti te devām̐lloke somapade sthitāḥ .. 6 ..
1.138.d:
तथा बर्हिषदो नाम राजपुत्रा मरीचिनः ॥
आप्याययन्ति ते देवाम्̐ल्लोके सोमपदे स्थिताः ॥ 6 ॥
1.138.m: Likewise, those named Barhiṣads are sons of kings, descendants of Marīci; / stationed in the world of the lunar abode, they nourish the gods.

1.138.s:
vibhrājaloke tiṣṭhanti agniṣvāttā narādhipa ..
pulastyasya ṛṣeḥ putrā bhaviṣyanti jaganti te .. 7 ..
1.138.d:
विभ्राजलोके तिष्ठन्ति अग्निष्वात्ता नराधिप ॥
पुलस्त्यस्य ऋषेः पुत्रा भविष्यन्ति जगन्ति ते ॥ 7 ॥
1.138.m: The Agniṣvāttas dwell in the Vibhrāja world, O lord of men; / the sons of the sage Pulastya, they will be the worlds.
The Dānavas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Piśācas, Uragas, Rākṣasas, / Daityas, Bhūtas, and Piśācas, as well as the hosts of Vidyādharas,
nāgas, sarpas, suparṇas, mountains, and rivers, / as well as the Kravyādas, Upahūtas, Ājyapas, and Sukālins,
nourish brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and outcastes. / The sons of Kavi, of Aṅgiras, and of the Prajāpati Kardama,

1.138.s:
vasiṣṭhasya tathā putrāḥ krameṇaite prakīrtitāḥ ..
jyotirbhāsaḥ smṛtā loke ye ca lokā marīcinaḥ ..11..
1.138.d:
वसिष्ठस्य तथा पुत्राः क्रमेणैते प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
ज्योतिर्भासः स्मृता लोके ये च लोका मरीचिनः ॥11॥
1.138.m: and likewise of Vasiṣṭha are proclaimed in order. / Those known in the world as Jyotirbhāsas and the worlds of Marīci,

1.138.s:
tejesvino māna sāśca krameṇaite prakīrtitāḥ ..
ete śrāddhasya bhoktāro viśvedevaiḥ sadā saha .. 12 ..
1.138.d:
तेजेस्विनो मान साश्च क्रमेणैते प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
एते श्राद्धस्य भोक्तारो विश्वेदेवैः सदा सह ॥ 12 ॥
1.138.m: the Tejasvins and the Mānasas are proclaimed in order. / These are the enjoyers of the śrāddha, ever together with the Viśvedevas.

1.138.s:
ete śrāddhaṃ sadā bhuktvā pitṝnsaṃtarpayantyataḥ ..
yatra kvacana dharmajña vartamānā hi yogataḥ ..13 ..
1.138.d:
एते श्राद्धं सदा भुक्त्वा पितॄन्संतर्पयन्त्यतः ॥
यत्र क्वचन धर्मज्ञ वर्तमाना हि योगतः ॥13 ॥
1.138.m: Always having enjoyed the śrāddha, they then gratify the ancestors / wherever they may be existing through yoga, O knower of dharma.

1.138.s:
ete ca puṣṭyā viniyojayanti śrāddhasya dātāramadīnasattvāḥ ..
tṛptāstathaite viniyojayanti dātuḥ pitṝnsarvagatānmahīpa ..14..
1.138.d:
एते च पुष्ट्या विनियोजयन्ति श्राद्धस्य दातारमदीनसत्त्वाः ॥
तृप्तास्तथैते विनियोजयन्ति दातुः पितॄन्सर्वगतान्महीप ॥14॥
1.138.m: And these [beings] of undaunted spirit endow the giver of the śrāddha with nourishment; / satisfied, they likewise direct the omnipresent ancestors of the giver [to him], O king.

1.139.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
vaivasvate'ntare prāpte prathame bhṛgunandana ..
śrāddhaṃ pradarśitaṃ kena tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 1 ..
1.139.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे प्राप्ते प्रथमे भृगुनन्दन ॥
श्राद्धं प्रदर्शितं केन तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.139.m: Vajra said: / When the first Vaivasvata period arrived, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / by whom was the śrāddha first revealed? Explain that to me as I ask.

1.139.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
hiraṇyākṣavadhe pūrvaṃ yadā tyaktvā dharādharāḥ ..
dharāṃ sapakṣā khagamāḥ khaṃ gatā manujeśvara .. 2 ..
1.139.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
हिरण्याक्षवधे पूर्वं यदा त्यक्त्वा धराधराः ॥
धरां सपक्षा खगमाः खं गता मनुजेश्वर ॥ 2 ॥
1.139.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, at the slaying of Hiraṇyākṣa, when the mountains, / possessing wings and moving in the sky, abandoned the earth and went into the firmament, O lord of men,

1.139.s:
dharādharaparityaktā tadā calitabandhanā ..
dharā sthānāccyutā vegātpraviveśa rasātalam .. 3 ..
1.139.d:
धराधरपरित्यक्ता तदा चलितबन्धना ॥
धरा स्थानाच्च्युता वेगात्प्रविवेश रसातलम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.139.m: the earth, abandoned by the mountains, with her fastenings shaken, / fallen from her place, swiftly entered the underworld.

1.139.s:
hiraṇyākṣaṃ tadā hatvā nṛvarāho janārdanaḥ .
prothena ca karābhyāṃ ca vidhārya vasudhāṃ balāt ..4 ..
1.139.d:
हिरण्याक्षं तदा हत्वा नृवराहो जनार्दनः ।
प्रोथेन च कराभ्यां च विधार्य वसुधां बलात् ॥4 ॥
1.139.m: Having then slain Hiraṇyākṣa, Janārdana as the Man-Boar, / violently tearing apart the earth with his snout and two hands,

1.139.s:
saṃpūjyamānastridaśaiḥ praviveśa rasātalam ..
rasātalatalaṃ gatvā śeṣamūrtau svake sthitaḥ .. 5 ..
1.139.d:
संपूज्यमानस्त्रिदशैः प्रविवेश रसातलम् ॥
रसातलतलं गत्वा शेषमूर्तौ स्वके स्थितः ॥ 5 ॥
1.139.m: entered the underworld while being worshipped by the thirty [gods]. / Having gone to the bottom of the underworld, he stood upon his own form, Śeṣa.

1.139.s:
daṃṣṭrāgreṇa samuddhṛtya mahīṃ dadhre tadā bhuje ..
vāmabāhuniviṣṭāṃtāṃ kṛtvā tridaśapuṅgavaḥ .. 6 ..
1.139.d:
दंष्ट्राग्रेण समुद्धृत्य महीं दध्रे तदा भुजे ॥
वामबाहुनिविष्टांतां कृत्वा त्रिदशपुङ्गवः ॥ 6 ॥
1.139.m: Lifting up the earth with the tip of his tusk, he then supported her upon his arm; / placing her on his left arm, the bull among the thirty [gods],

1.139.s:
ujjahāra mahātejā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā ..
ratnajvālāvalīpuñjadurvibhāvyamukhāmbujaḥ .. 7 ..
1.139.d:
उज्जहार महातेजा लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
रत्नज्वालावलीपुञ्जदुर्विभाव्यमुखाम्बुजः ॥ 7 ॥
1.139.m: possessing great splendour, desiring the welfare of the worlds, lifted her up, / his lotus-face difficult to discern amidst a mass of blazing jewel-flames.

1.139.s:
śeṣastuṣṭāva deveśaṃ tasminkāle jagadgurum..
puraṃdhriveśā vasudhā devaṃ tadbāhusaṃsthitā..8..
1.139.d:
शेषस्तुष्टाव देवेशं तस्मिन्काले जगद्गुरुम्॥
पुरंध्रिवेशा वसुधा देवं तद्बाहुसंस्थिता॥8॥
1.139.m: At that time, Śeṣa praised the lord of the gods, the guru of the universe; / the earth, in the attire of a married woman, resting on his arm,

1.139.s:
tadā tuṣṭāva bhūpāla ramaṇīyatamākṛtiḥ ..
uddhṛtya vasudhāṃ sthāne sthāpayitvā tathā svake..9..
1.139.d:
तदा तुष्टाव भूपाल रमणीयतमाकृतिः ॥
उद्धृत्य वसुधां स्थाने स्थापयित्वा तथा स्वके॥9॥
1.139.m: then praised the god, O protector of the earth, possessing a most lovely form. / Having raised the earth and placed her in her proper place,

1.139.s:
jagāma bhūmau dharmajña varāhaṃ nāma parvatam ..
kalpārambhe varāhasya paramūrteḥ saśailatām .. 1.139.10 ..
1.139.d:
जगाम भूमौ धर्मज्ञ वराहं नाम पर्वतम् ॥
कल्पारम्भे वराहस्य परमूर्तेः सशैलताम् ॥ 1.139.10 ॥
1.139.m: the knower of dharma went upon the earth to the mountain named Varāha; / at the beginning of the aeon, to the mountainous state of Varāha, his supreme form.

1.139.s:
tāṃ samāsādya dharmātmā devaḥ sarvagataḥ prabhuḥ ..
daṃṣṭāgralagnaṃ mṛtpiṇḍaṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe kare.. 11 ..
1.139.d:
तां समासाद्य धर्मात्मा देवः सर्वगतः प्रभुः ॥
दंष्टाग्रलग्नं मृत्पिण्डं गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे करे॥ 11 ॥
1.139.m: Having reached that, the righteous, all-pervading god, the lord, / took in his right hand a lump of clay clinging to the tip of his tusk.

1.139.s:
prasvedācca tilānkṛtvā darbhānromabhya eva ca ..
jalaprasravaṇābhyāśe tasmingirivare tadā .. 12 ..
1.139.d:
प्रस्वेदाच्च तिलान्कृत्वा दर्भान्रोमभ्य एव च ॥
जलप्रस्रवणाभ्याशे तस्मिन्गिरिवरे तदा ॥ 12 ॥
1.139.m: And having produced sesamum seeds from his sweat and darbha grass from his body-hairs, / near a stream of water on that best of mountains at that time,

1.139.s:
dakṣiṇāgrām̐stu vinyasya darbhāṃstānmadhusūdanaḥ ..
mṛtpiṇḍānsatilām̐steṣu dattavām̐strīnnarādhipa .. 13 ..
1.139.d:
दक्षिणाग्राम्̐स्तु विन्यस्य दर्भांस्तान्मधुसूदनः ॥
मृत्पिण्डान्सतिलाम्̐स्तेषु दत्तवाम्̐स्त्रीन्नराधिप ॥ 13 ॥
1.139.m: laying down those darbha grasses with their tips pointing south, Madhusūdana / offered three lumps of clay mixed with sesamum upon them, O lord of men.

1.139.s:
dattvā ca gandhapuṣpādyaiḥ pūjayāmāsa dhārmikaḥ ..
pūjayitvā ca maryādāṃ kṛtavānsa narādhipa .. 14 ..
1.139.d:
दत्त्वा च गन्धपुष्पाद्यैः पूजयामास धार्मिकः ॥
पूजयित्वा च मर्यादां कृतवान्स नराधिप ॥ 14 ॥
1.139.m: And having offered them, the righteous one worshipped them with perfumes, flowers, and the like; / and having worshipped them, he established the rule, O lord of men:

1.139.s:
adyaprabhṛti lokeṣu pretānuddiśya vai pitṝn ..
ye tu śrāddhaṃ kariṣyanti teṣāṃ puṣṭirbhaviṣyati .. 15 ..
1.139.d:
अद्यप्रभृति लोकेषु प्रेतानुद्दिश्य वै पितॄन् ॥
ये तु श्राद्धं करिष्यन्ति तेषां पुष्टिर्भविष्यति ॥ 15 ॥
1.139.m: "From this day forward, among the worlds, for those who perform a śrāddha / dedicated to the departed ancestors, there shall be nourishment.

1.139.s:
śrāddhakāle tathā tena piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ tathā ..
pitṝṇāṃ ye kariṣyanti teṣāṃ puṣṭirbhaviṣyati .. 16 ..
1.139.d:
श्राद्धकाले तथा तेन पिण्डनिर्वपणं तथा ॥
पितॄणां ये करिष्यन्ति तेषां पुष्टिर्भविष्यति ॥ 16 ॥
1.139.m: Likewise, for those who make an offering of piṇḍas / to the ancestors at the time of śrāddha, there shall be nourishment.

1.139.s:
pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ ..
pūjayā te bhaviṣyanti svayaṃ piṇḍeṣu nityadā .. 17 ..
1.139.d:
पिता पितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः ॥
पूजया ते भविष्यन्ति स्वयं पिण्डेषु नित्यदा ॥ 17 ॥
1.139.m: The father, the grandfather, and likewise the great-grandfather / shall always be present in person in the piṇḍas through this worship.

1.139.s:
teṣāṃ trayaḥ pūjitāśca bhaviṣyanti tathāgnayaḥ ..
trayo lokāstrayo devāstathaiva ca yugatrayam .. 18 ..
1.139.d:
तेषां त्रयः पूजिताश्च भविष्यन्ति तथाग्नयः ॥
त्रयो लोकास्त्रयो देवास्तथैव च युगत्रयम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.139.m: And the three fires shall be worshipped through them, / as shall the three worlds, the three gods, and likewise the three ages.

1.139.s:
pūjitāśca trayo devā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ ..
pūjitaistairbhaviṣyāmi caturātmā tathāpyaham.. 19..
1.139.d:
पूजिताश्च त्रयो देवा ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ॥
पूजितैस्तैर्भविष्यामि चतुरात्मा तथाप्यहम्॥ 19॥
1.139.m: And the three gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—shall be worshipped; / and when they are worshipped, I myself, possessing four forms, shall also be worshipped.

1.139.s:
pituḥ paitāmahaḥ piṇḍo vāsudevaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
paitāmahaśca nirdiṣṭastathā saṃkarṣaṇaḥ prabhuḥ .. 1.139.20 ..
1.139.d:
पितुः पैतामहः पिण्डो वासुदेवः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
पैतामहश्च निर्दिष्टस्तथा संकर्षणः प्रभुः ॥ 1.139.20 ॥
1.139.m: The great-grandfather's piṇḍa is declared to be Vāsudeva; / and the grandfather's [piṇḍa] is stated to be the lord Saṃkarṣaṇa;

1.139.s:
pitṛpiṇḍaśca vijñeyaḥ pradyumnaścāparājitaḥ ..
ātmā'niruddho vijñeyaḥ piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ budhaiḥ..21..
1.139.d:
पितृपिण्डश्च विज्ञेयः प्रद्युम्नश्चापराजितः ॥
आत्माऽनिरुद्धो विज्ञेयः पिण्डनिर्वपणं बुधैः॥21॥
1.139.m: and the father's piṇḍa is to be known as the unconquered Pradyumna; / the self is to be known as Aniruddha by the wise in the offering of piṇḍas.

1.139.s:
śrāddhaṃ kartuṃ kathaṃ śakyaṃ śakyaṃ vinā vaiṣṇavatejasā ..
evaṃ saṃpūjitastena caturātmā tvahaṃ sthitaḥ .. 22 ..
1.139.d:
श्राद्धं कर्तुं कथं शक्यं शक्यं विना वैष्णवतेजसा ॥
एवं संपूजितस्तेन चतुरात्मा त्वहं स्थितः ॥ 22 ॥
1.139.m: How can a śrāddha be performed without Vaiṣṇava splendour? / Thus worshipped by him, I, standing with four forms,

1.139.s:
bhaviṣyāmi pradāsyāmi tasya kāmānyathepsitān..
catvāraḥ pūjitā vedāścatvāraśca tathāgnayaḥ .. 23 ..
1.139.d:
भविष्यामि प्रदास्यामि तस्य कामान्यथेप्सितान्॥
चत्वारः पूजिता वेदाश्चत्वारश्च तथाग्नयः ॥ 23 ॥
1.139.m: shall exist and grant his desired wishes. / The four Vedas shall be worshipped, as well as the four fires;

1.139.s:
catvāraśca yugāstena catasraśca diśastathā ..
catvāraśca tathā varṇāścatvāraśca tathāśramāḥ.. 24 ..
1.139.d:
चत्वारश्च युगास्तेन चतस्रश्च दिशस्तथा ॥
चत्वारश्च तथा वर्णाश्चत्वारश्च तथाश्रमाः॥ 24 ॥
1.139.m: and through this the four ages, and the four directions, / as well as the four castes, and the four stages of life,

1.139.s:
catvāro lokapālāśca bhaviṣyantīha pūjitāḥ ..
evaṃ kṛtvā sa maryādāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata ..
tataḥ prabhṛti loke'smiñchrāddhaṃ sadbhiḥ prakīrtitam ..25 ..
1.139.d:
चत्वारो लोकपालाश्च भविष्यन्तीह पूजिताः ॥
एवं कृत्वा स मर्यादां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
ततः प्रभृति लोकेऽस्मिञ्छ्राद्धं सद्भिः प्रकीर्तितम् ॥25 ॥
1.139.m: and the four guardians of the world shall be worshipped here." / Having thus established the rule, he vanished right there; / from then on, the śrāddha has been proclaimed by the virtuous in this world.

1.139.s:
svargaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca yaśaḥ sukhāni rājyaṃ ca putrānatha bhūmipāla ..
striyaśca mukhyā vividhāṃśca kāmāndeveśvaraḥ śrāddhakṛto vidhatte .. 26 ..
pārvaṇa śrāddha vidhi
1.139.d:
स्वर्गं च मोक्षं च यशः सुखानि राज्यं च पुत्रानथ भूमिपाल ॥
स्त्रियश्च मुख्या विविधांश्च कामान्देवेश्वरः श्राद्धकृतो विधत्ते ॥ 26 ॥
पार्वण श्राद्ध विधि
1.139.m:
Heaven, liberation, renown, happiness, kingdom, and sons, O protector of the earth, / and excellent wives and various desires—the lord of the gods bestows all these on the performer of a śrāddha.
Rule for the Pārvaṇa Śrāddha
